a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t is the smallest possible unit of knowledge about an observation at time t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes, and repeatedly re-affirms as a 'candidate definition, not yet formally proven', K_t(o) = the smallest epistemically meaningful unit of knowledge about observation o at time t, explicitly warning against prematurely identifying K_t with a data point, a claim, or the existing six-tuple (entity/property/context/relation/time/authority) -- those may become representations of K_t, not K_t itself, restated as the invariant 'Representation != Knowledge Identity'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can K_t be decomposed into smaller knowledge units without losing the knowledge about the observation? If yes, it wasn't minimal. If no, we have a candidate minimal knowledge unit.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an operational minimality criterion for K_t via a decomposition test (K_t -> {K_t,1, K_t,2, ...}): if the decomposition preserves all knowledge about the observation, the original unit was not minimal; if no such decomposition exists, it is a candidate minimal unit -- offered as a way to formalize 'smallest' without prematurely fixing K_t's internal structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A sentence is a linguistic representation that may contain one or more K_t units. ... the number of sentences gives us a possible dimensional view, but not necessarily the true number of dimensions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Using a repeated Nexus-server worked example (RHEL 9.8, 8 vCPU, port 8081, etc. as ten atomic statements), argues a sentence is not necessarily one K_t unit -- e.g. 'has 8 vCPUs and 31 GB RAM' contains two atomic units -- and that an observation's true dimensionality is not bounded by however many sentences currently describe it (K_t(O) subset-of all potentially observable aspects of O; 'Knowledge at t != the complete observation'); new sentences discovered later add new dimensions (K_t^11), and a corrected statement changes an existing dimension's value rather than necessarily creating a new one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WorldState_t -> Observation_t^A -> InformationState_t^A -> EpistemicState_t^A -> KnowledgeAttribution, with history H_{<=t} preserved. It then proposes K_t^{A,R} as a time-indexed knowledge attribution, dependent on participant A, extraction regime R.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reading an unread-in-this-batch corpus document, reports its chain WorldState_t -> Observation_t^A -> InformationState_t^A -> EpistemicState_t^A -> KnowledgeAttribution (with preserved history H_{<=t}) and its participant/regime-relative K_t^{A,R}; explicitly distinguishes this from the dialogue's own new atomic-K_t hypothesis, treating the latter as a possible FURTHER refinement (one measurable statement per observation dimension) rather than something the attached document already established, and notes the document's own probability treatment P(K_t^A|F_t^A) as extraction-uncertainty, explicitly distinct from Knowledge itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q = domain of possible items; K subset-of Q = a particular knowledge state; script-K = space/family of possible states; probability (Q, script-K, p). The crucial distinction is: script-K != K_t != P(K_t | O_{<=t}).
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a Knowledge Space Theory (KST) formalism (Q as domain of possible items, K as a particular state, script-K as the family of possible states, with probability attached as (Q,script-K,p)) as external confirmation that a knowledge-space, a particular state, and a probability distribution over states are three genuinely different objects; notes KST's own K_t is a learner-capability state (a different, narrower sense than the dialogue's broader KnowledgeOS K_t), and that the dialogue's atomic-unit idea asks a question KST does not answer: what is the state/value of each individual knowledge unit within a state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(k_i | E) is the epistemic confidence/degree of support for proposition k_i, given the available evidence. ... k_i != P(k_i)
a_rows_sample.statement: Repeatedly insists that probability attached to a knowledge unit must be given a precise referent -- distinguishing P(claim is true), P(claim is supported by available evidence), P(the measurement/extraction is correct), and P(claim belongs to K_t) as not necessarily the same quantity, and stating k_i != P(k_i): the knowledge unit itself is not identical to its probability. Also proposes that not every claim's epistemic measure need be a probability -- it could be categorical status, an interval, a confidence level, measurement uncertainty, or logical entailment strength -- warning against forcing every kind of knowledge into probability merely because probability is mathematically convenient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EpistemicState = Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a multidimensional EpistemicState formulation (Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity) as already-derived corpus material supporting the general direction of a non-monolithic, multi-axis knowledge state, alongside a stated distinction chain Knowledge!=Reality, Observation!=Knowledge, Dimension!=Statement, Dimension!=Value, Guidance!=Decision, Zero!=Knowledge, Parsing!=Knowledge, Parsing!=Dimension-Discovery.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is the minimum structure of k_t such that the entire KnowledgeOS theory — evidence, probability, context, identity, Zero, evolution, proposal, decision and action — can be derived without adding arbitrary architectural assumptions?
a_rows_sample.statement: Closes the file's line of inquiry with an explicit unresolved research question: what is the minimal structure of the atomic knowledge unit k_t from which the rest of the theory (evidence, probability, context, identity, Zero, evolution, proposal, decision, action) could be derived without arbitrary additional architectural assumptions -- stated as the next major research question rather than answered.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A sentence is not automatically a knowledge dimension merely because it is syntactically a sentence. ... independent knowledge-bearing statement -> candidate dimension
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the minimal-knowledge-unit hypothesis k_t(O) (smallest independently meaningful unit of knowledge about an observation at t) with the qualification that sentence != dimension automatically -- semantic independence of a statement must be established before it counts as a candidate dimension; and states K_t(O) is necessarily partial, since K_t(O) subset-of D(O), the full (possibly unbounded) dimension set of the observation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: k_i = (O, d_i, v_i, t, E_i, p_i, q_i)
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the atomic knowledge claim to a seven-field tuple k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,p_i,q_i) -- observation, semantic dimension, claimed value, time, evidence/information source, epistemic probability, and an explicit information-sufficiency/support status q_i -- with K_t(O)={k_1,...,k_n} as the resulting knowledge state, and reiterates that dimensionality is representation-relative rather than an intrinsic finite property of the object (a sentence maps to one or more atomic claims, not one-to-one).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t should not be identified with a Kripke model or possible-world set. Status: research conclusion / compatibility constraint, not yet kernel theorem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the DEL document's rejection of K_t as a Kripke pointed model (M,w) strengthens (without proving) the corpus's independently-developed atomic-tuple direction k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,C_i,p_i,q_i); explicitly records the possible-worlds rejection as a research conclusion/compatibility constraint, not a kernel theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The missing step is: $$(O,E_{\le t},A,G,EC)\;\longrightarrow\;K_t(O)$$ ... The file itself almost explicitly states this as the unanswered operation \(\mathcal M\): $$\mathcal M:(O,E_{\le t},A,G,EC)\rightarrow K_t(O)$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the central missing derivation in the reviewed K_t/observation research as the unanswered operation M:(O, E_{<=t}, A, G, EC) -> K_t(O) -- the document being reviewed 'repeatedly approaches it but never actually derives it' -- where O is observation, E_{<=t} is evidence up to time t, A is the Knower/agent, G is goal, and EC is the epistemic contract.

a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects/sharpens the atomic-knowledge-unit hypothesis by pointing out that reviewed prior work jumps directly from an observation O to a set of atoms k_1..k_n without deriving them, despite itself distinguishing dimension != statement != knowledge atom != value; the transformation producing the atoms from an observation is never actually supplied.

a_rows_sample.statement: Names a second missing derivation: the aggregation of individual knowledge atoms {k_i,t} into the knowledge state K_t, with the mathematical type of the aggregate (set/vector/graph/distribution/state-space/other) left explicitly open.

a_rows_sample.statement: A three-part strategic-DDD test (language, ownership, change-reason) is applied to every declared bounded context, explicitly allowing a context with zero executable realization to still pass (rules-only contexts are real), while a context failing the language test cannot be rescued by code.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BC-1..BC-6 verdict table: CONFIRM boundary UNRESOLVED (BC-1) · CONFIRM but overloaded (BC-2) · CONFIRM (BC-3) · CONFIRM capability/CHALLENGE context (BC-4) · CHALLENGE as declared Core (BC-5) · CONFIRM cleanest boundary (BC-6)
a_rows_sample.statement: Each of the six declared bounded contexts receives a distinct strategic verdict from the three-part test: BC-1 confirmed but with a possibly-two-systems internal boundary unresolved; BC-2 confirmed but overloaded (hosts a second, foreign orchestration language); BC-3 confirmed cleanly; BC-4's capability is real but its context status is challenged (no state, no component, realized only by role model and human acts); BC-5's declared-Core status is challenged as not matching the measured center of gravity; BC-6 is the cleanest confirmed boundary in the system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PROMOTE TO CANDIDATE BC-7 ... the strongest candidate on the record
a_rows_sample.statement: An undeclared area realized entirely by workflow-record mechanisms (work item, session, role, transition, grant, handoff, human act) is promoted from the baseline's low-confidence Inferred status to the strongest candidate bounded context, named 'Governed Session Orchestration' (candidate BC-7), pending an ADR since it would reverse a recorded Increment-1 parsimony decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M-1..M-5 Misplaced responsibilities ... M-3 Composition root (CMP-001) | registry only — no declared context at all
a_rows_sample.statement: Five misplaced-responsibility findings are recorded, including the workflow-record mechanism sitting in the wrong declared context (M-1), the platform registry sitting under Design & Decision Support rather than its own governance context (M-2), and the composition root having no declared context home at all (M-3).

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-1..C-6 Coupling problems ... Authority state has no provenance — all workflow records gitignored, zero history
a_rows_sample.statement: Six coupling problems are recorded, most materially that the candidate orchestration context's own authority store has no provenance (gitignored, zero history, C-3) despite the context's purpose being auditable authority, and that the registry-first contract is declared binding but measured bypassable by three unregistered hooks (C-6).

a_rows_sample.statement: Governance requires distinguishing three rejection kinds (structure, policy, authority) rather than a single failure value, since malformed input and disallowed action are different governance facts; all three are executed and observed to fire in this artifact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: assert WellFormed(P); policy satisfied ... relate endpoints ∈ 𝒜; acyclicity for DAG families ... retract a ∈ 𝒜 ... 𝒜 ∖ {a}, ℛ cascade ... merge both structurally valid ... noop —
a_rows_sample.statement: Per-operation specification table for assert, relate, retract, merge, noop covering precondition, state effect, evidence/provenance effect, authority requirement, policy requirement, assessment effect, failure modes, determinism and idempotence — e.g. retract cascades through R and drops evidence carried with the retracted assertion; relate requires authority only for supersedes-type edges and acyclicity for DAG relation families.

a_rows_sample.statement: assert and relate are idempotent as a direct consequence of A and R being sets (not sequences/multisets) — re-executing a history is safe; executed confirmation that F(H1)=F(H3) where H3 re-asserts an already-present A1.

OUTPUT K' = ( same 𝒜 , { (8663022439, e2c73b5500, supersedes) } ) Outcome = ok ... |𝒜'| = 4 (unchanged — A1 RETAINED, not deleted: 218.21 honoured) ... contradicts(K', A1, A2) = False ← the supersession EXPLAINS the diff
a_rows_sample.statement: One fully instantiated transformation with every value concrete: a relate(...,supersedes) operation under policy 'evidence-required' and authority 'architect' against a four-assertion K, with explicit guard evaluation (endpoint membership, DAG-family acyclicity check, authority check) all passing, producing Outcome=ok, an unchanged assertion count (A1 is RETAINED not deleted, honouring step 218.21's supersession-not-deletion principle), and differential contradiction results — the supersession relation explains away contradicts(A1,A2) but a still-unexplained contradiction persists for contradicts(A1,A4).

a_rows_sample.statement: Three executed rejections against the same state demonstrate all three Outcome kinds: an under-privileged actor triggers REJECTED(authority); a reversed relate direction triggering a supersedes cycle triggers REJECTED(structure); an out-of-value-space version assertion triggers REJECTED(structure).

a_rows_sample.statement: The out-of-range-value rejection is possible only because the Proposition P=(E,D,V) formalization was closed (CB-2): before that, 'ill-formed' had no formal meaning, so the transformation guard could not detect it — a concrete downstream engineering payoff of resolving the proposition-type question.

a_rows_sample.anchor: deterministic YES ... closed YES ... total NO — deliberately partial ... composable YES, associatively ... identity element YES — noop ... idempotent (assert, relate, merge) YES ... monotone NO ... invertible NO ... congruent w.r.t. history YES, structurally
a_rows_sample.statement: Algebraic property table for T: deterministic (executed), closed (T(K,.) in K by construction), deliberately NOT total (three rejection kinds executed), composable associatively (Replay=fold(T,empty,H)), has an identity element (noop), idempotent for assert/relate/merge (set semantics, executed), NOT monotone (retract shrinks A), NOT invertible (retract's cascade is lossy), and congruent with respect to history (structurally, because T's domain contains no History — per artifact F).

a_rows_sample.anchor: transformation 𝕂 × Op × Policy × Authority ⇀ 𝕂 × Outcome CHANGES K, appends History ... assessment P × Evidence × Context × Policy → Σ K UNCHANGED, no History ... decision Determination × Authority → commitment K UNCHANGED, appends History ... governance action Policy × Transformation → Admissible K
a_rows_sample.statement: Four-way canonical distinction by signature and effect: transformation (changes K, appends History), assessment (leaves K unchanged, produces no History entry), decision (leaves K unchanged, appends History), governance action (leaves K unchanged, appends History) — clarifying which corpus 'operations' are actually state transitions versus which merely produce judgments or authorizations while History alone records them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assess was run four times against the same K and returned four different values without altering |𝒜| or |ℛ|. A function that returns different answers while the state is fixed cannot be a state transition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed proof that assessment is not a transformation: running Assess four times against the same fixed K returns four different values while leaving |A| and |R| unchanged — a function producing different outputs while its stated 'state' is fixed cannot itself be a state transition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assess(A2, policy="default") = (Supporting, Weak) ... Assess(A2, policy="strict-provenance") = (Neutral, None) SAME EVIDENCE, DIFFERENT Σ ... Therefore Σ is not a function of (P, e). This refutes any model that derives status from the assertion alone — and it is the formal reason Assessment needs fo
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed proof that Policy is a genuine argument of Assessment, not incidental: assessing the same assertion A2 with the same evidence under two different policies ('default' vs 'strict-provenance') yields different epistemic-status outputs (Supporting/Weak vs Neutral/None); therefore Sigma is NOT a function of (Proposition,evidence) alone, refuting any model deriving epistemic status from the assertion in isolation, and giving the formal reason Assessment must take four arguments (P, Evidence, Context, Policy).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can a complete Knowledge State be constructed from primitive inputs, transformed, compared, validated/assessed, and checked against invariants? YES. Executed.
a_rows_sample.statement: The decisive question of the whole verification mandate — can a complete Knowledge State be built, transformed, compared, assessed and invariant-checked purely from primitive inputs? — is answered YES, and is executed as real program output rather than prose or 'conceptually works' claims.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1 CONTEXT ... 2 OBSERVATION ... EVIDENCE ... 3 DIMENSION ... PROPOSITION ... 4 ASSERTION ... 5 IDENTITY ... 6 T: assert A1 -> ok |𝒜|=1 ... 7 T: relate(intern) -> REJECTED(authority) ... 8 T: cycle attempt -> REJECTED(structure) ... 9 INVARIANTS ... 10 ASSESSMENT ... FINAL STATE |𝒜|=4 |ℛ|=1 Semantica
a_rows_sample.statement: A single continuous ten-step executed run builds Context, Observation/Evidence (held by reference per ADR-T16), Dimension/Proposition (with WellFormed check), four concrete Assertions, an identity check (A1 != A3 despite the same proposition, differing only in context), four successful assert transformations, an authority-gated relate (one rejected, one accepted), two structural rejections (a supersedes cycle attempt and an ill-formed value), a full invariant check (StructuralValid, SemanticallyValid, acyclicity, three differently-explained contradiction checks), and five Assessment calls — ending in a final state of |A|=4, |R|=1, SemanticallyValid=True.

a_rows_sample.statement: Line 7 executes proof that Authority is a genuine, load-bearing parameter of T: the identical (K, operation, policy) triple produces REJECTED(authority) under an 'intern' actor and ok under an 'architect' actor.

a_rows_sample.statement: Line 8 fires two distinct REJECTED(structure) cases (a supersedes-cycle attempt and an ill-formed value assertion), and the cycle rejection is noted to enforce an acyclicity invariant that the real running EKP does NOT itself enforce — a concrete gap between the theory's guard and the deployed platform's actual validation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 10 | Σ is total on the conflicted region — ('Contested','Weak'), the gap that refuted the three-state model. And Σ is not a function of (P,e): same evidence, different policy, different status
a_rows_sample.statement: Line 10 executes the Assess calls showing Sigma is total even on a previously problematic conflicted-evidence region (returning ('Contested','Weak'), closing a gap that had refuted an earlier three-state epistemic-status model), and re-executes the earlier finding that Sigma is not a function of (Proposition,evidence) alone since the same evidence under different policy yields a different status.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This executes the THEORY, not KnowledgeOS. There is no KnowledgeOS implementation to run this against ... This is mathematical and computational verification, and it is explicitly NOT empirical validation of a running system. The one thing executed against real running software is in artifact G.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit scope limitation: the ten-step run executes the THEORY's own reference model, not an actual KnowledgeOS implementation (no bounded context, no domain layer exists to run against) — this is mathematical/computational verification, explicitly not empirical validation of a running system; the only artifact executed against real running software is a separate artifact G.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Theory (artifact C, prior phase, proven): supersedes is transitive; a cycle makes "which assertion is current?" undefined; therefore acyclicity is an invariant, not an optional check. EKP: circular_dependency is a warning, and its comment scopes it to requires/depends_on only. Supersession cycles ar
a_rows_sample.statement: The one genuine, actionable non-conformance finding: the theory proves (artifact C) that supersedes must be acyclic because a cycle makes 'which assertion is current' undefined, but the EKP's circular_dependency check is only a warning and is scoped only to requires/depends_on, leaving supersession cycles entirely unchecked; executed against the live graph, current supersedes edges among the 37 governed docs = 0, so the gap is currently vacuous but unguarded — the first supersession chain that closes would pass the linter. A concrete verifier recommendation follows: extend circular_dependency to supersedes/derived_from/refines and raise its severity to error for those families — explicitly noted as the first time in the whole verification programme that the mathematics told the implementation something it did not already know.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-2 | What is a Policy, formally? | Policy as a mathematical object: how it maps an evidence set to a support level | Assessment is well-typed but uncomputable without it; G-1 depends on it ... knowledge-schema.yaml IS an executing policy — a model exists ... BLOCKING
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-2 (BLOCKING, and the root blocker): Policy has no formal mathematical definition (how it maps an evidence set to a support level), leaving Assessment well-typed but uncomputable, and G-1 depends on it; the running EKP's knowledge-schema.yaml is noted to already BE an executing policy, giving an existing model to generalise from; resolution route is generalising from the EKP's schema-as-policy, tested by running assessment under at least two policies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-7 | retract breaks F∘T̂ = T∘F | either exclude retract or add tombstones | step 254's own adequacy criterion fails on one operation ... adopt append-only (matches ReplayAssertion's immutability invariant) ... OPEN — recommend append-only
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-7 (not blocking): the retract operation is found to break step 254's own commuting-square adequacy criterion F-compose-That = T-compose-F, evidenced by both a corpus citation (step 254) and an independently executed cascade-lossiness demonstration; the recommended resolution is to adopt an append-only model with tombstones (matching a separate ReplayAssertion immutability invariant) rather than excluding retract outright, tested by a commuting-square test specifically on retract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Proposition | A meaningful statement that can be true or false. | P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) ... Assertion | A proposition put forward as true, with a specific epistemic status... Knowledge | An assertion that satisfies the epistemic criteria for knowledge (justified true belief)
b_rows_sample.statement: Splits the Knowledge Atom into a three-level hierarchy Proposition subset-of Assertion subset-of Knowledge: Proposition=(E,D,V) is content without commitment; Assertion=(P,Sigma,Evidence,tau,Provenance) is a proposition put forward as true; Knowledge=(A,Justification,True) is a justified-true assertion; corrects the earlier Knowledge Atom to actually be an Assertion, not raw Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Who determines True? KnowledgeOS observes, reconstructs, compares, challenges and guides. It generally cannot access Truth itself... Truth \neq Truth Assessment
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects making absolute Truth an internal primitive of Knowledge, since KnowledgeOS cannot access Truth directly; replaces the three-level model with four levels (Proposition -> Assertion -> Epistemically Accepted -> Reality/Omega), where 'Knowledge' becomes K=(A,Justification,TruthAssessment) rather than requiring literal correspondence to reality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Candidate Proposition(s) ... because an observation can be ambiguous. ... 'Host responds on port 8081' -> P1/P2/P3
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects 'Observe -> Proposition' to 'Observation -> Candidate Proposition(s)', since one observation (e.g. a host responding on a port) can support multiple distinct, non-exclusive candidate propositions requiring Zero/Lord/Semantic-Reconstruction to disambiguate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Knowledge from a single giant tuple to a Knowledge State K_t = E_t(A_t), an epistemic evaluation function over the set of currently available assertions A_t, foreshadowing K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,Observation_t,Zero_t,Lord_t,Evidence_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_t \rightarrow O_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow A_t \rightarrow K_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the too-simple Reality->Observation->Knowledge pipeline into X_t (domain/reality) -> O_t (observation) -> R_t (semantic reconstruction/interpretation) -> A_t (assertion) -> K_t (knowledge state), with the critical point Observation ≠ Interpretation ≠ Assertion ≠ Knowledge, illustrated with the Bhīṣma example (seeing him = observation; 'Bhīṣma is a person' = interpretation; 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' = assertion; the same claim with provenance and epistemic qualification = knowledge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: P = \text{a semantically evaluable claim about entities, relationships, states or events}
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Proposition as a semantically evaluable claim (examples: IsOnBattlefield(Bhishma), GrandfatherOf(Bhishma,Arjuna), OpponentOf(Bhishma,Arjuna)), distinguished from Assertion: Proposition ≠ Assertion, and Assertion = Proposition + Epistemic Qualification + Provenance. Flagged as a distinction that 'should be frozen'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_3 = Inference( A_1,A_2,\ldots, Rule, Assumptions, Provenance )
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Infer(A_1,A_2,Rule)->A_3 to require every derived assertion to carry Rule, Assumptions, and Provenance so KnowledgeOS can explain 'why do you believe this?': every derived assertion traceable to source assertions + inference rule + assumptions + context, called essential for deterministic assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Document \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the naive Documents->Chunk->Embedding->VectorDB->RAG->LLM architecture as 'not KnowledgeOS' because it bypasses the epistemic model: a document is not knowledge but an information-bearing source from which observations/assertions may be constructed — Document ≠ Knowledge, Document ≠ Evidence — illustrated by Document->Observation->Candidate Assertion->Evidence->Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LLM\ Output \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Names three constitutional invariants for sources: (1) Source ≠ Knowledge (Document/API Response/Git Repository ≠ Knowledge); (2) LLM Output ≠ Knowledge — LLM Output -> Candidate Interpretation -> Epistemic Processing -> Knowledge; (3) Retrieval ≠ Knowledge Creation — Retrieve(Q) -> EvidenceCandidates -> Evaluate -> Knowledge. Overarching principle: 'Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Interpret: Observation \times Context \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Interpret:Observation×Context->CandidateMeaning is where the structural parser, semantic parser, domain model, and LLM participate, worked through 'those with whom I have to fight' -> structural parsing -> semantic parsing -> candidate semantic structure -> candidate dimensions {Actor,Target,Action,Relationship,Obligation,Context} — explicitly 'not yet accepted knowledge'. CandidateAssertion=(Proposition,Sources,Interpretation,Context), e.g. 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' becomes a candidate proposition via Interpret->CandidateAssertions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assess: CandidateAssertion \times Evidence \times Rules \times Context \rightarrow EpistemicAssessment
b_rows_sample.statement: Assess:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->EpistemicAssessment produces Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) per explicit policy, contrasting e.g. (Acquisition=Reported,Support=Moderate,Uncertainty=Moderate,Validity=Current) against (Acquisition=AI-Generated,Support=None,Uncertainty=High,Validity=Unknown) depending on what actually supports the proposition. CandidateAssertion --Assessment--> Assertion=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID); K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,A). Full acquisition chain: X->Artifact->Observation->Interpretation->CandidateAssertion->Assessment->Assertion->K_{t+1}, stated to be 'already a computable architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal P = \mathcal P_F \cup \mathcal P_N \cup \mathcal P_Q \cup \mathcal P_H \cup \mathcal P_I \ldots
b_rows_sample.statement: After ten tests, provisionally establishes 'Source Observation is computationally realizable' across documents, DB results, internet resources, human statements, LLM outputs, code, rules, ADRs, constitutions and instructions, preserving Source event ≠ Meaning ≠ Assertion. Surfaces two explicit unresolved theoretical points without deciding them: Open Point A — whether one Proposition abstraction P_F∪P_N∪P_Q∪P_H∪P_I∪... (factual/normative/definitional/instructional/question/hypothesis/interpretation) with an explicit semantic type suffices, versus needing genuinely distinct object types; Open Point B — whether the Observation model should stay unified (with acquisition method/type recording measurement vs statement vs database vs LLM etc.) rather than creating separate Observation concepts per source class.

b_rows_sample.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses two explicit architectural-fork questions to the domain authority rather than deciding unilaterally: Question 1 — should factual/normative/definitional/instructional/hypothetical/interrogative content be different TYPES of semantic proposition under one common Proposition abstraction (recommended: Yes — one Proposition abstraction with explicit semantic type, rather than unrelated objects)? Question 2 — should the observation model stay unified, with acquisition method/type recording whether it came from measurement/database/document/human/LLM/API/parser (recommended: Yes)? If both are agreed, proposes formally closing Observation and moving to 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation', testing whether parsing+ontology+rules+LLM+human interpretation can transform arbitrary source observations into candidate semantic structures 'without pretending that interpretation is truth'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS be allowed to create an Assertion with an explicitly unresolved epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses and then answers the pivotal admission-boundary design choice: should an Assertion require passing a minimum admission threshold, or may it hold an explicitly unresolved epistemic state (Unknown/Hypothesized/WeaklySupported)? Recommends and then (in a 'Domain Authority' voice) DECIDES the latter: Assertion ≠ Proven Truth. Rationale given for rejecting the threshold alternative: it would remove Zero's ability to detect gaps (no representation for Unknown/Hypothesized), remove Lord's ability to generate candidates (no place for them to reside), sever the Observation->Interpretation->Candidate->Assertion provenance chain, damage auditability (no record of 'what we considered but did not accept'), make the incomplete-question problem unsolvable, collapse the Unknown-vs-Absent distinction, and break the learning trajectory Hypothesized->WeaklySupported->StronglySupported.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = "This is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity."
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-runs all eight test cases (DB result -> StronglySupported; unstructured document -> WeaklySupported; internet page -> WeaklySupported with caveats; human statement -> Reported; LLM output -> Hypothesized; incomplete question -> no assertion created, Zero detects gap, clarification requested; conflicting sources -> both assertions remain in the Knowledge State with a detected Conflict; unknown value -> Assertion(Unknown)) through the new admission model. States the redefined meaning of 'the single source of truth': Truth = 'this is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity', NOT 'this is factually correct in reality' — the formalization of Knowledge ≠ Reality. Six constitutional invariants listed: Assertion≠Proven Truth; admission does not require verification; Unknown is a valid epistemic state (not absence of an assertion); epistemic status can evolve; multiple epistemic states can coexist (Conflicting is valid); provenance is preserved. Declares the Epistemic Admission Boundary computationally closed and proceeds to 'Computational Closure 3 — The Knowledge State'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A \not\equiv Truth(P)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Assertion A=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID) with A≢Truth(P): A is 'KnowledgeOS's governed representation of P'. Two assertions of the identical proposition 'Nexus.version=3.69' can carry different epistemic states (Σ_A=(Observed,Strong,Low,Current) vs Σ_B=(Reported,Weak,High,Unknown)) and are 'not epistemically equivalent', giving Assertion⇏StrongEvidence, Assertion⇏Certainty, Assertion⇏Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Admit(P,\Pi_1) \neq Admit(P,\Pi_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces admission policy Π_adm with Admit(P_c,E,C,Π_adm)->{Assertion|Reject|Defer|RequestMoreEvidence}; admission is purpose-dependent, Admit(P,Π_1)≠Admit(P,Π_2) (an exploration policy may allow Weak support, a production-migration policy may require Strong support) — connecting directly to the Ideal State theory: an assertion can exist with Σ_K=Weak while the Ideal State requires Σ_I=Strong, producing a discrepancy rather than an invalid assertion. Distinguishes Admission ('may this proposition exist as governed knowledge?', Candidate->Assertion) from Validation ('does this assertion satisfy a particular requirement?', Assertion×Constraint->ValidationResult): Admission ≠ Validation — an assertion can be admitted (e.g. during discovery) yet later FAIL a validation (e.g. a migration requiring verified version) WITHOUT being deleted; it 'remains useful historical knowledge'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion \in KnowledgeState ... KnowledgeState \neq SetOfAssertions
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier equation Assertion=Knowledge (too strong) to Assertion∈KnowledgeState while KnowledgeState≠SetOfAssertions: the Knowledge State is a structured object K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Relationships,Conflicts,Gaps,Provenance,Context,History,Constraints), 'a structured state, not simply a bag of claims' — called 'an important DDD correction'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Evidence is not a property of a document.}
b_rows_sample.statement: Central correction: Evidence is not a property of a document but 'a relationship between an observation and a proposition under a context and an evaluation rule' — Evidence(O,P,C,R). Prevents the mistake 'the document says X, therefore X is evidence [for whatever P]'. Gives Evidence≠Observation, Evidence≠Source, Evidence≠Support, Evidence≠Truth as four fundamental distinctions, and shows the SAME observation can be evidence for one proposition and not another (Evidence(O,P_1)≠Evidence(O,P_2)) — 'evidence is therefore relational'. E=(O,P,R,C,T,Q,Π): observation, target proposition, evaluation rule, context, temporal applicability, quality assessment, provenance.

type_signature.domain: observation x proposition x context x rule

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conclusion = Inference(Premises,Rule,Context)
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'the evidence voted for 3.69' informal aggregation, requiring Conclusion=Inference(Premises,Rule,Context) via an explicit inference rule (worked example: APIResponse.version=3.69 plus rule 'APIResponse(source=NexusProduction)=>CurrentVersion(NexusProduction)' yields the conclusion). Distinguishes four conclusion kinds: Deductive (Γ⊨P, entailed), Inductive (evidence increases support for a generalization without entailing it), Abductive (select the best explanation among hypotheses {H_1,...,H_n} — 'extremely relevant to KnowledgeOS'), Computational/derived (e.g. a version-vs-required-version comparison rule). Formalizes Conclusion object C_n=(P,Γ,R,κ,Σ,Π,t) (proposition, premises/evidence, inference rule, inference method, epistemic assessment, provenance, derivation time), letting KnowledgeOS answer 'why did you reach this conclusion?' not just 'what did you conclude?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Communication is two capabilities wearing one name. C-10 Knowledge Distribution -- a genuine, evidenced, unowned MECHANISM ... C-19 Communication Composition -- a STEWARDSHIP
a_rows_sample.statement: 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: fails on 6 of 10 => a STEWARDSHIP / cross-cutting expression concern ... the only state that could make a Communication context real -- delivery-with-acknowledgement -- is C-10's receipt, not C-19's. building C-10 would REDUCE the case for a Communication context.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD does not define a bounded context by noun category or organizational role ... Communication becomes a bounded context when it has its own domain language ... a reason to evolve separately.
a_rows_sample.statement: Challenges creating a Communication bounded context merely because a Communication Engineer role exists; a Communication context is defensible only if messages/audiences/consent/delivery/retention carry independent domain invariants and lifecycle, not merely presentation/rendering.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four unowned capabilities (corrected state)
a_rows_sample.statement: Records four capabilities with no bounded-context owner as one control loop (policy/knowledge DEFINED in BC-1 -> C-10 DELIVERS -> C-14 GATES -> C-19 EXPRESSES <- C-5 ATTESTS): C-5 Separation attestation (existence YES, cross-context control-plane assurance capability, NOT a bounded context); C-10 Knowledge distribution (existence NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred); C-14 Policy enforcement (existence CONTESTED, deferred); C-19 Communication composition (existence YES, stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern, NOT a bounded context). Flagged as a proposal finding, not adopted architecture; C-10/C-14 existence remain UNDECIDED.

a_rows_sample.statement: Re-runs the D285-5 action/result witness against all four corpus-named equality relations rather than the three previously tested, finding it vacuous under structural equality (as before), conditionally substantive under semantic equality only if a specific, currently-undecided discard-of-provenance choice is made, undefined-as-stated under observational equality pending a fixed observation set, and newly found VACUOUS under provenance-sensitive equality -- meaning two of the four relations make the property vacuous, one is conditional on an open decision, and one is undefined without further specification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Corpus (246) defines FOUR relations: structural, semantic, observational, provenance-sensitive. 'history' equality is NOT among them. The chain 'history ⊊ structural ⊊ semantic' appears ONLY in verification-lane artifacts... => the HIERARCHY is a verification-lane construct (DERIVED), not CORPUS. ... structural ⊊ semantic WITNESSED. D ⊆ semantic BY DEFINITION. observational is NOT comparable without fixing the permitted-observation set.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the previously-assumed three-level 'history subset structural subset semantic' equality hierarchy (used without verification in S2078's RQ mandate) by showing it is not actually a corpus-defined relation at all, only a verification-lane construct; the corpus's own four relations instead give a witnessed strict structural-subset-semantic inclusion, a by-definition provenance-subset-semantic inclusion, and an observational relation that is simply not comparable to the others without first fixing a specific observation set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CORPUS — Step 246 defines, at state level: A K1=K2 structural (byte/structurally identical); B K1≡K2 semantic (encode the same knowledge semantics); C K1≈K2 observational (every permitted observation produces the same result); D K1≅_λK2 provenance-sensitive (content and relevant provenance equivalent) — 'These are not interchangeable.' CORPUS — Step 264.15 additionally defines semantic equality at value level: v1≡_D v2, with 3m ≢_str 300cm but 3m≡_D 300cm.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the exact corpus citations (Step 246 for the four state-level equality relations, Step 264.15 for a parallel value-level semantic equivalence with a worked unit-conversion example distinguishing structural from semantic equality at the value level) grounding the corrected equality analysis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: structural=>semantic? True (witness holds). semantic=>structural? False => the inclusion is STRICT. provenance=>semantic? True (D is defined AS semantic+Pi). => structural⊊semantic WITNESSED. D⊆semantic BY DEFINITION. => observational is NOT comparable without fixing the permitted-observation set. The corpus hierarchy is a partial order over four relations, not the three-element chain previously cited.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes the three testable inclusion implications among the corpus's four equality relations, finding structural is strictly contained in semantic (witnessed) and provenance-sensitive is contained in semantic (by definition), while observational equality cannot even be compared to the others without first fixing a specific permitted-observation set -- concluding the equality space forms a PARTIAL ORDER over four relations, correcting the earlier assumption of a single strict three-element total-order chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **The investigation has converged on two genuinely irreducible formal gaps:** 1. `Qualify` has no executable/formal body — `G1` ... 2. Three corpus equality relations lack decision procedures — also `G1`
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies two genuinely irreducible formal gaps (both graded G1): (1) Qualify has no executable/formal body, remaining the blocker for making πK computable — Sanjaya recovers the missing referent/observation layer (W,Ω,O) but does not solve Qualify; (2) three corpus equality relations (≡ semantic, ≈ observational, ≅_λ provenance-sensitive) lack decision procedures — equality is not missing as a concept but is under-specified as an executable formalism, and the research should not invent another equality relation to make D285-5 work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **The next logical research target is therefore not another Sanskrit hypothesis. It is the formalization of the corpus equality relations and `Qualify`, with the two kept strictly separate.**
a_rows_sample.statement: States the overall verdict and next research target: the three gap-update artifacts show real progress (moving from 'are we missing concepts?' to 'which recovered concepts are formally specified enough to support executable claims?'); the next target is not another Sanskrit hypothesis but formalizing the corpus equality relations and Qualify, kept strictly separate — this is where the investigation can either make πK computable or rigorously demonstrate why it cannot.

a_rows_sample.statement: Freezes a 15-row status table as the current evidence state: W/Omega referent layer recovered/promoted; Observation closed as discovery gap; Sanjaya corpus-native six-valued structure; Jnana mapping corrected (Jnana~delta, not Knowledge); Knowledge primitive deliberately absent/corroborated; Kshetra/Kshetrajna ratified as genuine contribution; Karma/Phala corroborated but weakened to quotient-relative; Vairagya/outcome-independence independently supported; Sarathi/guidance-authority boundary independently implemented; K_atma destroyed; Theta_total rejected (does not type-check); Equality graded G1 (under-specified, not absent); =_semantic in D285-5 confirmed a methodological defect; history⊊structural⊊semantic is a verification-lane construct not corpus fact; Qualify still G1 and still the πK blocker.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **"What does each already-ratified equality relation mean operationally, and under what conditions can it be decided?"** That is exactly analogous to `Qualify`: the vocabulary exists, but the executable/formal body is missing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the equality research question away from 'what other equality should KnowledgeOS invent' toward 'what does each already-ratified equality relation mean operationally, and under what conditions can it be decided' — explicitly drawing the analogy to Qualify, where the vocabulary exists but the executable/formal body is missing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `≈` is a **family** of relations indexed by an observation set, not one relation. ... `≈_𝒬` for a declared query set `𝒬`; and `𝒬` must be declared per bounded context
a_rows_sample.statement: Target 2 (≈ observational equality) is partially derivable: its form is derivable directly from its own definition — it is a family of relations ≈_𝒬 indexed by a declared observation/query set 𝒬, not a single relation — but the set 𝒬 itself is NORMATIVE and must be declared per bounded context (since K_A(Reality)≠K_B(Reality) is a corpus principle), and parameterisation (by Ω, role, access level, or purpose — all four appear in the Sanjaya principles) is left open. The permitted-observation set is undeclared per corpus Step 261 §261.23, which states the observation set 'is not fully closed.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **structural** | 🔴 **FALSE** | ... | **semantic** | ✅ **TRUE** | only after unpacking `Assertion` ... | **observational** | 🔴 **FALSE** | answerable in `(𝒜,ℛ)`: `member`, `contradicts`, `supersede`, `lineage`. **Not answerable: `replay`, `policy-eval`, `authorize`**
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs the three equality tests against the (A,R)=πK(K_t) claim: structural equality FALSE (πK's image is {Entity,Observation,Proposition,Relation,State}, target is {Assertion,Relation}, and Assertion is not a ratified primitive); semantic equality TRUE, but only after unpacking Assertion into {Proposition,Entity,Observation}+{id,c,t,Π} modulo the declared drop; observational equality FALSE — (A,R) can answer member/contradicts/supersede/lineage queries but not replay/policy-eval/authorize.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Under the verification lane's own identity rule `id = H(P, e, c, t, Π)`, **`Π` is inside the hash.** So `o₁` and `o₂` produce assertions with *different ids*, hence **structurally different states**, and the antecedent `δ(K,o₁) = δ(K,o₂)` is **false** — the property never fires. **It fires only under semantic equality**
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows the property is equality-relative: under structural equality (id=H(P,e,c,t,Π), which includes provenance Π) o1 and o2 produce different ids, so the antecedent is false and the property never fires — vacuously true and useless under structural equality, required and load-bearing under semantic equality, and required under observational equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **1** | ⚠️ **`history ⊊ structural ⊊ semantic` is NOT a corpus hierarchy.** Measured: it occurs only in verification-lane artifacts. ... *"these are not interchangeable."* **`history` is not among them.** My citation is withdrawn
a_rows_sample.statement: Amendment 1: withdraws a citation that had claimed 'history ⊊ structural ⊊ semantic' as a corpus hierarchy — measurement shows this occurs only in verification-lane artifacts, while the corpus (location 246) defines exactly four non-interchangeable relations (structural =, semantic ≡, observational ≈, provenance-sensitive ≅_λ), and 'history' is not among them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$ \boxed{ Invariant(P) \text{ is relation-relative where }P\text{ compares objects} } $$ For example, a transformation can preserve semantic state ... while changing ... structural
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues that any invariant comparing objects is relation-relative among the four equality relations (=, ≡, ≈, ≅_λ): a transformation can preserve semantic state (K_t ≡ K_{t+1}) while changing structurally (K_t ≠_structural K_{t+1}) because metadata/representation changed, and provenance-sensitive equality may distinguish states that semantic equality identifies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: under **structural equality**, the relevant antecedent can be false; under **semantic equality**, the witness becomes substantive, but only after choosing what semantics preserve; under **observational equality**, the result depends on the permitted observation set; under **provenance-sensitive equality**, the same witness can cease to establish non-injectivity. So **"equality" is not one mathematical operation in this programme.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the D285-5 witness's behavior across all four equality relations as evidence that equality cannot be hand-waved: structural equality makes the antecedent false; semantic equality makes the witness substantive only after choosing what semantics preserve; observational equality's result depends on the permitted observation set; provenance-sensitive equality can make the same witness cease to establish non-injectivity — concluding 'equality' is not one mathematical operation in this programme but a family whose members must each be operationally decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: if we encounter something of the form $$ K_1 \equiv K_2 \Rightarrow P(K_1)=P(K_2) $$ we cannot call that a final invariant until the semantics of `≡` are fixed. ... any invariant relying upon observational equality must carry that parameter. And provenance-sensitive invariants ... must remain conditional until "relevant provenance" is formally specified.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires that any candidate invariant using an unresolved equality relation be marked explicitly conditional: a semantic-equality-based invariant is not final until ≡'s semantics are fixed; an observational-equality-based invariant must carry its query/observation-set parameter Q explicitly; a provenance-sensitive invariant must remain conditional until 'relevant provenance' is formally specified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$ \Sigma_1\approx_X\Sigma_2 \iff \pi_X(\Sigma_1)=\pi_X(\Sigma_2) $$ is a very useful reduction, but it does **not** choose which `X` KnowledgeOS should adopt. The research has reduced the governance question from "invent an observational equality" to "choose among a bounded family of projections."
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports finding F4: observational equality parameterised as Sigma_1 approx_X Sigma_2 iff their projections onto axis-subset X agree — a useful reduction of the governance question from 'invent an observational equality' to 'choose among a bounded family of projections' (32 candidate axis-subsets), but it does not itself choose X, so remains normative/governance-pending.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$ \Sigma_1 \approx_X \Sigma_2 \iff \pi_X(\Sigma_1) = \pi_X(\Sigma_2), \quad X \subseteq \{A, S, R, V, C\} $$ **The axes ARE the permitted observations.** $$ 2^5 = 32 \text{ candidate relations} $$
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the derivation that with a product state space, observational equality naturally becomes projection onto an axis subset X (Sigma_1 approx_X Sigma_2 iff pi_X(Sigma_1)=pi_X(Sigma_2)), so the axes themselves ARE the permitted observations — giving exactly 2^5=32 candidate relations forming a natural containment lattice (from ≈_∅, everything equal, to ≈_{A,S,R,V,C}, structural equality on Sigma); changes the target's status from an undefined normative parameter to a form-DERIVED relation with a bounded 32-option normative choice remaining.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `EXECUTED` — grep over all 116 documents: | "permitted observation" | **0** | | "relevant provenance" | **0** | | "semantic equality" / "equivalent propositions" | **0** | **These parameters were never lost — they were never posed.** **They are genuinely NORMATIVE, not recoverable.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes a grep over all 116 relevant documents and finds zero occurrences of 'permitted observation', 'relevant provenance', and 'semantic equality'/'equivalent propositions' — concluding these parameters were never lost from the corpus, they were never posed at all, and are therefore genuinely NORMATIVE rather than recoverable through further corpus archaeology.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### Dependency on unresolved D288 decisions Step 285 establishes the semantic projection independently of the unresolved equality procedures. It does **not** establish the decision procedures required to compute or test the relations `≡`, `≈`, or `≅_λ`, nor does it resolve `Qualify`. ... 285 establishes a **relationship** labelled semantic equality; it does not establish its **decision procedure**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends adding an explicit dependency note connecting Step 285 to D288: Step 285 establishes the semantic-equality relationship independently of the unresolved equality decision procedures, but does not establish those decision procedures for ≡, ≈, or ≅_λ, nor resolve Qualify; Step 287's invariant research may build on Step 285, but equality-dependent invariants must be marked conditional until D288 resolves -- otherwise a future reader could wrongly conclude 'Step 285 established =_semantic as an executable predicate.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: **KnowledgeOS** | ✅ **entirely** — from `id = H(P,e,c,t,Π)` and Step 246. **Derivable from typing alone** ... **Gītā** | 🔴 **NO** — 2.47–2.48 says nothing about equality relations on states ... `R6` — independently required, with ZERO philosophical content.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independence check for the equality result: the KnowledgeOS route reaches the full equality-relation result entirely and is derivable from typing alone (id=H(P,e,c,t,Pi) plus Step 246); the Gita route (Bhagavad Gita 2.47-2.48) contributes nothing to equality relations on states. Classified as 'R6' — a KnowledgeOS requirement that is independently required with zero philosophical content, described as the cleanest case in the wider programme of 'corroboration != derivation,' here with not even corroboration present.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity equivalence must be transitive within a defined identity context.
b_rows_sample.statement: Resolves the standing transitivity problem for identity equivalence (cong_I), flagged unsafe by five independent loci (25J.27, 25S.6, 25S.29, 38.16, 38.47), via context-relativization: step-195's invariant I_48 states identity equivalence must be transitive within a defined identity context, justified by 38.6/38.7/38.81's principle that RealWorldIdentity != DomainObjectIdentity and identity is contextual (KnowledgeOS must not globally impose a GlobalEntityIdentity where a domain has intentionally separate identities). Conclusion: cong_I is an equivalence relation within an identity context and is NOT one across contexts, so quotients exist per-context and are undefined globally -- described as the first genuine closure recorded on the equality axis by this research programme. Two provisos: (1) this resolves identity equivalence cong_I, not semantic equality (whether semantic equality is transitive within a semantic context remains open, though 25I.11's context-indexed relation is the same move); (2) 'identity context' itself is nowhere defined, so I_48 is well-formed with an unbound parameter, the same defect shape as other unbound relevance/observation parameters elsewhere in the programme. Step 195.15 also names the violation pattern A cong B and B cong C and A not-cong C as an 'identity consistency violation', proposed as a candidate checkable invariant.

type_signature.domain: reference x reference (within a fixed identity context)

b_rows_sample.anchor: three concepts, three questions, three answers ... Continuity appears in NONE of the five registers reconciled in Step 288
b_rows_sample.statement: Recovers 'Continuity' as a sixth relation absent from every register the programme had reconciled: Identity ('is it the same entity?'), Continuity ('does the history of one connect meaningfully to the other?'), and Similarity ('how much does it resemble the other?') are three distinct, non-collapsible concepts (195.21), with Similarity always evidence FOR identity or continuity, never either itself (195.21, 38.77: Similarity != Identity). Continuity is functionally defined: Continuity(x,y) = f(IdentityRelation, TransitionLineage, DomainRules, Evidence) (195.51) -- a relation between entities across a lineage, distinct from history-relating relations and reference-relating relations. 195.24 (boxed): Identity and Lineage are ORTHOGONAL (same identity/different states; different identity WITH continuity; different identity/no continuity), agreeing independently with a separately-cited Step 261.9 finding that Identity and Provenance equality are independent dimensions. Consequence: the equality-family register is nine relations, not eight, and Continuity is unique in having a functional definition rather than a predicate one.

type_signature.codomain: UNSTATED (functional composition of IdentityRelation, TransitionLineage, DomainRules, Evidence)

b_rows_sample.anchor: Without locale/context, normalization is ambiguous -> Normalization is itself an epistemic operation ... Canonicalization must follow evidence, not precede it
b_rows_sample.statement: Downgrades structural equality's decidability: Step 288 had placed '=' at Level 5 (decidable) throughout, qualified only by the id/mutable-state contradiction. Three loci show the decidability is itself conditional: 38.53 gives an ambiguous date string ('03/04/2026', 3 April or 4 March) showing normalization is itself an epistemic operation requiring locale/context; 38.85 states canonicalization must follow evidence, not precede it; 012 section 27 states canonicalization is not truth. Conclusion: '=' is decidable only relative to a fixed canonicalization, which the corpus forbids fixing a priori; the same defect applies to exact equality (defined as canonical serialization plus hash, 25J.2). Corrected count: zero state-level relations are unconditionally at Level 5, more severe than Step 288's own prior claim that one relation reaches Level 5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G-62 Compare undefined ... 012 section 46 defines it: Compare: P x P x C x Omega -> Q, with two companions, both partial: Resolve, Normalize
b_rows_sample.statement: Closes (narrows, not fully) the standing gap G-62 'Compare undefined': step-012 section 46 supplies a signature, Compare: P x P x C x Omega -> Q with Q = {Equivalent, Compatible, Contradictory, Related, Independent, Unknown}, plus two partial companion functions Resolve: R x C -\-> X and Normalize: R x Omega -\-> P. G-62 moves from OPEN-undefined to DEFINED(signature)-body-still-absent -- a signature is Level 3, not Level 6, so the gap narrows rather than closes. This reframes the programme's single named blocker 'Qualify' as one instance of a family of four partial epistemic functions (Qualify, Resolve, Normalize, Compare), all partial, all typed, none with bodies -- a better-posed problem (a discipline for partial epistemic functions) than a lone blocker.

type_signature.domain: Proposition x Proposition x Context x Ontology

b_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic equivalence is generally not fully decidable ... equiv can NEVER reach Level 5 in the Boolean sense. This is a theorem-shaped limit, not a work item.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens the Level-5 verdict on semantic equality (previously marked undecidable only for the weak reason 'no procedure specified'): step-012 section 35 gives the strong reason -- for arbitrary natural language, semantic equivalence P1≡P2 is not generally decidable, so KnowledgeOS cannot promise it will always determine whether two arbitrary sentences mean the same thing. This is framed as a theorem-shaped limit, not a work item: semantic equality can never reach a total Boolean decision procedure. Section 35 draws the corollary that the system must be able to say 'I don't know whether these mean the same thing' as a feature, not a failure -- the same rule independently found at three other loci (Step 224.11, 25S.4, 38.22), now four independent loci agreeing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FOUR rival codomains ... The relation itself should not be confused with its epistemic certainty. ... SC = (P1,P2,Relation,Context,Basis,Status)
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a prior count of two rival equality-decision codomains to four: 25S.3 {Same,Different,PossibleSame,Unknown}; 38.10 {Unknown,Candidate,Probable,Confirmed,Rejected,Contextual}; 012 section 35 {Determined,Supported,Candidate,Unknown}; 012 section 36/46 {Equivalent,Compatible,Contradictory,Related,Independent,Unknown}. Step 012 section 36 supplies the sorting principle: 'the relation itself should not be confused with its epistemic certainty' -- distinguishing a Relation dimension (what holds) from a Status dimension (how well we know it); 25S.3 is flagged as conflating the two (Same/Different are relations, PossibleSame/Unknown are statuses). Corpus product forms are recovered (012 section 36/47): SC=(P1,P2,Relation,Context,Basis,Status), ComparisonResult=(Relation,Basis,Confidence,Context,Provenance), ResolutionResult=(CandidateEntity,Status,Evidence,Provenance) -- equality decisions return epistemic objects, not verdicts. A non-corpus reconciliation is offered (marked DERIVED, not corpus, not adopted): Decide_equiv: K x K -> (Relation x Status), noting three of the four corpus codomains are flattenings of this product -- the same defect shape independently noted for Sigma's ten-value flattening of five axes, a second (still unpromoted) occurrence of that pattern.
