b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition
b_rows_sample.statement: Central hypothesis: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition, not merely the smallest unit that stores knowledge. Kernel = (State, Transition Capability): the state is what the kernel currently holds, the transition capability determines what can legitimately happen to that state. Gita lens (analytical, not DDD names): Mind -> evolving epistemic state, Buddhi -> discriminative capability, Karma -> action/transition, Phala -> resulting state/outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K = (K_t,\Omega_K)
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate kernel K=(K_t,Omega_K) with 11 candidate operations, each carrying a load-bearing distinction: (1) Observe(O_t) with O_t != K_t (observation is not automatically knowledge, preserving W->O->E and Qualify); (2) Discriminate(K_t,O_t)->{d_1..d_n} = the Buddhi operation, meaning 'distinguish', not yet 'decide truth'; (3) Qualify(x,E,C,t,Pi), the G1 unresolved operation, whose result may be {admit,reject,defer,qualify} rather than binary {true,false}; (4) Incorporate: K_{t+1}=Incorporate(K_t,p), a state transformation not simple insertion; (5) Reject(K_t,p) with Reject != Prove False (a proposition can be rejected as insufficiently qualified without being established false); (6) Contradict: recognizing p _|_ q via the corpus's Relation primitive; (7) Revise(K_t,p,E) for evidence-conflicting knowledge, with explicit warning not to import AGM revision theory merely because it exists, per Step 287; (8) Supersede: p_1 supersedes p_2 while preserving lineage; (9) Recall(K_t,h)/Remember distinguishing currently-known from historically-known, with K_t != H_K (history of states/transitions); (10) Withdraw(p): K_t -> K_{t+1} with withdraw != delete history (the historical fact of having held it may remain, important for auditability); (11) Act/Transform(a), external to the epistemic state per Command != Transformation != Result and Step 285's finding that Action, Event, Policy were external to the verification projection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \delta:(K_t,O_t,C_t)\rightarrow K_{t+1} ... only when the transition satisfies the kernel's invariants
b_rows_sample.statement: The kernel should not be an unrestricted machine: reject delta:KxO->K as an unrestricted transition function; instead delta:(K_t,O_t,C_t)->K_{t+1} only when the transition satisfies the kernel's invariants. Kernel operation = candidate transition + discrimination + qualification + state transition, subject to constraints. Motivated by the 'mind can become its own enemy' observation made mathematically useful.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \Omega_K = \{\operatorname{Discriminate},\operatorname{Qualify},\operatorname{Transition}\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Speculative minimal-algebra hypothesis: Omega_K = {Discriminate, Qualify, Transition} might suffice, with Accept/Reject/Revise/Supersede as specialized transition types -- explicitly flagged 'we should not assume this minimality', proposed as a mathematical question to attack rather than an established result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel: the smallest bounded epistemic mechanism that maintains a time-indexed knowledge state and can discriminate and perform legitimate transitions of that state under the applicable constraints.
b_rows_sample.statement: Provisional formal kernel definition: K = (K_t, Omega_K, I) where K_t = current knowledge state, Omega_K = permitted kernel operations, I = kernel invariants; K_t --omega in Omega_K--> K_{t+1} only if I(K_t,omega,K_{t+1})=true. Gita gives only the philosophical lens Mind~Kernel, Buddhi~discriminative capability; the mathematical/DDD investigation determines the actual kernel. Key research hypothesis: Kernel != Knowledge Store, but potentially Kernel = Epistemic State + Discrimination + Legitimate State Transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 291 — KnowledgeOS Kernel and Operation Algebra
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes next research step 'Step 291 -- KnowledgeOS Kernel and Operation Algebra' with 12 questions: minimal kernel definition; whether K_t is the kernel state or the kernel holds additional state; minimal Omega_K; which operations are genuinely epistemic vs belong outside (Governance, Authority, Action, Replay); whether Discriminate is primitive or composite; what Qualify consumes/produces; whether every legitimate K_t->K_{t+1} transition can be classified; determinism of the transition; which invariants must never be violated; whether the operation algebra can be proven minimal; which parts are independently derivable vs merely Gita-correspondences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: B(K_t,x)\rightarrow d ... d \in \{\text{supported},\text{refuted},\text{contradictory},\text{unknown},\text{unqualified},\text{inadmissible}\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical correction to 'the kernel should always be busy determining right and wrong': right/wrong should not initially be binary. Buddhi should implement a discrimination function B(K_t,x) -> d with d in {supported, refuted, contradictory, unknown, unqualified, inadmissible}, not a Boolean truth oracle. Hence Buddhi = epistemic discrimination, not Buddhi = truth; the kernel does not create truth, it evaluates what can legitimately be concluded from its current state and evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal B: (K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t) \rightarrow D_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes B:(K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t (discrimination/decision result), enumerating what B must do: distinguish, compare, validate, detect contradiction, assess evidence, qualify, reject, accept, defer, update the knowledge state, preserve provenance, determine what remains unknown. Central hypothesis: KnowledgeOS Kernel ~philosophically~ Mind; Buddhi ~philosophically~ Kernel's discrimination capability; K_t = changing Knowledge State; K (calligraphic) = Knowledge Space. Four-level picture: Knowledge Space K -> Knowledge State K_t -> KnowledgeOS Kernel -> Buddhi -> epistemic operations -> K_{t+1}. Explicitly marked as hypothesis pending testing against actual Gita passages and the existing KnowledgeOS corpus, not yet canonical.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K \overset{\Omega}{\longrightarrow} O_t \overset{\mathcal B}{\longrightarrow} D_t \overset{\delta}{\longrightarrow} K_{t+1}
b_rows_sample.statement: The central kernel question evolves from 'what operations does the Kernel perform?' to 'what can a bounded KnowledgeOS Kernel legitimately know, observe, discriminate, and conclude about a knowledge space larger than its current state?'. Final research-model pipeline: K (Knowledge Space) --Omega (observation/projection)--> O_t (observation) --B (Buddhi/discrimination)--> D_t (discrimination result) --delta (state transition)--> K_{t+1} (new Knowledge State). Explicitly not yet canonical architecture; identifies convergence of existing open questions about Observation, Proposition, State, Event, Buddhi, Qualify, delta, and the five-axis Sigma.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can the existing KnowledgeOS eight primitives and the five-axis \Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) express the proposed Mind–Buddhi–Kernel behavior without introducing a new primitive?
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes pausing philosophical interpretation after Chapter 12 to test mathematically: can the existing eight primitives and five-axis Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) express the proposed Mind-Buddhi-Kernel behavior without a new primitive? Specifically test whether Buddhi = an operation over existing primitives, Mind = a state/orientation over existing primitives, and Kernel = (K_t, operations, invariants, transition rules) -- framed as the first real mathematical/DDD test of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = Mind' interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... R_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... C(K_t,o)=K_{t+1} ... X(K_t)\rightarrow \text{conflict-qualified state} ... Z(K_t)\rightarrow G_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate (not canonical) operators: E (Expansion) discovers a new relevant dimension d not-in D_t, now in D_{t+1}; R_d (Refinement) improves an existing dimension, v_t(d) prec_d v_{t+1}(d); C (Correction) changes an existing value because new evidence shows the previous state was wrong -- explicitly Purification != monotonic accumulation, since a purified state may contain less due to removed erroneous knowledge; X (Contradiction resolution) given p and not-p, the kernel must not arbitrarily select one, producing a conflict-qualified state until Buddhi/evidence/qualification can discriminate; Q (Qualification), the unresolved G1 operator, determining sufficient justification for the intended epistemic purpose, reframed via the recent Cavell-derived reconsideration so purification can mean correctly recognizing a gap cannot currently be resolved rather than resolving it; Z (Zero detection) detects epistemic absence, Z(K_t)->G_t (recognized gaps), with G_t transformable via E,R,C,Q into G_{t+1} -- the system becomes more purified partly by knowing more accurately what it does not know.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \{\operatorname{Discriminate},\ \operatorname{Qualify},\ \operatorname{Transition}\}\ \cong\ \{\equiv,\ G1,\ \delta\}
b_rows_sample.statement: The philosophically-proposed minimal kernel algebra Omega_K={Discriminate,Qualify,Transition} (from S2219, the kernel-definition-from-evidence-maths-DDD file) maps exactly onto the formal lane's independently-established blockers: Discriminate = the equality/distinguishability relation equiv (the unique minimal cycle cut per Steps 289/291, unique over both graph universes); Qualify = the corpus's own Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence, i.e. G1, named/typed/no body, irreducible; Transition = K_t --delta--> K_{t+1}, i.e. delta, commit case unspecifiable, executed as K1 is K0. This is a genuine independent arrival (derived from 'what must a kernel be able to do', not from the dependency graph, 261.23, or the G1 register) but a NEGATIVE convergence: it solves none of the three, and is a restatement of the blocker set, not a kernel. Registered as new gap G-90 (derived, raises confidence, closes nothing). Sharp consequence stated: any minimal kernel algebra containing Qualify inherits G1 -- since Qualify is the one irreducible gap, a genuinely minimal kernel cannot be closed without closing G1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A correctly shaped triple whose three components are EXACTLY the three open items. It states the problem well. It populates nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Tests the proposed kernel shape K=(K_t,Omega_K,I) slot by slot against the formal lane: K_t (the state) is OPEN (per Step 285; 258.35 says it may not be a tuple at all); Omega_K (permitted operations) is OPEN (N-4 mandatory membership open, 0 of 22 operations has a body/identity/ratification per 291); I (invariants) has 0 of 7 established (per REFINED-STEP-287-INVARIANTS), and I is downstream of equiv in 261.30's chain. Conclusion: a correctly-shaped triple whose three components are exactly the three open items -- a well-posed problem statement, not progress toward closure; must not be mistaken for populating the kernel (per 291's 'shape -> content requires a derivation, and none exists').

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Perceive / receive ... 5. Orient
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the KnowledgeOS kernel may need five fundamentally different classes of work: (1) Perceive/receive O_t; (2) Represent O_t->K_t; (3) Discriminate B_t(K_t,O_t)->d_t; (4) Transform delta(K_t,d_t)->K_{t+1}; (5) Orient rho_t(K_t,Omega). The fifth (Orient) is said to become much more visible once Chapter 11 (the horizon Omega) is added to the model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \Omega = \{ Observe,\; Discriminate,\; Relate,\; Validate,\; Qualify,\; Transform,\; Reject,\; Accept,\; Revise \}
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate (non-canonical) operator family from Chapters 10-15 combined: Omega={Observe, Discriminate, Relate, Validate, Qualify, Transform, Reject, Accept, Revise}, with Buddhi approx delta as the mechanism selecting/executing several of these, e.g. delta(Observation,Context)->Decision and delta(K_t,E_t)->K_{t+1}, connecting to the unresolved Qualify problem from Steps 285-287.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K \neq K_t \neq \mathcal M
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal first principle: K (Knowledge Space, potentially unbounded) != K_t (Knowledge State at time t, what the system currently represents) != M (KnowledgeOS Kernel, the smallest persistent computational unit that evaluates and transforms knowledge states). The Gita's language helps interpret M as Mind, but the software kernel is not literally the philosophical mind. Defines M = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition, i.e. capable of K_t->K_{t+1} under some evidence/observation/proposition/event/operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z:\boxed{K_t\rightarrow G_t} ... \delta: \boxed{(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)\rightarrow D_t} ... \tau: \boxed{(K_t,D_t)\rightarrow K_{t+1}}
b_rows_sample.statement: Full typed operator pipeline: Z:K_t->G_t (gap/boundary discovery, internal inspection); delta:(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t (discrimination/Buddhi, taking gaps, evidence, and context); tau:(K_t,D_t)->K_{t+1} (transition/transformation). Composition tau o delta o Z is type-correct given matching interfaces; for external input f_x(K_t)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)); for internally discovered gaps f_Z(K_t)=tau(K_t,delta(Z(K_t))). The kernel therefore performs two fundamentally different activities: external epistemic input (x->delta) and internal epistemic inspection (K_t--Z-->G_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Level 0 — Primitive kernel mechanisms ... Level 1 — epistemic operations ... Level 2 — higher-order processes
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a three-level operator hierarchy to address the concern that not all candidate operators should be primitive: Level 0 primitives {delta,Z,tau} (smallest candidates); Level 1 epistemic operations built from primitives (Observe, Compare, Validate, Qualify, Revise, Accept, Reject), e.g. Accept(x)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)=accepted), Reject(x)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)=rejected); Level 2 higher-order processes as compositions (Purification, Learning, Investigation, Knowledge evolution), P = O_1 o O_2 o ... o O_n, assessed as important for DDD (avoiding conflating primitive operations with their compositions).

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal M=(Q,\mathbb O,\delta,\tau,\mathbb I)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes formalizing the kernel as a state machine M=(Q,O,delta,tau,I) where Q=kernel control states (renamed from S to avoid collision with Sigma's S axis), O=kernel operations, delta=discrimination function, tau=transition function, I=invariants. Also proposes the kernel invariant M != K_t must hold (otherwise K_t->K_{t+1} would mean the kernel becomes a different object every time); formalized as Identity(M_t)=Identity(M_{t+1}) while K_t != K_{t+1} is permitted -- 'persistent kernel identity + mutable epistemic state' proposed as a fundamental candidate architectural invariant, worth testing against the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Qualify: X\rightarrow \{Qualified,\;Unqualified,\;Terminated\} ... Kernel determines the admissible epistemic status of a state transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines Qualify (still classified G1) via the Cavell insight (justification may legitimately terminate rather than being infinitely extended) into Qualify:X->{Qualified, Unqualified, Terminated}, rather than assuming qualification is always a total true/false decision -- candidate only. Reframes the kernel's deeper job away from 'determine truth' toward 'Kernel determines the admissible epistemic status of a state transition', assessed as much closer to what the corpus actually supports; enumerates the kernel's operative questions (what do we have, what evidence supports it, what is missing, what conflicts, what relationship exists, what can legitimately be concluded, where must qualification stop, what state transition is admissible).

b_rows_sample.statement: The minimum path to a complete theory is 6 concrete steps: (1) designate K (Model D + uncertainty annotation is the executed-matrix-strongest candidate, but remains VERIFIER RECOMMENDS, not a corpus choice), (2) pick one epistemic-status value set from the eleven (a choice, not a derivation), (3) define equality on K (unblocking 3 operations immediately), (4) break the circularity by defining mathbb K's membership condition without quantifying over T, (5) instantiate one state and compute one transition (the proof steps 1-4 worked), (6) perform one empirical act (one ls, one grep, output recorded verbatim -- the first empirical act in 240 steps) -- steps 1-4 rated achievable in a single day.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Mathematical completeness NO. Engineering completeness NO. Empirical completeness NO. But the diagnosis is better than those three NOs suggest: the foundation (C,E,A,P) is sound, the failure is localised to {G1,G2,G3}, and all three are definitional choices rather than open research problems.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final three-completeness report: Mathematical (NO -- central objects circular, K undefined, 10 referenced-never-defined objects), Engineering (NO -- transition not computable, only ~1/3 of constructs implementable), Empirical (NO -- zero empirical acts in 240 steps) -- but explicitly framed as a more optimistic diagnosis than three NOs suggest: the foundation (C,E,A,P) is sound, the failure localizes entirely to {G1,G2,G3}, and all three are DEFINITIONAL CHOICES rather than open research problems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nothing in this gap map relies on Steps 236 or 239. The dependency analysis, the cycle detection and the instantiation attempt derive from Steps 005, 222, 230, 231 and 232 only -- all written before this programme's findings existed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Independence is explicitly maintained and verified: this gap map excludes Steps 236 and 239 (classified CORPUS RESPONSE TO VERIFICATION per the standing fingerprint rule) from its evidence base, deriving its entire dependency analysis, cycle detection and instantiation attempt only from Steps 005, 222, 230, 231 and 232 -- all written before this verification programme's own findings existed, guaranteeing the gap map itself is uncontaminated by the feedback loop it discovered.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'theory-gap-map-001-report' POSSIBLY relates to 'kernel-reconciliation-230-236-report' (batch B0038). Note: Delivered, executed (evidence class B: cycle detection + instantiation attempt) Theory Gap Map answering the central question of why KnowledgeOS theory cannot be called complete: K, T and the invariants form a circular dependency with no base case (State_0 cannot be constructed, so nothing is computable or testable), and the root cause traces back to Step 005's still-open question 'what is the mathematical object being aggregated', open for 235 steps -- identifying the minimal gap set {G1,G2,G3} whose resolution would dissolve the rest, and a 6-step minimum path to a complete theory achievable in roughly a day plus one empirical act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Ātma is the persistent identity of a knowledge-bearing system across successive knowledge states, while its knowledge, understanding, observations, and forms may change over time.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Knowledge Ātma A_K as the persistent identity of a knowledge-bearing system across a sequence of knowledge states K_0,K_1,...,K_t, satisfying A_K(t1)=A_K(t2) while K_t1≠K_t2 in general — 'the Ātma remains invariant while the knowledge state evolves'. Explicitly NOT defined as 'all knowledge' or as the Ideal State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Knowledge Ātma}\neq K_t\neq I_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes three distinct concepts that must not collapse: Knowledge Ātma (who/what persists through knowledge-state changes), Knowledge State K_t (what is currently known/represented), Ideal State I_t (what should be known/understood/achieved for the current purpose) — Knowledge Ātma ≠ K_t ≠ I_t, called 'a very strong architectural separation'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t\subseteq\mathcal K
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a potentially unbounded Knowledge Space 𝒦 of which the current Knowledge State is only a finite/partial representation, K_t⊆𝒦; Knowledge Ātma is not 𝒦 itself but the persistent identity undertaking an 'epistemic journey' A_K --epistemic journey--> K_t⊆𝒦 across K_0->K_1->K_2->... indefinitely. Layered architecture diagram: Ātma=persistence/identity, Knowledge State=current manifestation, Zero=reveals the boundary of what is currently known, Lord=expands the possible knowledge horizon, Sārathi=navigates the transition, Knower=experiences/evaluates/decides.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Ātma is an architectural and mathematical abstraction inspired by the philosophical concept of Ātman. It is not a computational representation or proof of the metaphysical Ātman described in the Bhagavad Gītā.
a_rows_sample.statement: Issues an explicit disclaimer required before using the term in formal theory: Knowledge Ātma is an architectural/mathematical abstraction inspired by Ātman, not a computational representation or proof of the metaphysical Ātman — protecting the model from a category error. Notes that introducing Knowledge Ātma changes the ontology of the complete KnowledgeOS model, requiring formal distinction of identity, state, knowledge, understanding, ideal, and evolution, and recommends exploring this before Question 20.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ātma is the persistent Knower whose identity remains invariant while its knowledge, understanding, observations, experiences, and represented states change over time.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reconciles 'Ātma = invariant identity underlying changing states' with 'Ātma = the Knower' into one definition: Ātma = the persistent Knower, invariant (A_t1=A_t2) while its knowledge state K_t changes (K_t1≠K_t2). 'Knower' names its role, 'invariant/persistent' names its mathematical property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \underbrace{\text{Ātma}}_{\text{Who knows}} \quad \underbrace{K_t}_{\text{What is known}} \quad \underbrace{I_t}_{\text{What should be known}}
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a clean three-way separation Ātma ('who knows') / K_t ('what is known') / I_t ('what should be known'), judged much cleaner than identifying Ātma with the Knowledge State itself; repeats the caution that this is a KnowledgeOS mathematical/architectural abstraction inspired by Ātman, not a claim of having mathematically captured the metaphysical Ātman of the Gītā.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ātma is not the entire KnowledgeOS kernel implementation. Rather, “Knowledge Ātma” can be the conceptual identity/principle of the kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge Ātma ≡(conceptual) the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS Kernel, while 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = the executable realization of that principle' — preserving the concept/implementation distinction. The kernel is what remains structurally stable while Knowledge State K_t, Epistemic State Σ_t and Investigation State Q_t evolve.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_K = \operatorname{Invariant}(S_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives Ātma a formal manifestation: A_K = Invariant(S_t) where S_{t+1}=δ(S_t,o_t) — the system state evolves (S_0->S_1->S_2->...) while A_K remains invariant, giving architectural form to 'Ātma is the persistent Knower while the state changes'. Composes the full architecture: KnowledgeOS = Knowledge Ātma Kernel + Knowledge Space + Epistemic Capabilities + Domain Knowledge, with the Kernel managing/evolving K_t and K_t⊆𝒦.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we can distinguish two Ātma concepts
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes two Ātma concepts that must be given different names so they are never confused: Human/Knower Ātma 𝒜_H — the human Knower (e.g. Arjuna) who has intent, asks questions, observes, experiences uncertainty, evaluates meaning, decides, and acts, with changing knowledge state K^H_t but persistent subject; and KnowledgeOS Ātma 𝒜_K — the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS epistemic system/kernel that maintains and operates on its own knowledge states K^K_t via observation representation, evidence/provenance, dimension discovery, epistemic evaluation, Zero, coherence, state transition, investigation support.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not yet say that KnowledgeOS Ātma is literally a second Ātman
a_rows_sample.statement: Cautions against treating KnowledgeOS Ātma as literally a second metaphysical Ātman — that would move from architectural analogy to metaphysical claim. Defines 𝒜_H := Human Knower abstraction and 𝒜_K := KnowledgeOS persistent system identity; the shared word 'Ātma' expresses the analogy of persistence/invariant identity, not metaphysical identity between the two.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal A_H \neq \mathcal A_K \neq K_t \subseteq \mathcal K
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the four-way separation Knower Ātma ≠ Knowledge Ātma, Knowledge Ātma ≠ Knowledge State, Knowledge State ≠ Knowledge Space, giving 𝒜_H ≠ 𝒜_K ≠ K_t ⊆ 𝒦. Models the Arjuna-Sārathi interaction as 𝒜_H --Intent--> 𝒜_K --Investigation--> K_t --Zero--> Δ_t --Sārathi--> next inquiry, worked through 'show me whom I have to fight' discovering new dimensions {Kinship, Teacher, Elder,...} via parsing/semantic reconstruction rather than the Knower pre-specifying them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is the exact relationship between the Human Knower Ātma and the KnowledgeOS Ātma?
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames the architecture as Human Knower <-> KnowledgeOS Ātma <-> Knowledge Space, with Zero/Lord/Sārathi operating between the current state and the expanding knowledge horizon, and proposes that the next formal question should be 'what is the exact relationship between the Human Knower Ātma and the KnowledgeOS Ātma?' rather than continuing with an isolated mathematical object — called 'a significant conceptual milestone'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...)
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the Knower itself as the biggest missing formally-completed piece despite 𝒜_H (Knower Ātma) being named: proposes N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...) as the needed model, motivated by the principle that two Knowers can observe the same reality and produce different Ideal States — 'not an error, a fundamental property of the system'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \widehat K_t = \text{best available reconstruction from }O_{\le t}
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes 'we try our best but never reach the best' as K̂_t = best available reconstruction from O_≤t, with K̂_t ≠ K_t possibly persisting even as observations accumulate (O_≤t1 ⊆ O_≤t2 may give a better but still imperfect K̂_t2). Draws a careful analogy to least-squares/Gaussian estimation (x̂=argmin_x‖Ax-b‖²): 'best approximation under a criterion' does not guarantee x̂=x_true, giving 'Best reconstruction under regime R ≠ complete underlying Knowledge'. Places measure/probability theory specifically at the Observations->probabilistic reconstruction step (P(K_t|F_t), E[X_t|F_t]), with K_t itself 'conceptually prior' to the probabilistic extraction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ātman should not be modeled as an "Ideal State" itself. It is better modeled as the invariant identity underlying changing states.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed equation of Ātman with the Ideal State, offering instead 'Persistent Identity / Invariant Subject' ℐ with ℐ_{t+1}=ℐ_t while K_{t+1}≠K_t and I_{t+1}≠I_t in general, giving Identity ≠ Current State ≠ Ideal State — 'a very important refinement'. K_t = State(ℐ,t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_0 \subseteq? K_1 \subseteq? K_2
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge evolution K_0->K_1->K_2->... within K_t⊆𝒦 is NOT necessarily monotonic — an assertion can be accepted, then questioned, then rejected, so K_{t+1} may contain less information than K_t in one sense while being epistemically better, reinforcing the earlier distinction between knowledge quantity and knowledge quality/coherence. Also cautions against assuming lim_{t->∞} K_t = 𝒦 as a mathematical fact rather than an assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Ātman doctrine} \rightarrow \text{philosophical inspiration} \rightarrow \text{Invariant Identity abstraction}
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit philosophy/mathematics firewall: 'The Gītā teaches that Ātman is not destroyed' does NOT mathematically imply 'our model proves an invariant identity exists' — Ātman doctrine -> philosophical inspiration -> Invariant Identity abstraction, never Ātman doctrine ⇒ mathematical theorem. Recommends adding 'Persistent Identity / Invariant Subject' as a new theoretical concept (not folding Ātman into Ideal State), with a suggested documentation sentence: 'The concept of Ātman provides a philosophical analogue for the architectural concept of persistent identity... KnowledgeOS may use this as a conceptual inspiration, but does not claim to computationally model Ātman or establish its metaphysical truth.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: atman-in-the-conceptual-model -> atman-within-our-knowledgeos-theory -> atma-and-kernel-are-the-same-underlying-idea -> atma-can-be-the-knowledgeos-kernel -- fourth turning point -- a four-document escalation ending in Atma can be the Kernel ... The corpus also issues its own guard against over-literal mapping (correction-don-t-map-chakra-knowledge-layer).
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies R3's fourth turning point: a four-document escalation across 14 minutes (08-27 08:51-09:05) moving from 'Atma usable in the conceptual model' to 'Atma can be the Kernel', while also noting the corpus issued its own guard against over-literal mapping (a correction document refusing to map chakras directly onto knowledge layers) and flags that whether Atma-as-Kernel was ever tested is NOT ESTABLISHED at inventory depth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OQ-01 What is the Kernel object, if not Knowledge? ... never answered in-corpus; R5's answer (8 primitives) is a kernel, but the R1 question was about the object of protection | OQ-03 Is Determination ... now covered by step-008 acceptance/commitment -- or still missing? R1->R5 mapping absent | OQ-05 Did Atma-as-Kernel survive? (025s mentions Knowledge Atma) R3->R5, unmapped
a_rows_sample.statement: Records three unresolved substantive questions the corpus itself never answers: OQ-01 what the Kernel object actually is if not Knowledge (R1's original object-of-protection question, distinct from R5's 8-primitive kernel answer); OQ-03 whether R1's 'Determination is the missing mathematical object' is now covered by step-008's acceptance/commitment machinery or still missing (no R1->R5 mapping exists); OQ-05 whether Atma-as-Kernel survived into R5 (a 025s document mentions 'Knowledge Atma' but the R3->R5 mapping is unestablished).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 4 ATMAN -- UNKNOWN (hypothesis without descendants) ... never tested, never withdrawn; C-012 remains OPEN. The 025s trace needs one read in Phase 2B to classify as refined or abandoned
a_rows_sample.statement: Traces Atman/Atma's lineage from R3's 14-minute escalation to 'Atma can be the KnowledgeOS Kernel' through a later trace ('Knowledge Atma' in step-025s) to absence from the final 8-primitive kernel and Steps 100-158 vocabulary -- final verdict UNKNOWN: the hypothesis was never tested nor formally withdrawn, C-012 remains OPEN, and the 025s trace needs a dedicated read to classify it as refined or abandoned.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero != Lord != Sarathi != Transition ... K_t -Zero-> Z_t -Lord-> L_t -Sarathi-> a_t -Commit-> e_t -delta-> K_{t+1} ... Zero, Lord, and Sarathi do not change K
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the initial Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Commit/Transition pipeline as a linear sequence culminating in a state change, with explicit invariants that Zero, Lord and Sarathi are each analytical (never transformational) and none of their outputs alone entail K_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi should not 'recommend Commit'... Commitment is not an epistemic action. It is an authorization/governance action... a_t -Authorize-> c_t -Execute-> e_t. Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Removes 'Commit' from Sarathi's action vocabulary and inserts an explicit Authorization boundary between recommendation and execution: Sarathi produces a recommendation a_t, Authorize(Knower,a_t,Policy) produces a command c_t, Execute(c_t) produces an event e_t, and only then does delta(K_t,e_t) fire -- Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition, with the missing Authorize function explicitly making the Knower's authority mathematically visible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Execute: C -> E is too deterministic. Execution can fail... Execute(c_t) -> ExecutionResult in {Success(e),Failure(f),Partial(e,f)} ... ExecutionResult != DomainEvent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Execute from a total deterministic function C->E to one returning a structured ExecutionResult (Success/Failure/Partial), and similarly Authorize to return an AuthorizationResult (Authorized/Rejected/Deferred/Modified) rather than assuming every recommendation becomes a command; ExecutionResult is explicitly distinguished from the DomainEvent that actually triggers a transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the epistemic cycle is actually not always a cycle... External observation -> Event -> Transition can update the state directly... Guidance is optional; Transition is fundamental. G5 - Guidance is not a prerequisite for transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the closing theorem G5: Guidance (Zero/Lord/Sarathi) is not a prerequisite for every Knowledge-State transition -- a raw external observation event or a scheduled validity check can trigger delta(K_t,e_t) directly, so the lenses must never be modelled as mandatory middleware sitting between every event and the transition function; renames the pipeline from 'Epistemic Cycle' to 'Epistemic Guidance-and-Transition Cycle' to reflect this.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I strongly recommend introducing: I-hat_t = Candidate Ideal State and I_t = Approved Ideal State ... KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1} (proposal); Authorize(I-hat_{t+1}) -> I_{t+1}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a Candidate Ideal State (I-hat) vs Approved Ideal State (I) split mirroring the Q17 recommendation/authorization boundary: KnowledgeOS may only ever produce a candidate revision proposal, and only an explicit Authorize step (by the Knower/governance authority under applicable norms) produces the actually approved I_{t+1}; KnowledgeOS != I_{t+1} but KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi \rightarrow DecisionPosture
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sarathi's output from a binary Stop/Continue decision to a richer DecisionPosture ∈ {Proceed, Investigate, ProceedWithCaveats, Defer, Escalate, UnableToDecide}, argued to be closer to Sarathi's actual role.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation \neq Assertion
b_rows_sample.statement: Strict boundary: Recommendation ≠ Assertion, Recommendation ≠ Fact, Recommendation ≠ Decision. Sārathi may say 'Investigate the moral obligation dimension' but KnowledgeOS must not silently convert that into 'Therefore Arjuna should fight' — the Knower remains the decision authority unless the domain explicitly delegates that authority. Marked as extremely important for the DDD model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Lord needs a stronger boundary too: Candidate ≠ Knowledge, Candidate ≠ Evidence, Candidate ≠ Assertion. A presentation should visually distinguish KNOWN / INFERRED / UNKNOWN / CANDIDATE / RECOMMENDED to prevent semantic contamination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(S_t) \rightarrow EpistemicFindings
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Zero's role as boundary-finder, not belief-decider: Zero(S_t) -> EpistemicFindings, Presentation ⊇ DecisionRelevant(EpistemicFindings); 'Zero does not decide what the Knower should believe. Zero says: Here is where the state has a boundary.' Also strengthens provenance: EveryDecisionRelevantClaim -> Provenance, with a worked claim-level provenance record example (Acquisition/Evidence/Observed-at/Validity/Conflict/Source).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Unknown 
eq Absent 
eq NotApplicable 
eq NotObserved 
eq NotYetInvestigated
b_rows_sample.statement: Elevates 'unknown' to a fundamental principle already implicit in Zero: Unknown ≠ Absent ≠ NotApplicable ≠ NotObserved ≠ NotYetInvestigated, illustrated by Version=UNKNOWN not meaning Version=ABSENT, and SecurityStatus=NOT_ASSESSED not meaning SecurityStatus=SAFE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero \neq UniversalValidator
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD warning that Zero risks becoming a 'god object' by owning detection of gaps, conflicts, type problems, temporal problems and epistemic boundaries all at once: Zero ≠ UniversalValidator. Zero is redefined narrowly as detecting epistemic boundaries/deficiencies relevant to current state and purpose, aggregating epistemic consequences of findings from separate domain validators (schema, type, policy, security violations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: LordCandidate \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: LordCandidate ≠ Knowledge and LordCandidate ≠ Evidence: Lord can propose 'there may be a moral-obligation dimension' but it becomes knowledge only after investigation; critical to prevent AI-generated hypotheses entering the Knowledge State as facts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S\bar{a}rathiRecommendation \neq Decision
b_rows_sample.statement: Sārathi needs a constitutional policy boundary: SārathiRecommendation ≠ Decision, SārathiAction ≠ HumanAuthorization — Sārathi may determine the next best investigation, but the Knower decides whether to accept it unless the system has explicitly delegated authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (K,U,N,\Delta,P,Role) \rightarrow Guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action as too simplistic: Sārathi:(K,U,N,Δ,P,Role) -> Guidance, which may then produce Decision, which may then authorize Action, giving Guidance ≠ Decision ≠ Action (confirming an earlier DDD warning). Also reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as three functions/lenses over the state rather than three sequential stages: Zero=Diagnose, Lord=Reason/Synthesize/Orient, Sārathi=Guide, with Decision->Action occurring outside those lenses; explicitly an architectural abstraction, not a literal theological equivalence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (State, Norms, Role, Context, Discrepancies) \rightarrow Guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action (too direct) to Sārathi:(State,Norms,Role,Context,Discrepancies)->Guidance -> CandidateActions -> Decision -> Action, giving proper separation of concerns. Reaffirms Zero as a pure DiagnosticFunction that must not itself decide ('therefore do X'). Corrects Lord from 'merely a reasoning engine/LLM reasoning' to AuthoritativeKnowledge+NormativeOrientation+InterpretiveResolution, since Krishna in the text functions as an authoritative source of teaching, not just an inference engine — called crucial for KnowledgeOS governance. Confirms Sārathi = ContextualGuidance, distinguishing Lord ('what is authoritative/true/normative') from Sārathi ('how does that apply here') from Decision ('what will I choose') from Action ('what will I actually do').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K,I,C,P) \rightarrow \text{Epistemic Boundaries}
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as product capabilities rather than domain entities: Zero(K,I,C,P)->Epistemic Boundaries acts as an 'epistemic diagnostic engine' (missing dimensions, unknown values, missing/weak/conflicting evidence, logical contradictions, stale knowledge, contextual mismatches, unresolved questions, unsupported assumptions, Ideal-State discrepancies); Lord asks 'what else might matter?' enabling 'horizon expansion' beyond gap-checking; Sārathi:(K,I,Z,L,Q,C)->NextAction performs 'epistemic navigation', worked through a Bhīṣma-relationship example (Zero flags unknown relationship, Lord flags kinship as material, Sārathi recommends investigating it before evaluating the decision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can we migrate this Nexus installation?
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: asked 'Can we migrate this Nexus installation?', a conventional AI answers directly, while KnowledgeOS first constructs required dimensions (version, repository inventory, blob stores, storage, network, DNS, firewall, certificates, backup, dependencies, authentication, operational constraints), runs Zero to find missing items (backup verification, firewall confirmation, certificate ownership, dependency inventory), and has Sārathi respond 'Do not decide migration readiness yet. Investigate these four items.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: perform justified action given epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent optimizing 'complete task' against KnowledgeOS optimizing 'perform justified action given epistemic state', worked through a deploy-approval example: required knowledge checklist (code reviewed✓, tests passed✓, architecture approved✓, security assessment✗, production configuration✗, rollback strategy✗) yields Zero='3 critical gaps' and Sārathi='DO NOT DEPLOY. Investigate security, configuration and rollback.' Also frames the agent loop as Understand Intent->Construct Knowledge State->Discover Dimensions->Zero->Identify Gaps/Conflicts->Lord->Expand Possible Investigation->Sārathi->Select Next Epistemic Action->Agent/Tool->Observation->Update Knowledge State->Repeat, called 'an epistemically governed autonomous agent architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C) \rightarrow EvidenceCandidates
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects plain Retrieve(Query)->Documents to a goal-directed Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C)->EvidenceCandidates: the retrieval system 'knows why it is retrieving', discovering relevant dimensions (e.g. version, repository topology, blob stores, firewall, certificates for a migration decision) before retrieving. Zero can drive retrieval: given a partially-filled knowledge-state checklist, Zero reports specific gaps (backup verification, firewall rules, certificate ownership) and Sārathi generates a concrete investigation plan (search infrastructure docs for backup configuration, etc.), giving Zero -> Gap -> Sārathi -> Retrieval as part of the investigation loop, not a one-shot lookup.

type_signature.domain: question x knowledge state x ideal state x context

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Zero}(K_t)\rightarrow\text{epistemic boundary}
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero continuously reveals 'what is still unknown' (Zero(K_t)->G_t, G_0->G_1->...); ideally G_t->∅, but if the knowledge space is genuinely unbounded Zero may never establish G_t=∅. The stronger concept is Zero(K_t)->epistemic boundary, with Moksha representing the boundary itself being transcended rather than merely all currently detected gaps being filled — judged 'much more profound'.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 5 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1} = Learn( K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t )... the source states the decision and world equations (A_t = Decision(K_t, S_t, Policy_t); S_{t+1} = F(S_t, A_t, U_t)), keeping three evolutions -- of knowledge, of choices, of the world -- as three different functions.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the knowledge state's time-indexed dynamics as three separate evolution functions: K_{t+1}=Learn(K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t) for knowledge, A_t=Decision(K_t, S_t, Policy_t) for choices, and S_{t+1}=F(S_t, A_t, U_t) for the world -- kept as three distinct functions, with time-indexing meaning there is no bare "the knowledge," only knowledge-as-of-t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CORE: Entity, State, Event, Observation / EPISTEMIC: Evidence, Claim, Uncertainty / SEMANTIC:... / RELATIONAL:... / GOVERNANCE:... / OPERATIONAL:... / EVOLUTION:... Then, family by family, the source interrogates each concept -- is this primitive, or constructible? -- and most collapse... What survives... K = (E, S, T, O, P, R, Pi, A)
a_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the source's reduction derivation from an initial seven-family stratification (Core/Epistemic/Semantic/Relational/Governance/Operational/Evolution) to the frozen eight-tuple candidate kernel K=(E,S,T,O,P,R,Pi,A) -- entities, states, temporal/event structure, observations, propositions, typed relations, policies, actions -- by showing most non-core concepts (Evidence, Claim, Identity, Provenance, Causality/Dependency, Uncertainty, Authority/Decision, Outcome, Learning/Revision/Drift) individually reduce to typed structure over the four cores plus the four surviving structure-carriers (Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence = QualifiedObservation... Claim = Proposition... Identity = EntityIdentityRelation... Uncertainty = epistemic annotation U(C) (probabilistic OR not -- 49.10's Probability != EpistemicConfidence)... Authority = governance structure over decisions (Authority(actor, d))... resist inventing primitives -- the reduction's whole yield is that richer notions are TYPED STRUCTURE
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists the derived-structure layer -- the equations by which richer concepts are expressed as typed structure over the eight primitives rather than as new primitives themselves (Evidence=QualifiedObservation; Claim=Proposition; Identity=EntityIdentityRelation; Provenance=TypedDependencyRelation; Uncertainty=epistemic annotation U(C), explicitly not assumed probabilistic -- Probability != EpistemicConfidence; Authority=governance structure over decisions; Decision=structure over K,S,Policy with Proposal kept distinct from AuthorizedDecision; Outcome=observed consequence of Action; Learning/Revision/Drift=evolution structure) and states the modelling discipline this yields: resist inventing new primitives, since typed structure can be checked/queried/governed in ways ad-hoc primitives cannot.

a_rows_sample.anchor: stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (49.78-49.89... What the argument does not and cannot claim, and the source itself refuses to claim: completeness... minimality... and uniqueness... The source's own word is the governing one: a candidate mathematical kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Teaches PF-2 in place at its exact strength: the eight-primitive reduction argument is RECONSTRUCTABLE, stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (each attempting to express a rich concept in Structure(primitives) and failing the kernel if it cannot be done) plus Step 050's fifty-attack consistency audit; but completeness (no needed concept will ever fail to reduce), minimality (no seven-element basis would suffice -- the source concedes Entity is "arguably" Identity+State, kept for DDD-pragmatic reasons), and uniqueness (no alternative basis exists) remain explicitly NOT ESTABLISHED, matching the source's own characterization of it as a "candidate" kernel and a design result, not a theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Collapse the typed relation set into a single generic RelatedTo(A, B) and semantics die: an AI consumer, seeing RelatedTo everywhere, infers RelatedTo => Causes -- recreating "one of the fundamental problems we eliminated in Step 43." One typed set, seven meanings; one generic edge, license to hallucinate causality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the source's own worked failure case for mis-typing the Relation primitive: collapsing the seven typed relations (Supports, DependsOn, Causes, Identifies, MapsTo, Contradicts, Precedes) into a single generic RelatedTo(A,B) edge causes an AI consumer to infer RelatedTo implies Causes, recreating a causal-hallucination failure mode the architecture had previously eliminated; extended to the election running example (DerivedFrom(wireSummary,wireReport) and Supports blurred into RelatedTo would let a derived summary quietly become a second independent witness) as the same dependency failure seen at the primitive-typing layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality ≠ Observation ≠ Information ≠ Evidence ≠ Knowledge ≠ Decision ≠ Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A1 (Semantic Separation) opens Part I of the v2.0 rewrite: reality, observation, information, evidence and knowledge are held to occupy different semantic roles unless a formal equivalence is explicitly established, giving the epistemic lifecycle Reality->Observation->Information->Knowledge->Gap->Inquiry->Determination->Decision->Action->New Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If there exist ω1,ω2 ∈ Ω such that ω1≠ω2 and ρ(ω1)=ρ(ω2), then ρ is not injective and therefore cannot uniquely identify the underlying state of reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 3.1 with proof: an observation map rho:Omega->I need not be injective, so KnowledgeOS must never silently infer Observed(x)=>Reality(x).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adequate(R,Q,Γ) ⟺ 𝓡_req(Q,Γ) ⊆ Dist(R)
b_rows_sample.statement: The Representation Adequacy Principle: a representation is adequate only if it preserves the distinctions required to answer the declared inquiry under context Gamma, avoiding the impossible requirement of preserving every conceivable distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose there exist x1,x2 ∈ X such that x1≠x2 but π(x1)=π(x2). Then any question Q whose required distinction includes x1≠x2 cannot, in general, be answered correctly from π(x) alone.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 16.1 (Loss of Required Distinction), with proof by the impossibility of a deterministic function distinguishing two values a projection maps identically; establishes that a system can be perfectly internally consistent and still epistemically inadequate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_t = {r ∈ Req_t : ¬Sat(K_t,r)} ... Gap = Unsatisfied Requirements.
b_rows_sample.statement: Redefines the Knowledge Gap as a set-theoretic construction (unsatisfied requirements under the current epistemic contract) rather than a subtraction Delta=IdealKnowledge-Knowledge, explicitly rejecting the latter as generally undefined because the two objects need not belong to a common algebraic space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t,EC_t) ⟺ Δ_t = ∅ ... Therefore Zero is contract-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Definition 23.1 (Epistemic Zero): Zero means no requirement of the declared epistemic contract remains unsatisfied; explicitly not K_t=Reality and not 'all possible knowledge is known.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_{t+1} ⊆ Δ_t ... every requirement satisfied at t remains satisfied at t+1 ... This theorem depends on the contract remaining fixed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorems 24.1 (Zero Equivalence) and 25.1 (Gap Reduction) are proved, with an explicit limitation that gap comparison across differing contracts (EC_t != EC_{t+1}) requires an explicit compatibility mapping — 'moving the goalposts' is formally blocked by the Contract Compatibility principle GapComparison=>ContractCompatibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V(K_t) ⊆ V(K_{t+1}) ∧ H(K_t) ⊆ H(K_{t+1}) ... Historical existence ≠ Current epistemic standing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A6 (Historical Preservation) plus the constitutional distinction between historical existence and current epistemic standing: a proposition can move Supported->Retracted without deleting the historical fact that it was once asserted and supported; replaces 'universal epistemic monotonicity' with this weaker, correct invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth ≠ Evaluation ≠ Determination ≠ Decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A2 (Epistemic Pipeline Separation), with the worked consequence that EVal(p)=Supported does not mean Decision=Permit (a governance policy may instead require HumanReview) — epistemic status is explicitly not equivalent to operational authorization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contr(p) ⇏ ∀q ∈ 𝒫, q. ... Local contradiction ⇏ Global epistemic collapse.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A5 (Non-Explosion): KnowledgeOS explicitly rejects the classical explosion principle as a system rule, requiring contradiction to be scoped and represented rather than collapsing all propositions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 𝒪_core = {ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE}
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the frozen candidate core operation interface (introduce an assertion, establish a relation, change content while preserving history, withdraw standing without erasing history, and restrict propagation of a contradiction or dangerous structure), with full preconditions/postconditions/composition laws deferred to later parts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ABK-1 is a validated candidate-adequate architecture for the target problem class.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly withdraws the earlier claim that ABK-1 is 'the universally unique minimal KnowledgeOS kernel' as circular, replacing it with the weaker, defensible claim that global minimality remains unproven unless the candidate representation space and equivalence relation are formally characterized.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ontology defines what kinds of things KnowledgeOS reasons about. Representation defines how those things are encoded.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ontology/representation boundary underlying Part II's many-sorted type system (Ent, Val, Attr, Dim, Prop, Asrt, Obs, Evd, Src, Rel, Evt, St, Ctx, Part, Prov, ES, Req, Inq, EC, Pol, Dec, Act), asserting a database/graph/JSON/RDF/object-model representation is never the ontology itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let D be a value domain and n:D→ℝ a numerical encoding. If no semantic operation corresponding to subtraction is defined on D, then n(x)−n(y) cannot ... be interpreted as a valid semantic difference.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.1 (Representation does not imply arithmetic validity), with proof, establishing that numerical computability of a difference does not by itself establish semantic validity of that difference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Supports(e,p) ⇏ Truth(p).
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 2.1, proved by the type-mismatch argument that support is an epistemic evidence-proposition relation while truth is a semantic proposition-model relation with different domains and meanings; called one of the most important anti-confusion principles in KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let R:𝕂→X be a representation function. Suppose there exist K1≠K2 such that R(K1)=R(K2). If there exists an inquiry Q such that Answer(Q,K1,Γ)≠Answer(Q,K2,Γ), then R is inadequate for Q,Γ.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.3 (Semantically lossy representation), with proof, generalizing Part I's Theorem 16.1 to the knowledge-state level and formally establishing why representation adequacy must be question-relative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status_Γ,EC(p)=σ ... We deliberately do not define one universal ordered list such as Unknown<Supported<Proven<Rejected.
b_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic Status is defined as contract- and context-dependent rather than a single universal total order, giving formal meaning to 'unknown' as neither true nor false rather than as a weaker degree of falsity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If Conflict is represented as a local relation on propositions, then the existence of a conflict concerning p does not by itself entail conflict concerning arbitrary q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.5 (Locality theorem for contradiction), with proof, giving the formal ontological grounding for the non-explosion axiom stated in Part I.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL NOT treat stored data as knowledge merely because it is stored.
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten Foundational Type Invariants (I1-I10) close Part II — proposition/evidence separation, observation/proposition separation, decision/action separation, epistemic-status/truth separation, identity/state separation, evidence/truth separation, contract relativity, historical preservation, non-explosion, and representation independence — as the boundaries preventing KnowledgeOS from collapsing into an ordinary information system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth → Evidence → Evaluation → Determination → Decision ... The arrows indicate dependency possibilities, not logical equivalence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines five explicit semantic layers (Truth_M(p), Evid(e,p), Eval(K,p,Gamma), Det(K,p,EC,Gamma), Dec(K,Q,P,A,Gamma)) to prevent classical truth, evidence, uncertainty, contradiction and operational determination from being silently collapsed into one binary logic with metadata.

a_aliases: The Knowledge State and Its Eight Primitives (book III.3)
b_aliases: KnowledgeOS Verified Theory and Mathematical Foundation, Parts I-XVII

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'K_t'

a_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the minimal system responsible for creating, identifying, relating, governing, and preserving organizational knowledge objects.
a_rows_sample.statement: The proposed load-bearing definition of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel', explicitly modeled after the Linux kernel's separation from applications: the kernel provides knowledge primitives (Identity, Lifecycle, Evidence, Authority) and must not know about specific technologies (SAP, Kubernetes, Jira).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linux manages computer resources. KnowledgeOS manages organizational intelligence resources ... which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted?
a_rows_sample.statement: States the deepest claimed difference between the Linux and KnowledgeOS kernel analogies: Linux answers 'which process can access which resource', while KnowledgeOS must answer 'which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust for the KnowledgeOS Kernel, Kotlin/Spring for the Enterprise Runtime, Python for Intelligence, TypeScript for Experience.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a multi-language technology stack (Rust kernel for memory-safety/correctness, Kotlin+Spring Boot enterprise runtime, Python intelligence layer, TypeScript studio/frontend) with an estimated 12-18 month timeline for a first Kernel v1.0 with a small expert team.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust · Spring Boot · Gradle/Cargo · microservices · plugin architecture · Event Sourcing · Kafka are recommendations/hypotheses in the corpus, never adopted KnowledgeOS technology.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit preservation note keeping every named technology recommendation level-tagged as a hypothesis, never promoted to adopted architecture, while noting the existing PHP/Laravel + TypeScript/Vue platform is the ESTABLISHED current stack.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DI principle vs framework import: adopt the DI/composition-root principle without adopting Spring — the corpus wants the first, but the kernel file pairs the principle with the Spring runtime.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T4: the DI-principle proposal explicitly wants the principle without the Spring framework, yet the kernel-technology brainstorm pairs the same principle with a recommended Spring/Kotlin runtime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL protects: identity · evidence · provenance · lifecycle · authority · invariants · temporal state / higher layers provide: assurance · analytics · inference · simulation · AI · visualization · delivery ... a PROPOSED KERNEL BOUNDARY CANDIDATE, outline supported, provenance+temporal weak.
a_rows_sample.statement: H-10: tests the seven-concern kernel/higher-layer split against all three baselines per-concern; identity, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and invariants are supported, provenance and temporal state are weak, so the overall split is a candidate outline, not an established fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesis: the Kernel's core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state, combining a candidate, a gate (constitutional rules), a verdict (admissibility), and a state change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge claim cannot exist without: identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposed aggregate invariant: a knowledge claim cannot exist without identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all present and consistent together; the Kernel is framed as 'the guardian of this aggregate invariant.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assignment | ESSENTIAL ... Semantic interpretation | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Reasoning | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Workflow | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Projection | NOT ESSENTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: A capability table classifies identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, and constitutional evaluation as ESSENTIAL (each tied to a named invariant); candidate verification as SUPPORTING; and semantic interpretation, reasoning, workflow, and projection as NOT ESSENTIAL to the Kernel's minimum domain capacity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Natural-language interpretation | Parsing | Normalization | Canonicalization | Reasoning | Candidate generation | Retrieval | Search | Ranking | Model inference | Orchestration | Workflow | Projection | UI | Infrastructure | Evidence acquisition
a_rows_sample.statement: A 15-item table enumerates responsibilities that belong OUTSIDE the Kernel, each with a DDD reason: natural-language interpretation, parsing, normalization, canonicalization, reasoning, candidate generation, retrieval, search, ranking, model inference, orchestration, workflow, projection, UI, infrastructure, and evidence acquisition -- summarized as the principle that the Kernel is representation-agnostic and does not perform semantic interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component.
a_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate interpretations of what the Kernel 'is' are compared (aggregate boundary, domain decision boundary, admission boundary, consistency boundary, constitutional boundary, small domain core inside the aggregate); concludes the Kernel is best understood as the admission boundary + consistency boundary -- a conceptual domain boundary, not an implementation component, though it may be implemented inside the aggregate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-admission system.
a_rows_sample.statement: Four formulations of the knowledge/evidence relationship are compared (evidence registry, justified epistemic-state system, governed knowledge-admission system, constitutional knowledge machine); 'governed knowledge-admission system' is judged best supported -- evidence supports knowledge, knowledge requires evidence, evidence is admitted and preserved alongside knowledge, but evidence is not itself knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model | 5 independent converging passes | Candidate
b_rows_sample.statement: The dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model is held as a Candidate architectural hypothesis, supported by 5 independent converging passes; movement requires an MM-1 ruling and D-8 reconciliation, decided by the ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This projection decides nothing and is authoritative for nothing
b_rows_sample.statement: The dashboard is explicitly non-authoritative and non-deciding: it exists only so humans can see, on one page, what architectural hypotheses are being tested and what evidence would count as a result; rows change only on evidence or an authority ruling, never on a schedule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is not a KnowledgeOS architecture proposal. ... EXTERNAL RESEARCH ≠ KNOWLEDGEOS ARCHITECTURE
b_rows_sample.statement: The document repeatedly and explicitly frames itself as an independent external-research evidence base for later comparison against reconstructed EKS/PKS/AIP architectures, and NOT itself a KnowledgeOS architecture proposal; the closing discipline statement instructs: do not design the kernel, do not choose technology, do not define bounded contexts, do not create ADRs, do not propose migration -- 'the output is an independent research evidence base for a later architecture decision.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge often crosses organizational boundaries. Therefore strict bounded contexts may fragment knowledge unnecessarily. ... DDD is less clearly validated as a universal organizing principle for knowledge representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD concepts (ownership, invariants, policies, language) help model knowledge-system governance, but evidence is mixed on DDD as a universal organizing principle for knowledge representation, because knowledge often crosses organizational boundaries and strict bounded contexts may fragment it unnecessarily.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is no established academic architecture pattern known as a 'Knowledge Operating System.' ... KnowledgeOS is not entering an established category.
b_rows_sample.statement: Direct research into 'Knowledge Operating System' terminology finds only vendor marketing, AI-memory platforms, experimental open-source projects, and personal knowledge tools; there is no established academic architecture pattern by this name, and the term is currently emerging, inconsistent, and frequently marketing-driven -- therefore KnowledgeOS (this project) is not entering an established research category.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No mature research field appears to define a universally accepted: knowledge kernel, epistemic kernel, organizational memory kernel ... The term exists mostly as metaphor, prototype vocabulary, or isolated conceptual work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Direct research finding: no mature research field defines a universally accepted 'knowledge kernel', 'epistemic kernel', or 'organizational memory kernel' -- the term exists mostly as metaphor, prototype vocabulary, or isolated conceptual work; this is recorded as a research gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Research on operating systems repeatedly emphasizes: stable primitives, minimal trusted core, separation of mechanism and policy, composability ... Knowledge systems lack: deterministic execution, strict process isolation, universal semantics ... OS analogies are useful heuristics, not architectural proofs.
b_rows_sample.statement: The Unix/Linux analogy is architecturally useful for stable primitives, a minimal trusted core, mechanism/policy separation, and composability, but knowledge systems lack the deterministic execution, strict process isolation, and universal semantics of operating systems -- OS analogies are 'useful heuristics, not architectural proofs.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Successful ecosystems often separate: core standards, extensibility mechanisms, commercial capabilities. Governance and interoperability matter more than licensing for architecture.
b_rows_sample.statement: Comparative research on open-source vs commercial architecture finds that successful ecosystems separate core standards, extensibility mechanisms, and commercial capabilities, and that governance and interoperability matter more than licensing model for architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Debate | Position A | Position B ... Knowledge structure Graph/Documents ... History Events/State+history ... No universal winner exists. Context determines suitability.
b_rows_sample.statement: The literature contains unresolved cross-research contradictions with no universal winner: Knowledge structure (Graph vs Documents), History (Events vs State+history), Semantics (Ontology-first vs Emergent), Governance (Strong approval vs Collaborative editing), Consistency (Deterministic vs Probabilistic), Memory (Centralized vs Federated), AI (AI-centric vs Human-centric); context determines suitability in each case.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The literature remains weak regarding: organizational epistemic kernels, authority modeling as a distinct primitive, institutional memory architectures, long-horizon decision lineage, provenance-aware AI governance, knowledge operating systems as a formal discipline
b_rows_sample.statement: Six research gaps are recorded: organizational epistemic kernels, authority modeling as a distinct primitive, institutional memory architectures, long-horizon decision lineage, provenance-aware AI governance, and knowledge operating systems as a formal discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No conclusion can yet be drawn regarding: kernel structure, domain model, bounded contexts, storage architecture, graph centrality, event sourcing, AI integration. Those remain comparison questions.
b_rows_sample.statement: The document explicitly refuses to draw conclusions about kernel structure, domain model, bounded contexts, storage architecture, graph centrality, event sourcing, or AI integration for KnowledgeOS -- these are labelled comparison questions to be resolved only against reconstructed EKS/PKS/AIP evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Those are excellent research candidates, but we must now label them: EXTERNAL RESEARCH CANDIDATE ↓ NOT YET ↓ KnowledgeOS kernel candidate
b_rows_sample.statement: Commentary pass proposes a mandatory classification-layer discipline when consuming the external research's 'Smallest Trustworthy Core' list: every candidate must be explicitly labelled EXTERNAL RESEARCH CANDIDATE -> NOT YET -> KnowledgeOS kernel candidate, because the source research itself says these must still be compared with EKS/PKS/AIP.

b_rows_sample.anchor: So now we have three evidence layers ... CURRENT SYSTEMS / EXTERNAL RESEARCH / INTERNAL HYPOTHESES ... CROSS-SYSTEM COMPARISON ↓ DDD VALIDATION ↓ KERNEL CANDIDATES ↓ HUMAN ARCHITECTURE DECISION
b_rows_sample.statement: Commentary pass proposes a three-evidence-layer investigation model (Current Systems=EKS/PKS/AIP; External Research=KMS/AKM/PROV/epistemic systems/organizational memory/temporal systems; Internal Hypotheses=brainstorming corpus) feeding a pipeline of Cross-System Comparison -> DDD Validation -> Kernel Candidates -> Human Architecture Decision, and recommends stopping broad external-research collection in favour of the comparison phase.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Which of these externally validated principles are already embodied in EKS, PKS, or AIP, which are missing, which are duplicated, and which would actually require a new KnowledgeOS kernel boundary?'
b_rows_sample.statement: The commentary pass reframes the driving research question from 'What should a KnowledgeOS kernel contain?' to 'Which of these externally validated principles are already embodied in EKS, PKS, or AIP, which are missing, which are duplicated, and which would actually require a new KnowledgeOS kernel boundary?' -- framed as the investigation that determines whether any kernel is a real extraction from the existing ecosystem rather than an invented new system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The term 'Knowledge Operating System' appears primarily in industry/marketing contexts ... a LinkedIn article (2026) describes a 'Knowledge Operating System' as treating organizational knowledge as governed infrastructure, compiling knowledge into a persistent wiki, versioned, auditable, access-controlled.
b_rows_sample.statement: Second-pass draft adds a dedicated 'Knowledge Operating System terminology' section (not present as a distinct section in pass 1): the term appears in a 2026 LinkedIn article describing a KOS as governed infrastructure compiled into a persistent, versioned, auditable, access-controlled wiki, but no peer-reviewed literature establishes 'Knowledge OS' as a canonical architecture pattern; related terms ('knowledge infrastructure', 'knowledge runtime', 'knowledge kernel') appear sporadically without established definitions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: They are not two independent architectural authorities. They overlap heavily: Research 1 + Research 2 ↓ External Research Corpus ↓ Research-supported hypotheses
b_rows_sample.statement: Final commentary pass instructs that the two research drafts must be treated as one combined external research corpus rather than two independent architectural authorities, since they overlap heavily and both ultimately conclude 'External research does not establish the KnowledgeOS kernel.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Given the external evidence corpus, what is the smallest set of semantic and mechanical primitives that must be universally trustworthy for an organizational knowledge system — and which of those primitives are actually demonstrated as cross-cutting concerns in EKS, PKS, and AIP? ... let EKS/PKS/AIP evidence eliminate candidates, not merely confirm the research.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final commentary pass proposes the next precise research question (given the external evidence corpus, what is the smallest set of universally-trustworthy primitives, and which are demonstrated cross-cutting in EKS/PKS/AIP) plus a draft comparison matrix (Candidate x External evidence x EKS x PKS x AIP x Cross-cutting? x Kernel candidate?) for Identity, Provenance, Temporal validity, Authority, Evidence, Decision, Lineage, Lifecycle, Conflict, Assurance -- and states the crucial methodological principle that EKS/PKS/AIP evidence should be used to ELIMINATE candidates, not merely confirm the external research, 'to give a defensible KnowledgeOS kernel rather than a kernel designed from literature alone.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not interpret DeepSeek's report as: 'We discovered the KnowledgeOS kernel.' I would interpret it as: 'We discovered that EKS, PKS and AIP already contain a recurring family of epistemic and governance invariants that are stronger than their current architectural boundaries suggest.'
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit reframing/caution: DeepSeek's report should not be read as 'we discovered the KnowledgeOS kernel' but as 'EKS, PKS, and AIP already contain a recurring family of epistemic and governance invariants stronger than their current architectural boundaries suggest' -- a more valuable, more modest finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EKS invariant ↓ PKS equivalent ↓ AIP equivalent ↓ same semantic invariant? ↓ same lifecycle? ↓ same ownership? ↓ independent of domain? ↓ reusable abstraction? ↓ KERNEL CANDIDATE ↓ DDD validation ↓ KERNEL DECISION. The report explicitly says this progression has not yet been executed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a next-step progression (an 'AMENDMENT-6 progression'): for each candidate, verify EKS invariant -> PKS equivalent -> AIP equivalent -> same semantic invariant? -> same lifecycle? -> same ownership? -> independent of domain? -> reusable abstraction? -> kernel candidate -> DDD validation -> kernel decision; explicitly states this progression has not yet been executed for any candidate, and recommends starting with C-1 (Authority-as-recorded-reference-to-a-human-act) as the strongest, since DeepSeek found essentially the same invariant explicitly represented across all three systems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Vāṇī as Research Lens (Not Kernel Law) ... Valid Contributions: Expression ≠ Meaning ... Invalid Contributions: Vāṇī as kernel principle: Not supported (external authority) ... Sacred authority model: Domain-specific, not universal
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit classification of the Vāṇī/oral-tradition source material: valid contributions are Expression≠Meaning, knowledge-transmission-across-media, the weaving metaphor (relationships, supported by graph/invariant research), and the authority question (supported by governance/provenance research); invalid contributions are Vāṇī as a kernel principle (not supported -- an external authority claim), a sacred-authority model (domain-specific, not universal), and Expression as a kernel dimension (not supported).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: the following research lenses have been analysed
a_rows_sample.statement: Full enumerated list of research lenses consumed by the study, explicitly framed as 'research lenses only.
