They are not automatically kernel laws': EKS/PKS/AIP archaeological evidence; Epistemic Control Systems; Knowledge lifecycle and snapshot models; TMS/AGM belief revision; Logic and inference theory; Nyaya Tarka Shastra reasoning; Vedanta epistemology; Jnana/Jneya/Jnata distinction; Vani (expression and transmission); Zero as neutral-state metaphor; Topological invariants; Sheaf/context composition; and six Navya-Nyaya sub-lenses: Abhava (structured absence), Avacchedaka (semantic delimitation), Hetvabhasa (reasoning fallacies), Coextension without identity, Intensional identity preservation, Type-theoretic interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expected Registered Invariants ... Identity Family ... Evidence Family ... Authority Family ... Transformation Family ... Temporal Family ... Reasoning Family ... Contradiction Family ... Agent Family
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 3 schema (ID|Invariant|Dimensions|Forbidden Collapse|Evidence|Strength|Validation Target|Notes/Boundary) plus the expected 8-family protect-statements: Identity (Representation != Identity: 'knowledge identity survives representation changes'; Expression != Meaning; Context Preservation: 'meaning requires semantic frame'); Evidence ('Observation != Interpretation', 'Evidence != Authority'); Authority ('Source authority is assigned, not intrinsic'); Transformation ('Knowledge evolution must preserve lineage'); Temporal ('Knowledge exists with temporal validity'); Reasoning ('Observation != Inference'; 'Inference requires preserved justification'); Contradiction ('Contradiction != Failure'; 'Conflicting knowledge may coexist'); Agent ('Knower identity is part of epistemic state').

a_rows_sample.anchor: Family 1 -- IDENTITY (What is this knowledge? -- identity conditions of meaning)
a_rows_sample.statement: Family 1 (IDENTITY) table: INV-KOS-002 Semantic Continuity (forbids Representation->Meaning); H-KOS-Context-001 Semantic Frame Preservation (forbids Context Removal->Meaning); H-KOS-Context-002 Avacchedaka (forbids Unbounded Claim->Over-extended Knowledge; compression ruling SUBSUMES SemanticBoundary-001, Ontology-001, Abhava Boundary-001 facet, and the type-model context-clause as facets of this one row); H-KOS-Relationship-001 Knowledge Relationship Integrity/Tripuji (forbids Known Object->Detached Autonomous Truth); H-KOS-Relation-001 Epistemic Relations as First-Class (forbids Relation->Attribute; compression ruling: the general principle UNDER the separation family, with INV-001..004 + Expression!=Meaning + Observation!=Inference as its instances).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Family 2 -- EVIDENCE (Why should we believe this?)
a_rows_sample.statement: Family 2 (EVIDENCE) table: INV-001 Evidence != Authority (ESTABLISHED); INV-KOS-Pramana-001 Means of Acquisition (forbids the 'Source-role collapse' -- flattening sensor=expert statement=AI inference=historical document; the designation ruling names the Pramana source-role separation AS this row's Forbidden-Collapse content, not a separate row); H-KOS-EvidenceAuthenticity-001 Evidence vs Pseudo-Evidence (forbids Pseudo-evidence->Evidence, anti-hallucination); H-ZERO-001 UNKNOWN is a Valid Epistemic State (forbids Unknown->False / Unknown->Missing, i.e. Unknown != Absent != False); H-KOS-Uncertainty-001 Structured Doubt/Samsaya (forbids Doubt->Missing data; compression ruling: a proposed H-KOS-Abhava-001 compresses INTO Uncertainty-001).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 83.67 — New invariants: I_TemporalTruth, I_EventTime, I_HistoricalIntegrity, I_TemporalAuthority, I_TemporalUncertainty, I_TemporalSupersession
a_rows_sample.statement: States six new named invariants: I_TemporalTruth (claims whose truth can change must have explicit temporal interpretation), I_EventTime (event/observation/processing times must remain distinguishable when materially relevant), I_HistoricalIntegrity (historical decisions must be interpreted using knowledge/models/policies/authorities valid at decision time), I_TemporalAuthority (authorization must be evaluated at time of action), I_TemporalUncertainty (unknown/interval timestamps must not be converted into false point precision), I_TemporalSupersession (superseded knowledge remains historically reconstructable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 82.72 — New invariants: I_UncertaintyPreservation, I_Dependence, I_ModelUncertainty, I_Calibration, I_EpistemicPrecision, I_DecisionSensitivity, I_UncertaintyImpact
a_rows_sample.statement: States seven new named invariants: I_UncertaintyPreservation (transformations must not silently discard material uncertainty), I_Dependence (dependencies between uncertain variables must be represented when material), I_ModelUncertainty (model-structure uncertainty must be distinguished from parameter uncertainty), I_Calibration (probabilistic claims should have defined semantics and empirical calibration where applicable), I_EpistemicPrecision (output precision must not misrepresent evidence quality), I_DecisionSensitivity (when uncertainty can change the selected action, sensitivity must remain visible), I_UncertaintyImpact (material upstream evidence changes must permit identification of affected downstream knowledge/decisions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 84.63 — New invariants: I_Intervention, I_CounterfactualProvenance, I_CounterfactualUncertainty, I_TemporalCausalSeparation, I_CounterfactualGovernance, I_Interference
a_rows_sample.statement: States six new named invariants: I_Intervention (observed association must not be represented as causal intervention without justification), I_CounterfactualProvenance (material counterfactual claims retain their model, evidence, and assumptions), I_CounterfactualUncertainty (counterfactual results preserve uncertainty and model sensitivity), I_TemporalCausalSeparation (observed historical outcomes must remain distinct from unobserved alternative outcomes), I_CounterfactualGovernance (causal feasibility of an intervention does not imply authorization to execute it), I_Interference (counterfactual analysis must account for material interactions between agents, components, or interventions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 85.77 — New strategic invariants: I_IncentiveAlignment, I_MetricIntegrity, I_StrategicRobustness, I_AuthorizationUnknown, I_GovernanceBoundary, I_MetaGovernance, I_IncentiveObservability
a_rows_sample.statement: States seven new strategic invariants: I_IncentiveAlignment (material incentives must not systematically reward behavior violating higher-level objectives), I_MetricIntegrity (governance metrics must not be equated with the underlying objective without justified relationship), I_StrategicRobustness (governance evaluation should consider adaptive/optimizing-against-mechanism behavior), I_AuthorizationUnknown (unknown authorization must not be interpreted as permission), I_GovernanceBoundary (material governance constraints must account for alternative execution paths), I_MetaGovernance (changes to governance mechanisms are themselves governed changes), I_IncentiveObservability (where strategic behavior is material, the system should model incentives and information as part of the behavioral model).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 87.75 — New invariants: I_Aggregation, I_AuthorityExpertise, I_CollectiveConstraint, I_Quorum, I_Delegation, I_HistoricalAggregation, I_RecommendationDecision, I_DecisionAuthorization
a_rows_sample.statement: States eight new invariants: I_Aggregation (every collective decision must use an explicitly defined aggregation mechanism), I_AuthorityExpertise (expertise, evidence quality, preference, and decision authority must not be conflated), I_CollectiveConstraint (collective preference cannot override higher-order mandatory constraints), I_Quorum (a decision requiring quorum must not become valid without sufficient authorized participation), I_Delegation (delegated authority cannot exceed the authority validly delegated by the delegator), I_HistoricalAggregation (historical decisions must be interpreted using the aggregation rules valid at decision time), I_RecommendationDecision (recommendation must not automatically become decision without required authority), I_DecisionAuthorization (a decision does not automatically grant execution authority unless the governance model explicitly defines that transition).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 86.83 — New invariants: I_Mechanism, I_IncentiveCompatibility, I_IndependentVerification, I_GovernanceSurface, I_StrategicRobustness2, I_MechanismVersioning, I_FeasibleActionSpace
a_rows_sample.statement: States seven new invariants: I_Mechanism (governance mechanisms must be evaluated by resulting behavior, not only formal rules), I_IncentiveCompatibility (where truthful/desired behavior is required, the mechanism must not create a systematic incentive to deviate), I_IndependentVerification (material claims should not depend exclusively on self-reported evidence when independent verification is feasible and material), I_GovernanceSurface (material alternative execution paths must be governed, restricted, or recognized as exception paths), I_StrategicRobustness2 (governance must be evaluated under plausible strategic responses, not only cooperative behavior), I_MechanismVersioning (changes to governance mechanisms must be versioned, authorized, and historically reconstructable), I_FeasibleActionSpace (optimization must occur within the set of constitutionally, governance, and authority-valid actions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 88.80 — New mathematical invariants: I_InformationPreservation, I_Sufficiency, I_CompressionProvenance, I_CompressionTime, I_CompressionUncertainty, I_NegativeKnowledge, I_RetrievalAssurance, I_DerivedReproducibility, I_RepresentationSeparation
a_rows_sample.statement: States nine new invariants: I_InformationPreservation (a transformation must preserve all information required for its declared assurance purpose), I_Sufficiency (a representation declared sufficient must specify the question, model, and assurance context), I_CompressionProvenance (compression must not destroy required provenance relationships), I_CompressionTime (material temporal semantics must survive representation changes), I_CompressionUncertainty (compression must not convert uncertainty into unjustified certainty), I_NegativeKnowledge (failure to retrieve evidence must not automatically imply falsity), I_RetrievalAssurance (evidence completeness requirements must be proportional to decision criticality), I_DerivedReproducibility (material derived knowledge should retain sufficient references to reproduce/audit its derivation), I_RepresentationSeparation (derived representations such as embeddings/summaries/indexes must remain distinguishable from authoritative evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 89.73 — New invariants: I_Decidability, I_ComputationalFeasibility, I_ProofScope, I_ModelReality, I_VerificationState, I_Approximation, I_ComputationProvenance, I_SafetyLiveness, I_GovernanceConsistency, I_ProofEstimation
a_rows_sample.statement: States ten new invariants: I_Decidability (distinguish undecidable from merely unknown), I_ComputationalFeasibility (infeasibility must not be represented as logical impossibility), I_ProofScope (verification claims must identify model, assumptions, scope), I_ModelReality (proof of a model property must not automatically be proof of the real-world property), I_VerificationState (verification must support True/False/Unknown), I_Approximation (approximate computation must remain distinguishable from exact), I_ComputationProvenance (material derived results must retain sufficient computational-derivation information for their assurance level), I_SafetyLiveness (governance verification must distinguish safety from liveness properties), I_GovernanceConsistency (mandatory governance rules must not contain unresolved logical contradictions), I_ProofEstimation (statistical/probabilistic support must not be represented as formal proof without explicit justification).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 90.73 — New invariants: I_Complexity, I_Incremental, I_CacheValidity, I_DecisionPrecision, I_GracefulDegradation, I_DistributedTime, I_Correlation, I_AssuranceOptimization, I_CriticalityBudget
a_rows_sample.statement: States nine new invariants: I_Complexity (material computational limits must be distinguishable from logical impossibility), I_Incremental (incremental recomputation must be semantically equivalent to required full recomputation under the declared model), I_CacheValidity (cached knowledge must retain the versions/validity conditions it depends on), I_DecisionPrecision (computational precision must be sufficient relative to the decision boundary and required assurance), I_GracefulDegradation (resource exhaustion must not silently convert incomplete computation into a definitive result), I_DistributedTime (observations from distributed sources must preserve their temporal semantics), I_Correlation (multiple computational outputs must not be treated as independent evidence when they share material dependencies), I_AssuranceOptimization (performance optimization must not silently reduce declared assurance), I_CriticalityBudget (computational resources and verification depth should be proportional to decision criticality where governance permits optimization).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 91.80 — New invariants: I_Refinement, I_Representation, I_Contract, I_Trace, I_MeaningTechnology, I_SpecSync, I_Composition, I_ExecutableInvariant, I_AssuranceProvenance
a_rows_sample.statement: States nine new invariants: I_Refinement (every implementation behavior affecting governed semantics must correspond to a permitted formal-model behavior), I_Representation (every concrete state exposed as valid must map to a valid abstract state), I_Contract (component implementations must satisfy declared preconditions/postconditions/invariants), I_Trace (observable implementation traces must remain within the permitted specification trace space), I_MeaningTechnology (implementation technology must not silently redefine domain semantics), I_SpecSync (material specification changes must trigger assessment of affected implementations), I_Composition (component-level correctness must not be promoted to system-level correctness without validating interaction contracts), I_ExecutableInvariant (where feasible, critical invariants should be represented as executable contracts/tests/enforcement), I_AssuranceProvenance (implementation-correctness claims must retain evidence of how they were established).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 92.79 — New invariants: I_AtomicInvariant, I_Concurrency, I_Conflict, I_Version, I_CausalOrder, I_Idempotency, I_AuthorizationFreshness, I_AuthorityUniqueness, I_DecisionSnapshot, I_GlobalInvariant, I_IrreversibleAction
a_rows_sample.statement: States eleven new invariants: I_AtomicInvariant (every atomic transition must preserve declared transaction-scope invariants), I_Concurrency (concurrent executions must not produce a state forbidden by the sequential spec), I_Conflict (unmergeable concurrent modifications must become explicit conflicts, not silent overwrites), I_Version (material writes must identify the state version validated against), I_CausalOrder (causal relationships must not be inferred solely from arrival order), I_Idempotency (idempotent operations must preserve semantic result under duplicate execution), I_AuthorizationFreshness (authorization decisions must satisfy freshness requirements per criticality), I_AuthorityUniqueness (distributed systems must prevent simultaneous conflicting authoritative states where exclusive authority is defined), I_DecisionSnapshot (material decisions must identify the evidence/policy/model/authority state used), I_GlobalInvariant (a multi-component invariant must be enforced at a boundary observing the combined state), I_IrreversibleAction (irreversible actions require assurance proportional to impact and rollback inability).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 93.75 — The strongest recovery invariant ... I_Recovery: for every supported failure mode F, recovery must either restore a valid state, or explicitly enter a declared degraded/unknown state. The system must never silently fabricate validity.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest recovery invariant I_Recovery: for every supported failure mode, recovery must restore a valid state or explicitly enter a declared degraded/unknown state — never silently fabricate validity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 93.78 — New invariants: I_AtomicRecovery, I_Durability, I_RecoveryValidity, I_FailureHistory, I_Reconciliation, I_RecoveryFreshness, I_RetrySafety, I_Compensation, I_FailureEpistemics, I_RecoveryAssurance
a_rows_sample.statement: States nine further new invariants: I_AtomicRecovery (failed atomic transitions must not leave semantically invalid committed states), I_Durability (a committed authoritative state must remain recoverable per its durability contract), I_RecoveryValidity (recovery must produce a valid state or explicitly degraded/unknown state), I_FailureHistory (recovery must not silently erase evidence of failure/partial execution/compensation), I_Reconciliation (recovered state must be reconciled with surviving authoritative state where divergence is possible), I_RecoveryFreshness (a recovered state must not be represented as current unless freshness is established), I_RetrySafety (retryable operations must have explicit duplicate-execution semantics), I_Compensation (compensation must remain distinguishable from perfect rollback and preserve residual effects), I_FailureEpistemics (observed failure, inferred cause, and unresolved cause must remain distinct knowledge states), I_RecoveryAssurance (recovery assurance must include correctness, completeness, freshness, and provenance appropriate to criticality).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 94.71 — New invariants: I_AuthorityIntegrity, I_AINonAuthority, I_TrustBoundary, I_AuthSeparation, I_LeastPrivilege, I_ProvenanceSecurity, I_IntegrityTruth, I_TemporalTrust, I_AdversarialEvidence, I_SeparationOfDuties, I_MultiPartyAuthorization, I_SecurityEvidence
a_rows_sample.statement: States twelve new security invariants: I_AuthorityIntegrity (authority must originate from an authorized governance mechanism, not an untrusted claim), I_AINonAuthority (AI-generated statements must not acquire authoritative status solely through generation), I_TrustBoundary (crossing a trust boundary must not automatically increase authority/trust level), I_AuthSeparation (identity verification must remain distinct from permission verification), I_LeastPrivilege (actors must possess no more capability than required), I_ProvenanceSecurity (material claims must retain sufficient provenance to distinguish authoritative/verified/unverified/untrusted origins), I_IntegrityTruth (integrity verification must not be represented as proof of semantic truth), I_TemporalTrust (trust/identity/authority/credentials must be evaluated within their applicable time interval), I_AdversarialEvidence (evidence exposed to material adversarial manipulation must carry a trust/risk assessment), I_SeparationOfDuties (no single actor may perform mutually exclusive roles in the same decision process where required), I_MultiPartyAuthorization (actions requiring multiple authorities must not execute until all required independent authorizations are established), I_SecurityEvidence (material security events must remain observable and attributable so they can become auditable evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 95.69 — Privacy as a mathematical invariant ... I_Privacy: for every actor, purpose, time, and context, the information accessible through the system must remain within the authorized information boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the core privacy invariant I_Privacy: accessible information must remain within the authorized information boundary for every actor/purpose/time/context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 95.75 — New invariants: I_InformationAuthorization, I_PurposeLimitation, I_DataMinimization, I_InformationFlow, I_DerivedProtection, I_AuthorizedRetrieval, I_PrivacyComposition, I_TemporalPrivacy, I_DeletionPropagation, I_AuditPrivacy, I_AIContextBoundary
a_rows_sample.statement: States eleven further new invariants: I_InformationAuthorization (permission to act must not automatically imply permission to access all relevant information), I_PurposeLimitation (knowledge access must respect the declared/authorized purpose), I_DataMinimization (only information necessary for the purpose should be exposed where practicable), I_InformationFlow (restricted information must not flow into less-protected representations without authorized transformation), I_DerivedProtection (derived knowledge/summaries/embeddings/predictions/AI outputs remain subject to applicable information controls), I_AuthorizedRetrieval (access policy should constrain retrieval, not merely final presentation, wherever feasible), I_PrivacyComposition (repeated disclosures must be evaluated collectively), I_TemporalPrivacy (information authorization/classification must remain valid for the applicable time interval), I_DeletionPropagation (material deletion requirements must evaluate derived representations/downstream artifacts), I_AuditPrivacy (conflicts between audit retention and privacy requirements must be explicitly governed, not silently resolved), I_AIContextBoundary (an AI agent must receive only knowledge within its authorized epistemic boundary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 94 established Security = Preservation of invariants under adversarial behavior. But security alone is not enough. Permission to Act ≠ Permission to Know.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the foundational Step 95 distinction Permission to Act ≠ Permission to Know: an authenticated/authorized actor may still be forbidden from seeing particular knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.1 — Action authorization versus information authorization ... CanAct(A,x), CanKnow(A,k). No mathematical reason that CanAct(A,x) ⇒ CanKnow(A,k). Experiment 1: manager authorized to Approve(Request) but not to see EmployeeSalaryDetails. Expected: CanAct=True, CanKnow=False. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines CanAct(A,x) and CanKnow(A,k) and confirms via Experiment 1 (a manager who can Approve but cannot see EmployeeSalaryDetails) that CanAct(A,x) does not imply CanKnow(A,k); result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.2 — KnowledgeOS therefore needs an information-access model ... Access(A,K,C) where A=actor, K=knowledge, C=context. Access=True only if the applicable information policy permits it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the information-access model Access(A,K,C) over actor, knowledge, and context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.3 — Experiment 2 ... Actor is authenticated with role Developer. Knowledge object contains confidential HR information. Expected: authentication alone does not grant access. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: an authenticated Developer role does not automatically grant access to confidential HR information; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.4 — Classification of knowledge ... Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. AccessPolicy(K) must be explicit.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a knowledge classification scheme (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) requiring an explicit AccessPolicy(K).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.5 — Experiment 3 ... K=Restricted. Actor clearance: Internal. Expected: Access=False. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: an Internal-clearance actor is denied access to Restricted knowledge; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.6 — But classification alone is insufficient ... K=Internal. Actor is also Internal. That does not necessarily imply access. There may be Purpose, Domain, Role, NeedToKnow constraints.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues matching classification alone (Internal knowledge, Internal actor) does not necessarily imply access; Purpose, Domain, Role, and NeedToKnow may also constrain it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.7 — Need-to-know ... Need(A,K,Q) where Q is the purpose. Access might require AuthorizedRole(A) ∧ Need(A,K,Q) ∧ PermittedPurpose(Q).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines need-to-know Need(A,K,Q) and a combined access condition AuthorizedRole(A) ∧ Need(A,K,Q) ∧ PermittedPurpose(Q).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.8 — Experiment 4 ... Developer authorized for architecture documents for EngineeringPurpose. Developer requests employee medical information for the same project. Expected: purpose does not justify access. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: an engineering-purpose authorization does not justify accessing unrelated employee medical information; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.9 — Purpose limitation ... Access=f(Identity,Role,Classification,Purpose,Need,Context,Time). Significantly stronger than Access=f(Role).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the full access function Access=f(Identity,Role,Classification,Purpose,Need,Context,Time), far stronger than a role-only Access=f(Role).

type_signature.domain: Identity x Role x Classification x Purpose x Need x Context x Time

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.10 — Temporal access ... Auth(A,K,t). Auth(A,K,t1)=True does not imply Auth(A,K,t2)=True.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines temporal access Auth(A,K,t): validity at t1 does not imply validity at t2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.11 — Experiment 5 ... Employee has access until 2026-08-31. At 2026-09-01, the access is revoked. Expected: Access=False. Result: PASS. Again, time is part of semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: employee access revoked as of 2026-09-01 must yield Access=False thereafter; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.12 — Data minimization ... an agent needs only AgeRange for a decision. Providing FullDateOfBirth creates unnecessary information exposure. Provide the minimum information necessary for the declared purpose.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the data minimization principle: provide only the minimum information necessary for the declared purpose (e.g. AgeRange, not FullDateOfBirth).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.13 — Experiment 6 ... Decision requires Age≥18. System provides DateOfBirth=1987-04-12. Expected: if the exact date is unnecessary, this exposes more information than required. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: providing an exact date of birth when only Age≥18 is required over-exposes information; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.14 — Derived information can also be sensitive ... the system hides Salary but provides SalaryBand where the band is sufficiently narrow to reveal the salary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates derived-information leakage: a sufficiently narrow SalaryBand can reveal the hidden raw Salary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.15 — Experiment 7 ... Raw value hidden. Derived statistic uniquely determines the raw value. Expected: PrivacyLeak. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: a derived statistic that uniquely determines a hidden raw value is PrivacyLeak; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.16 — Inference attacks ... An actor may infer K from K_1,...,K_n. K_1,...,K_n ⇒ K-hat.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines inference attacks: composing multiple non-sensitive pieces of knowledge (K_1..K_n) to infer sensitive K̂.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.17 — Experiment 8 ... System never exposes 'Employee X is being investigated.' But exposes unusual access logs, investigation workflow state, restricted project assignment. Actor infers Investigation(X)=True. Expected: potential inference leakage. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: indirect signals (access logs, workflow state, project assignment) letting an actor infer an undisclosed investigation is potential inference leakage; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.18 — Privacy is therefore a property of information flow ... InformationFlow: K_source→K_derived→Actor. Not merely Database→Actor.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes privacy as a property of information flow K_source→K_derived→Actor, not the simplistic Database→Actor.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 95.19 — Information-flow policy ... Label(K) as confidentiality classification. Flow(K_1,K_2) only if PermittedFlow(Label(K_1),Label(K_2)).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines information-flow policy: Flow(K_1,K_2) requires PermittedFlow(Label(K_1),Label(K_2)).

a_rows_sample.statement: The 11-law Adopted Constitutional Core (P5's validated recommendation, NOT adopted law here): 1 Identity Law; 2 Dimension Law; 3 Authority Law; 4 Decision Law; 5 Projection Law; 6 Verification Law; 7 Failure-state Law; 8 Contradiction Law; 9 Unknown Law; 10 Agency Law; 11 History Law -- each independently failure-tested (removing it opens a distinct, named corruption not covered by any other law's removal-test); the 4 Established rows appear unchanged as the spine of laws 3-5; the 22 surviving candidate rows render into the 11 laws without loss of content.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Selected kernel law (final wording) ... Failure signature (if removed)
a_rows_sample.statement: The 11 laws given final selected wording with their rendered rows and failure signatures, reproduced from the P5 Decision Matrix (Identity Law renders INV-KOS-002+Context-001+Context-002+Relationship-001+Relation-001; Dimension Law renders INV-KOS-001+NonInterference-001 with NonInterference merged per Decision 2a; Authority Law renders INV-001+INV-003+Pramana-001; Decision Law renders INV-002+Decision-001; Projection Law renders INV-004; Verification Law renders Inference-001+Justification-001+Reasoning-Separation-001+Reasoning-Provenance-001+Vyapti-001+EvidenceAuthenticity-001+Pramana-001; Failure-State Law renders Fallacy-001(state)+Failure-001; Contradiction Law renders Contradiction-001+Dialogue-001(boundary); Unknown Law renders H-ZERO-001+Uncertainty-001+Abhava(requirement); Agency Law renders Agent-001+Relationship-001(knower-side); History Law renders Revisability-001+Temporal family). a_rows_sample.anchor: NonInterference -> Dimension Law (law 2): Epistemic dimensions evolve independently. No value passes from one dimension to another without an explicit, governed transition; no dimension collapses into another (no single-score knowledge).
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision 2a: the P4 SS3.9 OVERLAPPING ruling (deferred to P5) is resolved -- H-KOS-NonInterference-001 is the transition-form of INV-KOS-001 (Dimension Independence); they render as one law with final frozen wording. Rows rendered: INV-KOS-001, H-KOS-NonInterference-001; the 'no implicit transition' clause is NonInterference's content, now stated inside the law -- no separate row, no lost content.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Article 2 -- Dimension: 1. ... independent epistemic dimensions ... 2. No value SHALL pass from one dimension to another without an explicit, governed transition ... 3. no single score SHALL replace epistemic structure
a_rows_sample.statement: Article 2 (Dimension), 3 clauses: knowledge SHALL evolve along independent epistemic dimensions; no value SHALL pass between dimensions without an explicit, governed transition; no dimension SHALL collapse into another -- 'a knowledge quality scalar is a forbidden surrogate.' Renders INV-KOS-001, H-KOS-NonInterference-001. Failure if removed: Knowledge Quality = 0.87; silent cross-dimension interference.

b_rows_sample.statement: Article 4 (Decision), 2 clauses: observation/knowledge SHALL NOT constitute decision; knowledge SHALL inform action, SHALL NOT execute it -- the knowledge/decision boundary SHALL be governed, never implicit. a_rows_sample.anchor: Article 6 -- Verification: 1. No claim SHALL enter knowledge without a preserved justification path ... 3. Generation SHALL NOT be justification. ... 5. Observation SHALL NOT become inference; AI output SHALL NOT become reality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Article 6 (Verification), 5 clauses (the densest article): no claim SHALL enter knowledge without a preserved justification path (authentic evidence + acquisition method + inference rule + reasoning path); pseudo-evidence SHALL NOT be evidence; generation SHALL NOT be justification (an AI output/model response/generated conclusion SHALL be a candidate, never knowledge by generation alone); reasoning SHALL be a governed transformation, never a black box, and evidence SHALL NOT become a conclusion without a preserved inference rule; observation SHALL NOT become inference, AI output SHALL NOT become reality. Renders Inference-001, Justification-001, Reasoning-Separation-001, Reasoning-Provenance-001, Vyapti-001, EvidenceAuthenticity-001, Pramana-001. Failure if removed: AI output=reality; unsupported claim=knowledge; black-box generation; opaque inference; hallucination=evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pi_value_set was declared to read the value field. Under T_D_relational its value is computed from rank, and rank is produced by ordering values within a tag group -- so the observable was in fact carried by tag, the very field Q reads. It did not know this. Neither did I, and I wrote it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a KR-BRIDGE-02 (Pi x Q grid) finding that the observable Pi_value_set, declared to read only the value field, actually derives its value under transformation T_D_relational from a rank computed by ordering values within a tag group -- so it was in fact carried by the tag field, the very field the inquiry Q reads, an undetected coupling that violates the target/observable-independence discipline established for the bridge experiments.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the corrected map was still wrong: Pi_arity reads no field by declaration, and after T_C_dedup it reads v -- because arity is a function of which records survive, and membership is decided by a field. A perturbation test found this; reading the code did not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a second, subtler provenance error even after the first was corrected: Pi_arity, declared to read no field, actually reads the v field after transformation T_C_dedup because arity depends on which records survive deduplication and survival is decided by that field, a coupling found only by a perturbation test (changing one input field and observing which outputs move) and not by reading the implementation code.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The structural point, stripped of its soteriology: the agent's account of its own activity is not the activity. Pi reports {v}. Pi is in fact carried by {v, tag}. Its self-description is sincere and wrong, and its wrongness is not visible from inside itself -- it is visible only from the transformat
a_rows_sample.statement: Reads Gita 3.27 as corroborating the shape of the KR-BRIDGE-02 failure: an observable's declared self-description (Pi reports {v}) can be sincere yet wrong (Pi is actually carried by {v,tag}), and this wrongness is not visible from inside the declaration itself, only from the transformation that actually constitutes the observable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: gahana karmano gatih -- 4.17 -- 'the way of action is deep / impenetrable.' Not mysticism here: dependency structure is not surface-readable. Two of my three provenance maps were wrong, and I was reading the code that produced them each time.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reads Gita 4.17 ('the way of action is deep/impenetrable') non-mystically as corroborating that dependency structure is not surface-readable: two of three declared provenance maps in this cycle were wrong despite reading the very code that produced them each time.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Effective-read closure: an observable's read-set must be computed through the transformation's provenance, never declared. [PROP] FR-003 -- but established by experiment (KR-BRIDGE-02), not by the lens. ... Declaration != verification as a standing experimental obligation [PROP]. Two independent occ
a_rows_sample.statement: Registers candidate FR-003 (effective-read closure: an observable's read-set must be computed through the transformation's actual provenance, never taken from its declaration), established by the KR-BRIDGE-02 experiment itself with the lens only naming it after the fact; registers 'declaration != verification' as a standing experimental obligation [PROP] with two independent occurrences now (KR-BRIDGE-01's T_B label mismatch and KR-BRIDGE-02's provenance failures), explicitly noting two occurrences is not promotion per ES-006.1; and rejects both non-doership as a kernel stance (no mechanical content) and 'action's depth' as an argument for interpretive humility in the kernel (legitimate only as a reason to test, which is already an obligation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We have experimentally separated three things that we previously tended to mix together: information elimination, preservation of a business inquiry, and successful realization by a decoder. Eliminability != Preservation != Realization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the three-way separation of Eliminability, Preservation, and Realization as the strongest result of the KR-REP-REDUCTION/KR-ZERO assessment, restating the formal three questions (can the business question be answered: H(Q|R)=0; can something be eliminated: Zero_{T,Pi}; can the decoder recover the answer: O(R)=Q(D)).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every future mathematical statement in KnowledgeOS must carry its epistemic status: Definition, Theorem, Corollary, Empirical Result, Proposition, Conjecture, Refuted, or Open. That is what will allow us to turn this from an interesting research program into a genuinely rigorous mathematical theory
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes making it a permanent methodological rule that every future KnowledgeOS mathematical statement carry an explicit epistemic-status tag (Definition, Theorem, Corollary, Empirical Result, Proposition, Conjecture, Refuted, or Open), to prevent accidentally promoting an experiment into a theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The original read-disjointness gate was unsound. It checked declared source-field reads, but transformations can derive output fields from other fields. The corrected gate has to operate on the actual transformed representation and be verified empirically.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that KR-BRIDGE-02 discovered its own original read-disjointness gate was unsound because it checked declared source-field reads while transformations can derive output fields from other fields (matching the Pi_value_set/tag coupling found in the companion Gita study), requiring the corrected gate to operate on the actual transformed representation and be verified empirically rather than by declaration.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The first adjudication criterion was wrong. Marginal RD simply rediscovered the redundancy confounding already identified in BRIDGE-01. A conditional bridge has to survive within redundancy strata, using the Mantel-Haenszel risk difference.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that KR-BRIDGE-02's first adjudication criterion (marginal risk difference) was wrong because it simply rediscovered the redundancy confounding already identified in BRIDGE-01, requiring instead that a conditional bridge survive within redundancy strata using the Mantel-Haenszel risk difference.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No admissible (Pi,Q,T) produced a substantive within-stratum Zero-preservation relationship replicated on both train and test. ... the document does not establish a universal 'no-bridge law.' Only 31 of 112 cells were actually searched after the increasingly strict gate and informativeness requireme
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the KR-BRIDGE-02 headline finding after both corrections: no admissible (Pi,Q,T) configuration produced a substantive within-stratum Zero-preservation relationship replicated on both train and test, but this is explicitly not a universal 'no-bridge law' since only 31 of 112 candidate cells were actually searched after applying the increasingly strict gate and informativeness requirements, scoping the negative result to the tested region only.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pi-family size != mechanism count. After deduplication, value multiset, value set, and arity become mutually determined, so several apparently different Pi observations are actually the same mechanism under that transformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new methodological finding to preserve in the theory: Pi-family size does not equal mechanism count -- after a deduplication transformation, the observables value-multiset, value-set, and arity become mutually determined, so several apparently distinct Pi observations collapse into the same underlying mechanism under that transformation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The governance status is exactly right: experiment + audit, not yet adjudicated theory. The document explicitly keeps Theory v1.2 frozen and says nothing here has yet been promoted into Theory v1.3.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms KR-BRIDGE-02's governance status as experiment plus audit, not yet adjudicated theory, with Theory v1.2 remaining frozen and nothing promoted to Theory v1.3.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would treat BRIDGE-02 as a significant methodological strengthening of the research program, especially because the experiment caught its own measurement/gating assumptions twice rather than merely producing another numerical result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Judges KR-BRIDGE-02 a significant methodological strengthening of the research program precisely because it caught its own measurement/gating assumptions wrong twice (the read-disjointness gate and the marginal-RD adjudication criterion) rather than merely producing another numerical result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BRIDGE-02 was designed specifically to attack the remaining Pi/Q gap identified here, while also discovering that the original read-disjointness gate itself was insufficient. So the sequence is now clear: KR-ZERO -> KR-REP-REDUCTION -> BRIDGE-01 -> BRIDGE-02, with the governance rule still: Experime
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the now-clear overall research sequence KR-ZERO -> KR-REP-REDUCTION -> BRIDGE-01 -> BRIDGE-02, with BRIDGE-02 having been designed specifically to attack the remaining Pi/Q gap left by BRIDGE-01, under the unchanged governance rule Experiment -> Audit -> Adjudication -> Theory v1.3 and Theory v1.2 remaining frozen.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not predict Preservation
a_rows_sample.statement: Four experiments of increasing power (H-RR2 boundary-crossing Zero rate 0.0377 vs 0.0426; KR-BRIDGE-01 marginal RD=-0.363 fully explained by redundancy confounding; KR-BRIDGE-02 H1 not refuted; KR-BRIDGE-03 at 13x informative strata, H1 still not refuted, surviving cells 14->1) converge on the same negative finding, stable under a 13-fold power increase.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
a_rows_sample.statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No Zero/preservation bridge exists for read-disjoint (Π, Q).
a_rows_sample.statement: Standing conjecture with an explicit refutation condition (one substantive, replicating, gate-clean cell with |MH-RD|>=0.01 on both splits); stated so it can be attacked rather than hardening into an assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Read-disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T) and verified empirically.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-003, CANDIDATE this cycle, established by KR-BRIDGE-02 §2 catching a false positive (MH-RD=-0.155, replicating) that a hand-inspected provenance map (wrong twice) would otherwise have let through; needs a second independent adopter before promotion per ES-006.1.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero predicts preservation [NEG] — 4 independent tests
a_rows_sample.statement: Refuted claims about the bridge: Zero does not predict preservation (4 independent tests), Zero does not mark the reduction boundary, admissibility is a property of (Pi,Q,T) not (Pi,Q), read-disjointness cannot be established by declaration, and neither flattening the redundancy distribution nor raising population size increases informative strata.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The one substantial effect in the entire grid was an artifact of shared reads.
a_rows_sample.statement: KR-BRIDGE-02's instrument failed twice before reporting anything: first a marginal-RD adjudication falsely reported 'H2 SUPPORTED, 27/27 replicate' (re-finding the known confounder), then a naive read-disjointness gate let through an inadmissible cell (MH-RD=-0.155, replicating) caused by rank=f(value,tag) leaking into Pi; a second, corrected gate was itself found unsound by perturbation testing (Pi_arity effectively reading value via dedup survivorship), yielding the rule 'admissibility is a property of the TRIPLE (Pi,Q,T), never of the pair' and 'declaration is not verification.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability, Preservation and Realization are three distinct questions. None implies another.
b_rows_sample.statement: The load-bearing result of the Theory 00-14 programme: Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))) [Zero/eliminability], Hhat(Q|T(D))=0 [Adequacy/preservation] and O(T(D))=Q(D) [Realization] are shown to differ in every system tested, by independent mechanisms; tagged [EXP] deliberately rather than [THM] because necessity of the separation in general is unproven.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not predict Preservation
b_rows_sample.statement: Four experiments of increasing power (H-RR2 boundary-crossing Zero rate 0.0377 vs 0.0426; KR-BRIDGE-01 marginal RD=-0.363 fully explained by redundancy confounding; KR-BRIDGE-02 H1 not refuted; KR-BRIDGE-03 at 13x informative strata, H1 still not refuted, surviving cells 14->1) converge on the same negative finding, stable under a 13-fold power increase.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preservation does not give Realization
b_rows_sample.statement: Hhat(Q|R5)=0 (adequate) is a separate fact from O(R5)=Q(D) (realized): a fixed decoder can fail on information-theoretically adequate data because it was fixed in advance and not refit; flagged as a design defect that the KR-REP-REDUCTION chain never operationalized this separation (no dropped record/source ever made constraint C fail), so 'the separation is real; that experiment could not exhibit it.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not give Realization
b_rows_sample.statement: Not derivable merely from the other two separations (explicitly not a corollary): Zero is defined via Pi, which is read-disjoint from Q by construction, so it carries no information about Q's recoverability 'by design' — verified rather than assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Realization ⟹ Adequacy
b_rows_sample.statement: Standing conjecture that if a fixed decoder recovers Q from R on every observed case, R determines Q on the realized cases; refutable by a decoder that is right by luck (correct on every observed case while the fiber is Q-heterogeneous); explicitly 'not tested.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do the separations survive a non-synthetic carrier?
b_rows_sample.statement: Flagged as the central transfer problem: whether eliminability/preservation/realization separations generalize beyond the tested synthetic carrier is explicitly open.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The estimand for any bridge claim is the within-stratum effect.
b_rows_sample.statement: The programme's central methodological error was estimating the wrong quantity competently — the marginal P(A|Z)-P(A|not Z) was already known to be confounded before KR-BRIDGE-02 ran; re-estimating it produced a false 'H2 SUPPORTED'; the correct estimand is the Mantel-Haenszel within-stratum effect.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A stratum is informative iff (a_k+b_k)>0 ∧ (c_k+d_k)>0 ∧ (a_k+c_k)>0 ∧ (b_k+d_k)>0
b_rows_sample.statement: Both Zero and non-Zero must occur and both Adequate and Inadequate must occur for a stratum to be informative; strata at deterministic extremes contribute nothing, explaining why flattening the redundancy distribution failed (balance is not power) and why choosing a finer stratification variable (multiplicity partition, then partition x |S|) gave 13x the informative strata.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sign agreement alone is not replication.
b_rows_sample.statement: Under a sign-only replication rule, 14 cells 'replicated' with |RD|~0.001 and 12 of 14 had no stratum CI excluding zero; all 14 collapsed at higher power. Replication requires sign agreement AND clearing a substantive floor on both splits AND at least one stratum's 95% CI excluding zero; per-stratum RDs must be reported, not only the pooled MH estimate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If the floor is declared after first inspection, record that fact in the artifact
b_rows_sample.statement: Effect-size floors must be declared and used as a reporting tier rather than a filter (publish every surviving cell at both tiers) since at n~10^5 statistical significance is not evidence of anything; a post-inspection floor must be disclosed as such.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bootstrap CI on Ĥ ... [DEFECT] invalid here
b_rows_sample.statement: Estimator hygiene register: N_viol is exact and bias-free (authoritative for combinatorial adequacy questions), the Miller-Madow correction is used for Hhat, Haldane+0.5/Woolf CI is used for sparse odds-ratio tables, and bootstrap CI on Hhat is invalid because resampling duplicates cases and depresses conditional entropy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaves as a common cause of Zero occurrence and of inadequacy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Standard formalized here: never state a regime-specific empirical finding as a general causal law; a single-mechanism explanation of the KR-BRIDGE-01 confound was itself withdrawn once the Zero-count was found constant at r=1 but varying at r=2, showing the exact RD=0 had two different causes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Power is a property of the informative region, not of n.
b_rows_sample.statement: Measured across four candidate power levers: population size (no effect, 73/74/70 across n=1500/4000/8000) and flattening the confounder distribution (73->75, no effect) both do nothing, while record count (73->233) and finer stratification variable (~30->388) are the effective levers; when power stops responding to sampling, the constraint has moved into the design (the 67 dead cells are invariant across nine generator regimes because the adequacy definition itself saturates).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Everything in this set is built from six objects and one operator.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theory 01 fixes the six-object signature of the KnowledgeOS transformation carrier: D (data, a finite multiset of records), T (transformation D->R), R=T(D) (representation), Q (inquiry D->Y), Pi (observable R->O), O (decoder R->Y), and C (constraint predicate on R), plus the inquiry frame Pi_frame=(Q,C,O) with O fixed in advance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a record r = (value, source, tag, timestamp)
b_rows_sample.statement: A record in the tested carriers is r=(value,source,tag,timestamp), optionally a derived rank; explicitly flagged as an experimental carrier, not declared to be the mathematical carrier of KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Set subtraction D \ S is INVALID wherever a field is relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: The elimination operator E_S must be typed to the level it acts at and must recompute relative fields (e.g. within-group rank) after removing S; naive set subtraction D\S leaves stale relative values and produces a representation the level's own rules forbid.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is indexed by (T,Π) and by the subset S; adequacy by (T,Q) and the population; realization by (T,Q,O) and the case.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero, Adequacy and Realization are defined with different index sets and are not three readings of one quantity: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) <=> Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))); Adequate(T,Q) <=> Hhat(Q|T(D))=0; Realized(T,Q,O) <=> O(T(D))=Q(D).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
b_rows_sample.statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier.
b_rows_sample.statement: Every experiment used a deliberately small numerical carrier (|D|<=6) so fibers would collide and adequacy would be measurable; this is a calibration choice, not an ontological one, and the move to documents/claims/entities/relations/provenance/contradictions/temporal states/evidence is the open research problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A transformation family is either sequential (Rk+1 = Tk(Rk)) or parallel (Rk = Tk(D)) — never silently mixed
b_rows_sample.statement: Sequential vs parallel transformation families is a permanent type-discipline rule, load-bearing because the data-processing inequality (document 04) applies to sequential families and not to parallel ones.
