a_rows_sample.anchor: NextEpistemicAct(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,Pi) ... a_t in {Clarify, Search, Observe, ConsultResource, AssessEvidence, Determine, Defer, Act}. ... EA1..EA7
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a four-layer Epistemic Agency Execution Loop (front-end interaction; gap detection & classification via K_t|=Q; epistemic agency selection via a*=argmax[ExpectedGapReduction/(Cost+Risk)]; determination & output) and seven hypotheses EA1-EA7: EA1 observation!=interpretation; EA2 intent as unconfirmed hypothesis; EA3 typed gap resolution over {Semantic,Epistemic,...}; EA4 epistemic action optimization a*=argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost]; EA5 resource-bounded actions A_t=Filter(A,Resources_t); EA6 Lord/Sarathi duality (generate vs select); EA7 Determine(Evidence) before Act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t |= Q ... This notation is dangerous. ... Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) ... or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) ... should not become a new KnowledgeOS primitive. Use the existing vocabulary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the dangerous overloading of logical entailment notation K_t|=Q (which normally means semantic entailment, much stronger than intended) to the existing Adequacy/Determination vocabulary Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R), so as not to introduce a redundant new primitive, consistent with the established Determination!=Knowledge and Adequacy!=Determination!=Knowledge distinctions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_t in {Semantic, Epistemic, Resource, Policy} ... I would not call these the four gap types yet ... ClassifyGap: Delta_Q -> G where G is itself still research-open.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects freezing the four-way gap taxonomy {Semantic,Epistemic,Resource,Policy} as exhaustive; recommends Delta_Q(K_t) as a typed collection of unsatisfied requirements with a ClassifyGap:Delta_Q->G mapping where G remains research-open, illustrated by four metro-scenario gap readings (inquiry gap, knowledge gap, resource gap, decision/policy gap).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gap -> Opportunity -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution ... Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action. That distinction should remain intact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates four conflated concerns in the original design (what is missing, what can be done, what should be done, what is allowed) into an explicit chain Delta_t -> A_t^possible -> A_t^feasible -> a_t* -> Authorization(a_t*) -> Execute(a_t*), preserving the existing Proposal!=Decision!=Authorization!=Action distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a_t^* = argmax_{a in A_t^feasible} EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) ... KnowledgeOS should not assume that epistemic information gain is always the objective.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA4's argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost] formula as an insufficient decision rule (pure info-gain/cost could select an unsafe action, and sometimes not acting is optimal), generalizing to a_t*=argmax EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) without freezing the exact utility formula, and abstracting the capability as NextEpistemicAct:(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,C_t,EC_t)->A_t to be determined experimentally.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Resource_t(r) = (Avail,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...) ... Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) becomes meaningful.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA5's simple Filter(A,Resources_t) model to a richer per-resource state Resource_t(r)=(Availability,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...), making Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) meaningful and connecting to the existing evidence-channel work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: unless your actual observation included a specified probability model, that inequality is not established. Likewise "maintaining eye contact" was not part of the original factual description. ... Never move directly O -> P(H) without specifying the inference model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags that the worked human trace contains invented (unobserved) details treated as facts (e.g. an unstated probability inequality, 'maintaining eye contact', 'language barrier'), violating the very Observation!=Interpretation discipline KnowledgeOS is meant to enforce; recommends explicitly labeling O(observed)/I(interpretation)/H(hypothesis)/P(probability output) and never moving directly from O to P(H) without a specified inference model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q_0 -> Clarification -> Q_1 -> Clarification -> Q_2 ... until WellFormed(Q_n,C) and only then Gap(Q_n,K_t). ... Inquiry Formation ... distinct from Inquiry Resolution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the pipeline with a multi-cycle Inquiry Formation stage (Q0->Clarification->Q1->...->WellFormed(Q_n,C)) preceding gap analysis, explicitly distinguished from Inquiry Resolution; illustrated by the metro example needing a follow-up clarifying question ('Where are you going?') before the direction question is answerable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Determine(Evidence) BEFORE Act. ... I would not make this universal. ... Required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA7 (universal Determine-before-Act) by distinguishing three action classes (epistemic actions like search/inspect/ask which may precede determination; operational actions requiring determination+authorization; safety/emergency actions taken under uncertainty), giving the conditional rule 'required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination', preserving Epistemic Decision != Operational Decision != Authorization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a metaphor can expose a structure without proving that the metaphor names an architectural component. ... [PROP] Lord/Sarathi is an interpretive naming lens for the two functions; not a canonical architectural name.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demotes EA6's Lord/Sarathi naming to CandidateGenerator(K_t,Delta_t,R_t)->A_t and ActionSelector(K_t,Delta_t,A_t,C_t,EC_t)->a_t, tagging Lord/Sarathi as merely [PROP] interpretive naming, invoking the prior Gita governance lesson that a metaphor can expose a structure without naming an architectural component.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract? ... A new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required capability absent from the current model, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the kernel question from 'should Epistemic Agency become a kernel operator' to 'does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract', restating the standing rule that a new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required absent capability, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation equivalence not-implies Intent equivalence ... Good action selection not-implies Correct knowledge ... Resource availability not-implies Resource reliability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a controlled factorial benchmark (fixed K_t,Q,Delta while varying resources R_t across cases A-D, then epistemic standards/risk/inquiry across cases E-G, expecting A*_A!=A*_B!=A*_C!=A*_D when resources materially differ) plus two adversarial experiments: a 'wrong assumption' test with four worlds sharing an identical observation but different underlying intent, giving Observation equivalence does not imply Intent equivalence; and a 'wrong resource' test where good action selection leads to a wrong search result, giving Good action selection does not imply Correct knowledge and Resource availability does not imply Resource reliability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a) = E[U_gap(a)] - C_resource(a) - Omega_risk(a) + U_task(a) ... the additive form is not theoretically established. ... EU = F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task) as the general specification, and treat the additive version as [PROP] EU_additive.
a_rows_sample.statement: The draft's additive four-term utility decomposition EU(a)=E[U_gap(a)]-C_resource(a)-Omega_risk(a)+U_task(a) is corrected to a general (unestablished-form) specification EU=F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task), with the additive version relegated to [PROP] EU_additive pending experimental validation, since e.g. risk may interact with epistemic benefit rather than subtract independently.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ||Delta_Q(K_t)||_G ... This is currently underdefined ... These don't naturally form a vector space. ... U_gap(a) = V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a; Q,C,EC,S) where V is a candidate gap-value/reduction function.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects assuming a generic norm ||Delta||_G over the gap space, since typed gaps (missing value, missing dimension, contradiction, insufficient evidence, unobservable quantity, underdetermination, model insufficiency, semantic ambiguity) do not naturally form a vector space; replaces it with a general candidate gap-value/reduction function U_gap(a)=V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a;Q,C,EC,S), with an actual metric d(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}) introduced only if experiments establish a numerical structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reduction != Validation != Determination != Knowledge ... U_gap must not silently become KnowledgeGain. I recommend the term Expected Gap Resolution Value rather than Expected Epistemic Value
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues raw gap-cardinality reduction (|Delta_{t+1}|<|Delta_t|) does not imply epistemic improvement, via a worked example (3 hypotheses reduced to 1 surviving hypothesis that is false), extending Reduction!=Validation!=Determination!=Knowledge; recommends renaming 'Expected Epistemic Value' to 'Expected Gap Resolution Value' to prevent gap reduction being silently equated with knowledge gain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: rho(a) * E[DeltaRed] ... This risks double counting ... E[U(a)] = sum_o P(o|a,K_t,M) U(a,o) where reliability belongs in the observation/evidence model
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's reliability multiplier rho(a)*E[DeltaRed] as risking double-counting reliability (since it may already shape the observation distribution P(O|a,K)); recommends the cleaner E[U(a)]=sum_o P(o|a,K_t,M)U(a,o), moving resource reliability into the observation/evidence model P(O|a,R_t,...) instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Constraint != Preference. ... PrivacyViolation(a)=1 may mean a not-in A^feasible rather than EU(a)-1000. ... A^safe = {a: P(harm|a) <= epsilon} and only then a* = argmax_{a in A^safe} EU(a).
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's treatment of safety/risk as a soft utility penalty (Omega_risk subtracted, beta(R_t) scaling) to a hard feasibility constraint where appropriate: Constraint != Preference, e.g. a privacy violation should remove an action from A^feasible rather than merely penalize its utility, giving A^safe={a: P(harm|a)<=epsilon} filtered before a*=argmax_{a in A^safe}EU(a); likewise the draft's 'high-precision mode' weight adjustment is reframed as a hard safety constraint rather than a mere utility-weight change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a1) approx EU(a2) does not mean a1 equiv_sem a2. So I would call it: candidate deterministic tie-break policy not: selection invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's tie-breaking rule (favor lower latency when utilities are approximately equal) from a 'selection invariant' to a 'candidate deterministic tie-break policy', noting approximately-equal expected utility does not imply semantic equivalence of the two actions, and that the tie-break policy should itself be configurable under the active decision regime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Stop or NoFurtherInvestigation ... Suppose Adeq(K_t,Q,...) = True. Continuing to investigate can have negative utility. ... This prevents KnowledgeOS from becoming an agent that always searches.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds a Stop/NoFurtherInvestigation candidate action to the action set A^possible, so that once Adeq(K_t,Q,...)=True continuing investigation can legitimately have negative utility and EU(Stop) can win, preventing KnowledgeOS from becoming an agent that always searches.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Agreement(Selection,Validation) not-implies Truth. ... ActionDecisionRecord_t containing at minimum: Inquiry, Current Knowledge State, Typed Gap, Candidate Actions, Resource States, Feasibility Results, Utility Model, Utility Parameters, Risk Policy, Selected Action, Rejected Alternatives, Decision Reason, Authorization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a counterfactual-action-quality experiment (estimate P(Adeq(K_{t+1}^a,Q)=1 | K_t,Q,R_t) for every candidate action and compare to the selected action, using a candidate Regret(a)=U(a*)-U(a) or outcome proxies) and an adversarial reliability test giving Agreement(Selection,Validation) does not imply Truth; requires an ActionDecisionRecord_t (inquiry, state, typed gap, candidates, resource states, feasibility, utility model/parameters, risk policy, selected action, rejected alternatives, decision reason, authorization) for inspectability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: How does an epistemic system know what to do when the original request is not itself the real task? ... The inquiry was not completely known at the beginning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses a worked human example (a man asks 'Do you speak Urdu?', is answered 'How can I help?', then reveals he needs metro directions) to argue the real inquiry Q is not always known at the outset; formalizes the sequence Observation O1 -> intent hypotheses H1 -> clarifying question -> the actual inquiry Q emerging only after interaction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t |=? Q ... No. So Zero(K_t,Q) != 0 ... You have discovered an epistemic gap. But then something interesting happens. You don't simply say "I don't know." You begin an epistemic search strategy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes gap discovery (K_t does not entail Q, so Zero(K_t,Q)!=0, i.e. Delta_Q(K_t)!=empty) as triggering not a bare 'I don't know' but an active epistemic search strategy considering available resources (map, search, asking someone, information display), i.e. a policy for reducing the gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NextEpistemicAct: (K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,A,C,EC) -> a_t ... This is a major capability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes 'Epistemic Agency' as a missing KnowledgeOS layer answering 'how does the system decide what epistemic activity to perform next', formalized as NextEpistemicAct:(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,Resources,Constraints,EpistemicStandard)->a_t, where a_t in {answer directly, ask clarification, search, inspect map, consult another source, compare hypotheses, gather observation, defer, report uncertainty, escalate, act}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation: Person asked "Do you speak Urdu?" Hypothesis: Person may need assistance. Confidence: uncertain ... KnowledgeOS therefore should not silently convert interpretation into fact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues an interpretation (e.g. 'he needs help') that could be wrong must be tracked as a hypothesis with explicit confidence rather than silently converted into an established fact; the epistemic state should preserve observation, hypothesis, confidence, action, and how the hypothesis was later confirmed/refined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lord-like function: Generate possible epistemic moves ... Sarathi-like function: Select/navigate among those possible moves.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the earlier Lord/Sarathi research not as 'Lord = God-like kernel' but as two functions: Lord(K_t,Delta,Q,Resources)->CandidateActions (generate possible epistemic moves) and Sarathi(K_t,Delta,CandidateActions,Cost,Risk,Context)->a_t (select among those moves), explicitly tagged [PROP], not to be put into Theory v1.2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic uncertainty ... Uncertainty(Intent) ... Epistemic uncertainty ... Uncertainty(Answer) ... Gap != GapType.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes semantic uncertainty (why did he ask that question -- requires clarification) from epistemic uncertainty (which direction is correct -- requires search/observation/consultation), giving Gap != GapType: the system needs to know what kind of gap it has before choosing an intervention, and notes a third possible gap where the inquiry itself is underspecified (Gap_semantic could precede Gap_epistemic).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not merely answer inquiries; it must manage the process of becoming able to answer them.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a candidate stronger definition of KnowledgeOS's purpose: the system should not merely answer inquiries but must manage the process of becoming able to answer them, extracted from seven human-behaviour-to-hypothesis mappings (interpretation separate from observation; intent as hypothesis until supported; interactive inquiry elicitation; required gap detection; gap-reduction investigation actions; epistemic action selection; determination preceding response) and recommends KR-EPISTEMIC-AGENCY-2026-09 as the next research artifact.

a_aliases: From Knowledge State to Next Epistemic Act

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'KR-EPISTEMIC-AGENCY-2026-09'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity is unitary, primitive, indefinable, and absolutely fundamental ... The Kernel should treat identity as a primitive invariant, not as something defined by properties or content. This confirms our suspicion that content-hash-based identity is insufficient.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports McGinn's Chapter-1 thesis (identity is unitary, primitive, indefinable; numerical identity is the only real identity; no sortal relativity) as validating a prior 'C-8 Identity Continuity' candidate and the KnowledgeAssertionRecord identity requirement, concluding the Kernel should treat identity as a primitive invariant rather than something derived from properties or content, and that content-hash-based identity is insufficient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Non-existent (representation-dependent absence); Unknown (epistemic state); False (contradicts known facts); Missing (expected but not found). These are not the same thing, and conflating them was precisely the C-1 problem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses McGinn's existence-as-first-order-property thesis (existence is a property; non-existence is representation-dependent, not a special state) to split a prior conflated 'REJECTED' concept into four distinct states -- Non-existent (representation-dependent absence), Unknown (epistemic state), False (contradicts known facts), Missing (expected but not found) -- explicitly identified as the fix to a prior 'C-1' problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This validates our decision to keep semantic interpretation outside the Kernel. The Kernel should preserve assertions with propositional references, not attempt to determine what the proposition "really means" in all contexts.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses McGinn's predication thesis (predicates denote properties, not extensions; extension is extra-semantic) to validate keeping semantic interpretation outside the Kernel: the Kernel preserves assertions with propositional references without determining what a proposition 'really means' in every context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Modal words modify the copula, not the predicate; they are modes of instantiation, not quantifiers over worlds. ... The Kernel should preserve mode of instantiation (necessary/contingent/contextual) as a first-class attribute of assertions, not as derived via possible-worlds quantification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports McGinn's necessity-as-copula-modification thesis (modal words are modes of instantiation, not quantification over possible worlds), concluding the Kernel should preserve mode of instantiation (necessary/contingent/contextual) as a first-class attribute of assertions rather than deriving it via possible-worlds semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth is a genuine property; disquotation does not imply deflation. ... The Kernel must not conflate: Truth (property of propositions), Justification (evidence for truth), Confidence (degree of belief), Proof (formal derivation).
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports McGinn's robust (non-deflationary) truth thesis, deriving a four-way non-collapse rule: Truth (property of propositions), Justification (evidence for truth), Confidence (degree of belief), and Proof (formal derivation) are distinct properties with different application conditions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If we import this uncritically ... That would make the Kernel a metaphysical engine, not a preservation boundary. ... semantic multiplicity is extra-semantic ... modality is primitive and irreducible, which means we shouldn't try to "resolve" modal claims in the Kernel. We should preserve them as they are, not attempt to evaluate them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags three ways McGinn's positions would be architecturally dangerous if imported uncritically: (1) his robust metaphysical realism about logical properties would turn the Kernel into a 'metaphysical engine' rather than a preservation boundary -- correct response is to use his distinctions as adversarial lenses, not mandates; (2) his absolute rejection of predicate 'multiple reference' is too semantically limiting since KnowledgeOS predicates do apply to many things -- correct response is that semantic multiplicity is extra-semantic (extension, not meaning) and belongs outside the Kernel; (3) his possible-worlds critique, while philosophically correct, is architecturally irrelevant since KnowledgeOS is not building a possible-worlds engine -- the Kernel should preserve modal commitments as given, not attempt to resolve or evaluate them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: McGinn's Identity Test: Is this identity primitive, or derived from properties? If derived → not Kernel-primitive. ... McGinn's Truth Test: Is this trying to determine truth? If yes → belongs outside the Kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes five per-chapter falsification tests for any proposed Kernel member: Identity Test (primitive or derived from properties?), Existence Test (about existence, or does it conflate existence with status?), Predication Test (trying to determine meaning?), Necessity Test (trying to evaluate modal claims?), Truth Test (trying to determine truth?) -- each with an explicit 'if yes/derived, then outside the Kernel' rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity, existence, predication, necessity, and truth are primitive, irreducible, and distinct. Do not conflate them. Do not try to reduce one to another. Do not try to build a system that "solves" them. Preserve the distinctions.
a_rows_sample.statement: States McGinn's central contribution to the Kernel-finding exercise as a single verdict: identity, existence, predication, necessity, and truth are primitive, irreducible, and distinct; the Kernel must preserve these distinctions rather than conflating, reducing, or attempting to 'solve' them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeOS architecture contains multiple implicit quantification regimes that are currently inconsistent and underspecified. ... we are treating fundamentally different kinds of attributes as if they were the same type of quantity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens the 'KnowledgeOS Attribute Quantification Review' with the finding that the architecture contains multiple implicit, inconsistent, underspecified quantification regimes, treating fundamentally different kinds of attributes (logical, epistemic, temporal, structural, social) as if they were the same type of quantity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence ... What does 0.7 mean? Is it probability? Credence? Certainty? ... Confidence is not truth, proof, or existence. It is an epistemic state of an agent, not a logical property. Treating it as a scalar conflates: Probability, Credence, Certainty, Justification strength.
a_rows_sample.statement: Critiques the existing Confidence attribute (C-11, an open question, currently an unqualified 0.0-1.0 scalar) for conflating four distinct notions -- probability (objective frequency), credence (subjective belief), certainty (epistemic closure), justification strength (evidence weight) -- since Confidence is an epistemic state of an agent, not a logical property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic Status ... Status values are not ordered. "Supported" and "Verified" are qualitatively different, not quantitatively different. This is not a scale — it's a state machine. ... Lifecycle Status ... orthogonal to epistemic status. An assertion can be: Verified + Superseded, Disputed + Active, Unknown + Retired.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Epistemic Status (ASSERTED/SUPPORTED/DISPUTED/VERIFIED/UNKNOWN) from an implicit ordered scale into an unordered state machine, since truth is a property of propositions while epistemic status is a property of the knower's relationship to the proposition; and reaffirms Lifecycle Status (PROPOSED/ACTIVE/SUPERSEDED/RETIRED) as an orthogonal state machine, since e.g. Verified+Superseded, Disputed+Active, and Unknown+Retired are all valid combinations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Temporal Validity ... What does "valid" mean temporally? Is it: True at time T? True throughout interval? True as of known date? ... Authority ... not quantifiable on a single scale. It has multiple dimensions: Institutional authority, Expertise, Role, Contextual legitimacy. ... Provenance ... a structural property that requires graph quantification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires Temporal Validity to specify explicit semantics (POINT: true at time T; INTERVAL: true throughout interval; HISTORICAL: true as of a known date) rather than an underspecified interval; requires Authority to be multi-dimensional (institutional authority, expertise, role, contextual legitimacy) rather than single-scale, noting existence as a property does not depend on authority; requires Provenance to be quantified as a graph structure (entities/activities/agents/derivations), not a scalar, since it is a causal/historical property not reducible to truth/existence/identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assessment Results ... "TRUE" as assessment result = "proposition was evaluated as true under this regime." This is distinct from the proposition being true. ... Semantic Normal Form ... SNF is about semantic equivalence, not logical properties. ... SNF should preserve propositional identity, not determine truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Assessment Result=TRUE ('evaluated as true under this regime') from the proposition itself being true (truth is a property of propositions, assessment a property of the evaluation act, reinforcing the assessment-as-act principle), and distinguishes Semantic Normal Form (a mechanism for determining whether two expressions express the same proposition, an equivalence relation) from logical truth-determination, since predicates denote properties not extensions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is Missing: Identity equivalence; Proposition equivalence; Justification strength; Context similarity; Relation types.
a_rows_sample.statement: Catalogs eight currently-quantified-but-underdefined attributes (Confidence, Epistemic Status, Lifecycle Status, Temporal Validity, Authority, Provenance, Assessment, SNF) and five needed-but-missing quantifications: identity equivalence (when are two records the same identity?), proposition equivalence (when do two expressions express the same proposition?), justification strength (how much evidence supports a claim?), context similarity (when are two contexts the same?), and relation types (what kinds of relations exist between assertions?).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Logical Properties (Primitive, Irreducible) ... not quantifiable on a single dimension. They are primitive logical categories that the Kernel must preserve, not evaluate. ... Epistemic Properties (Qualified by Agents) ... Temporal Properties (Qualified by Time) ... Structural Properties (Qualified by Relations).
a_rows_sample.statement: Classifies all reviewed attributes into four non-conflatable categories: Logical Properties (Identity, Existence, Predication, Necessity, Truth -- primitive, not quantifiable on a single dimension, to be preserved not evaluated), Epistemic Properties (Confidence, Justification, Assessment, Authority -- quantifiable only with explicit qualification: in what, by whom, based on what), Temporal Properties (Temporal Validity, Lifecycle Status -- quantifiable by time intervals with explicit semantics), and Structural Properties (Provenance, Predication-as-instantiation, SNF -- quantifiable by relation types, not scalar values).

a_rows_sample.anchor: identity(recordA, recordB) → BOOLEAN ... Confidence: subject, agent, value, type: PROBABILITY|CREDENCE|CERTAINTY|EVIDENCE_WEIGHT, basis, context, assessedAt ... Lifecycle x Epistemic Combination Table: ACTIVE+VERIFIED=True as of T; SUPERSEDED+VERIFIED=Historically true; ACTIVE+DISPUTED=Under contention; RETIRED+UNKNOWN=Not evaluated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Supplies concrete proposed schemas per attribute: Identity as a binary equivalence predicate (distinct from qualitative sameness of properties); Confidence requiring explicit subject/agent/value/type(PROBABILITY|CREDENCE|CERTAINTY|EVIDENCE_WEIGHT)/basis/context/assessedAt fields; Epistemic Status and Lifecycle Status each as explicit state machines with named transitions, combined in a worked Lifecycle x Epistemic x Validity table (e.g. ACTIVE+VERIFIED = true as of T; SUPERSEDED+VERIFIED = historically true; ACTIVE+DISPUTED = under contention; RETIRED+UNKNOWN = not evaluated); Temporal Validity with POINT/INTERVAL/HISTORICAL semantics; Authority as multi-dimensional (agent/role/institution/jurisdiction/legitimacy/context); Provenance as an explicit graph; Assessment as categorical-with-qualification (subject/evaluator/regime/context/result/uncertainty/basis); SNF as categorical equivalence (STRONG/WEAK/CONTEXTUAL).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Immediate: Split REJECTED into ... Distinguish epistemic from lifecycle status as orthogonal axes ... Medium-Term: Define identity equivalence criteria ... Long-Term: Build SNF as semantic equivalence mechanism (outside Kernel) ... Do not conflate: Truth with Confidence; Existence with Status; Identity with Content; Necessity with Temporal Validity; Assessment with Truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Closes with a three-horizon action plan (immediate: split REJECTED into four states, separate epistemic from lifecycle status, qualify confidence explicitly, specify temporal-validity semantics, distinguish assessment results from truth values; medium-term: define identity equivalence and proposition equivalence criteria, develop provenance graph quantification, establish authority dimensions; long-term: build SNF as an outside-Kernel semantic-equivalence mechanism, develop confidence-aggregation models, establish cross-context identity mapping) and a five-item final non-conflation rule (Truth/Confidence, Existence/Status, Identity/Content, Necessity/Temporal Validity, Assessment/Truth).

a_rows_sample.anchor: McGinn (Logical): Identity, Existence, Predication, Necessity, Truth. O'Connor (Metaphysical): Persons, Objects, Properties, Powers/Capacities, Causes, Reasons, Intentions, Actions. ... The Kernel should preserve McGinn's logical properties. ... The Kernel should NOT implement O'Connor's metaphysical categories. They are the content of knowledge claims.
a_rows_sample.statement: Cross-checks O'Connor's metaphysical categories against McGinn's logical properties, concluding the Kernel preserves McGinn's five logical properties (invariant structure of any knowledge claim) and must not implement O'Connor's metaphysical categories (which are the semantic content of knowledge claims, not Kernel structure), giving a three-level architecture: Kernel Level (Identity/Existence/Predication/Necessity/Truth), Content Level (Persons/Objects/Properties/Powers-Capacities/Causes/Reasons/Intentions/Actions, each 'as claimed'/'as asserted', never as Kernel primitives), and Explanation Level bridge (Explanation Records: causal/reasons/intentional/explanatory claims, preserved as content).

a_rows_sample.anchor: identity, existence, predication, necessity, and truth may be structural primitives of the space in which knowledge is expressed at all. ... LOGICAL STRUCTURE: IDENTITY, PREDICATION, EXISTENCE -> PROPOSITION -> TRUTH, MODALITY. And then we can place persons/objects/... inside that structure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the emerging entity-list model (Objects/Persons/Events/States/Properties/Causes/Reasons/Intentions/Claims/Evidence) by identifying a deeper logical-structure layer (Identity, Predication, Existence -> Proposition -> Truth, Modality) that must exist first, with all ontological content placed inside that structure rather than beside it, citing McGinn's framing of the project as 'logical ontology'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the very structure of predication therefore already incorporates identity and distinctness. ... A KnowledgeOS object cannot safely be identified merely by its current description. We need: ENTITY -> identity, separately from ENTITY -> properties, descriptions, names, classifications, observations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues predication itself already presupposes identity/distinctness (asserting 'x is red' already distinguishes x from other objects and red from other properties), concluding a KnowledgeOS entity's identity must be modeled separately from its properties/descriptions/names/classifications/observations; illustrated by one Person Identity underlying multiple names/roles/descriptions/observations/references ('Alice', 'Dr. Smith', 'the committee chair', 'the person who submitted proposal X') -- avoiding confusing different descriptions of a thing with different things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Persons and objects are not merely two kinds of "things." Persons introduce agency, reasons, intentions, and causal powers into the space. Causes introduce directed dependency between things, states, events, and actions. ... Cause -> RELATION / DEPENDENCY
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a model that would treat Person, Object, and Cause as equivalent node types: Person and Object are both entities/nodes but Person additionally carries agency, beliefs, desires, reasons, intentions, and action-capacity beyond Object's mere properties/capacities; Cause is not an entity at all but a relation/dependency type (e.g. Fire--causes-->heating, Person--causes-->intention), citing O'Connor's distinction between event causation and agent causation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: particulars have properties → properties ground causal capacities → capacities can be exercised → effects occur. ... capacity / capacity becomes an important bridge between WHAT SOMETHING IS and WHAT SOMETHING CAN DO.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes O'Connor's causal-capacity structure for objects (Object->Properties->Causal capacity->[circumstances]->Effect) and agents (Person->{beliefs,desires,reasons}->Agent capacity->Intention->Action), illustrated by 'a person can open the door' requiring bodily capability+knowledge+desire+opportunity before capacity-to-act yields possible action; Capacity is identified as the bridge concept between what something is and what it can do.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Person -> believes X, desires Y, has reason R -> deliberation -> intention -> action ... KnowledgeOS can represent not just: what happened? but: why did it happen? That is a completely different class of knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Chains reasons/beliefs/desires into a deliberation->intention->action sequence, arguing this lets KnowledgeOS represent 'why did it happen' as a distinct knowledge class from 'what happened', citing O'Connor's connection of actions to the agent's desire-belief complexes or reasons.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS doesn't necessarily need a primitive object called Knowledge. Instead it can represent: PERSON Alice, EVENT opening-the-door, ... REASON wanting-to-leave, CAUSAL/EXPLANATORY RELATION wanting-to-leave --explains--> opening-the-door, TRUTH-BEARER ... The knowledge emerges from the structured configuration.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes 'Alice opened the door because she wanted to leave' into Person/Event/Object/Mental-State/Reason/Causal-Explanatory-Relation/Truth-bearer/Truth-status/Evidence/Source without any primitive 'Knowledge' object, concluding knowledge emerges from the structured configuration -- explicitly connected to Merricks' 'arranged-X-wise' eliminativism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cause ≠ explanation, Person ≠ object, Reason ≠ cause, Action ≠ event-description, Capacity ≠ actual exercise. ... Knowledge is not a primitive bucket containing facts. Knowledge is structured intelligibility over different kinds of entities, states, events, relations, reasons, causes, and truth-bearers.
b_rows_sample.statement: Combines Merricks' non-collapses (Truth≠evidence≠aboutness≠truthmaker) with five new O'Connor-derived non-collapses (Cause≠explanation, Person≠object, Reason≠cause, Action≠event-description, Capacity≠actual exercise) into the central converging principle: knowledge is not a primitive bucket containing facts, but structured intelligibility over different kinds of entities, states, events, relations, reasons, causes, and truth-bearers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dimension A — What exists / what we refer to (Particulars: Objects/Persons-Agents/Events/States/Situations; Universals/Properties: Properties/Capacities/Powers/Relations) ... Dimension B — How things are connected (identity, instantiation, part-of, about, causes, enables, prevents, depends-on, explains, supports, intends, believes, desires, acts-on) ... Knowledge Space = Entities × Relations × States × Claims × Contexts.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes two intersecting dimensions for the Knowledge Space instead of one hierarchy: Dimension A (particulars: objects/persons/events/states/situations vs universals: properties/capacities/powers/relations, citing O'Connor's particular/universal distinction) and Dimension B (fourteen relation types: identity, instantiation, part-of, about, causes, enables, prevents, depends-on, explains, supports, intends, believes, desires, acts-on), combined as Knowledge Space = Entities x Relations x States x Claims x Contexts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Persons are not merely objects inside Knowledge Space. They are participants that traverse and transform Knowledge Space. ... a person is simultaneously an entity + a bearer of properties + a causal agent + a source of reasons + a holder of beliefs + a holder of intentions + an actor + an observer + a knower + a producer of claims.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies Person as the bridge between ontology and epistemology, being simultaneously entity, bearer-of-properties, causal agent, source of reasons, holder of beliefs/intentions, actor, observer, knower, and producer of claims, so that WORLD->perception->PERSON->{belief,reasoning,intention,decision,action}->WORLD; concludes persons are participants that traverse and transform Knowledge Space, not merely objects inside it. (This claim is explicitly challenged as architectural 'overreach' later in this same file's Critical Analysis section.)

b_rows_sample.anchor: humans don't merely ask: What caused X? They ask: Why X? Those aren't always identical. ... KnowledgeOS probably needs CAUSE and separately EXPLANATION, with relationships between them ... physical explanation, causal explanation, functional explanation, intentional explanation, reasons explanation, historical explanation, logical explanation ... without pretending they're all the same thing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes CAUSE from EXPLANATION as separate KnowledgeOS concepts with relationships between them, since 'why X?' is not always identical to 'what caused X?', enumerating seven non-identical explanation kinds (physical, causal, functional, intentional, reasons, historical, logical) that must not be treated as the same thing, citing O'Connor's exploration of the relationship between causal and reasons-based explanation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Space is not primarily a hierarchy of topics. It is a relational space whose nodes represent entities, events, states, properties, propositions and mental contents, while its edges represent relations such as identity, instantiation, aboutness, causation, explanation, dependence, support, intention and agency. Then topics become views over that space. Not primitives.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the file's central research hypothesis: Knowledge Space is a relational space (nodes: entities/events/states/properties/propositions/mental contents; edges: identity/instantiation/aboutness/causation/explanation/dependence/support/intention/agency), not a hierarchy of topics; Topics become projections over this space rather than primitives, illustrated by 'Topic: Free Will' as a projection over Persons+Actions+Reasons+Intentions+Causes+Possibilities+Responsibility+Time+Truth-claims.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merricks: Truth cannot be reduced to truthmaking/evidence/aboutness. O'Connor: Persons, objects, properties, powers, causes, reasons, intentions and actions cannot simply be collapsed into events or objects. Our KnowledgeOS investigation: Knowledge must remain reconstructible, contextual, governed and evidentially traceable. ... Is this a primitive entity, a relation, a property, a state, a representation, a perspective, or merely a useful projection?
b_rows_sample.statement: States three converging constraints from Merricks, O'Connor, and the project's own KnowledgeOS investigation, concluding the right next step is not to declare an ontology but to run a 'Knowledge Space Ontological Discovery' over 22 candidates (Persons, Objects, Properties, Events, States, Actions, Agents, Causes, Effects, Powers, Capacities, Reasons, Intentions, Claims, Propositions, Truth, Evidence, Sources, Contexts, Time, Modality, Explanation), asking of each whether it is a primitive entity, relation, property, state, representation, perspective, or merely a useful projection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel should preserve records of agency (who asserted what, based on what reasons), not implement agency itself. ... KnowledgeOS cannot be the arbiter of what truly explains what. That would be a semantic oracle. ... The correct response is: The Kernel should preserve claims about explanation, not the explanations themselves.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against four dangers of importing O'Connor's framework uncritically: (1) treating Person/Agent Causation/Intention/Action as Kernel primitives would make the Kernel a metaphysical engine -- the Kernel should preserve records of agency, not implement agency; (2) the Kernel becoming an arbiter of what truly causes/explains what would make it a 'semantic oracle' -- it should preserve claims about explanation, not the explanations themselves (paralleling Assertion-preserved vs Truth-evaluated-externally); (3) capacities/powers are notoriously hard to formalize (counterfactuals, contexts, degrees, interactions) and belong in assertion content, not Kernel structure; (4) treating persons as active Kernel-level transformers of Knowledge Space is overreach -- the Kernel should preserve records of participation (who made what claim, when, based on what), not model transformative agency itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: McGinn (Logical): Identity, Existence, Predication, Necessity, Truth. O'Connor (Metaphysical): Persons, Objects, Properties, Powers/Capacities, Causes, Reasons, Intentions, Actions. ... The Kernel should preserve McGinn's logical properties. ... The Kernel should NOT implement O'Connor's metaphysical categories. They are the content of knowledge claims.
b_rows_sample.statement: Cross-checks O'Connor's metaphysical categories against McGinn's logical properties, concluding the Kernel preserves McGinn's five logical properties (invariant structure of any knowledge claim) and must not implement O'Connor's metaphysical categories (which are the semantic content of knowledge claims, not Kernel structure), giving a three-level architecture: Kernel Level (Identity/Existence/Predication/Necessity/Truth), Content Level (Persons/Objects/Properties/Powers-Capacities/Causes/Reasons/Intentions/Actions, each 'as claimed'/'as asserted', never as Kernel primitives), and Explanation Level bridge (Explanation Records: causal/reasons/intentional/explanatory claims, preserved as content).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeAssertionRecord ... relationRefs: CAUSAL_CLAIM: (WANTING-TO-LEAVE → OPENING-DOOR); EXPLANATORY_CLAIM ...; AGENT_CLAIM ...; REASON_CLAIM ... ... The Kernel should NOT: Determine whether Alice actually wanted to leave; Determine whether the desire caused the action; Determine whether the explanation is true; Model "agent causation" as a Kernel primitive.
b_rows_sample.statement: Provides a fully worked test case ('Alice opened the door because she wanted to leave') showing exactly what the Kernel preserves -- a KnowledgeAssertionRecord (id, propositionRef, contextRef, assertedBy, assertedAt, temporalScope, epistemicCommitment, relationRefs including CAUSAL_CLAIM, EXPLANATORY_CLAIM, AGENT_CLAIM, REASON_CLAIM) -- against a six-item list of what the Kernel must never do (determine whether Alice actually wanted to leave, whether the desire caused the action, whether the explanation is true, model agent causation or capacity as primitives, or treat person differently from object at the Kernel level), with those determinations explicitly assigned to outside Semantic Interpretation, Evaluation, and Reasoning layers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Space Is Not Flat ... nine distinct ontological regions ... Relations Are Not Uniform ... nine distinct relation types ... The Space Has Directionality ... TEMPORAL: Past → Present → Future ... EXPLANATORY: Cause → Effect (causal); Reason → Action (intentional); Ground → Claim (epistemic); Premise → Conclusion (logical).
b_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes three structural discoveries about the Knowledge Space: it has nine distinct ontological regions (Objects, Persons, Events, States, Properties, Powers/Capacities, Causes, Reasons, Explanations); relations are not uniform, spanning nine distinct types (Identity, Instantiation, Causation, Agent Causation, Explanation, Intention, Belief, Desire, Representation); and the space has directionality both temporal (Past->Present->Future) and explanatory (Cause->Effect causal; Reason->Action intentional; Ground->Claim epistemic; Premise->Conclusion logical), each direction type kept distinct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Persons and Causes Lens ... Is this entity an object with causal powers, or a person with reasons, intentions, and agency? ... Knowledge is not just about facts. It's about persons, reasons, intentions, actions, causes, and explanations. ... Reason ≠ Cause (Persons and Causes lens); Person ≠ Object (Persons and Causes lens); Explanation ≠ Event (Persons and Causes lens).
b_rows_sample.statement: Names 'the Persons and Causes Lens' with defining question 'is this entity an object with causal powers, or a person with reasons, intentions, and agency?', usable as adversarial lens/content specification/boundary warning; closes with the bottom line that knowledge is about persons, reasons, intentions, actions, causes and explanations (expanding what must be preservable) without the Kernel needing to implement agency, causation, explanation, or intentionality, extending the project's non-collapse family (Expression≠Meaning, Truth≠Proof, Assertion≠Reality) with Reason≠Cause, Person≠Object, Explanation≠Event.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Layer 0 — Logical primitives: Identity, Predication, Existence, Truth, Necessity/Modality ... These are not ordinary knowledge objects. They define the space in which knowledge can be represented. ... Layer 1 — Ontological particulars ... Layer 2 — Properties and powers ... Layer 3 — Relations ... Layer 4 — Epistemic representations ... Truth is not merely another epistemic attribute. It connects the epistemic representation back toward reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a five-layer KnowledgeOS architecture: Layer 0 Logical primitives (Identity, Predication, Existence, Truth, Necessity/Modality -- defining the representational space itself, not ordinary knowledge objects); Layer 1 Ontological particulars (Person, Object, Event, State, Situation); Layer 2 Properties and powers (Property, Capacity, Causal Power, Disposition, Role, State); Layer 3 Relations (identity, instantiation, part-of, causes, enables, depends-on, supports, explains, intends, believes); Layer 4 Epistemic representations (Claim, Proposition, Observation, Evidence, Source, Argument, Inference, Interpretation), with Truth singled out as connecting the epistemic representation back toward reality rather than being merely another epistemic attribute.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Persons and Causes gave us the dynamics of the space. Logical Properties gives us the structural grammar of the space. ... KnowledgeOS is fundamentally a structured space of predication and reference over entities, properties, events and agents, constrained by identity, existence, truth and modality, with causal, explanatory, evidential and intentional relations connecting the structures.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the file's converging hypothesis combining both McGinn and O'Connor readings: KnowledgeOS is fundamentally a structured space of predication and reference over entities, properties, events and agents, constrained by identity, existence, truth and modality, with causal, explanatory, evidential and intentional relations connecting the structures -- explicitly held as a hypothesis not yet implemented.

b_rows_sample.anchor: current knowledge includes C and E -> temporarily remove C -> ask whether E becomes less expected -> C has causal relevance. His probabilistic criterion is that, in the contracted epistemic state, occurrence of C raises the probability of E. ... probabilistic influence alone does not automatically establish causation ... P(E|C) > P(E) is not automatically C causes E. ... preserve causal_hypothesis separately from statistical_association.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes causal belief via contraction: temporarily remove candidate cause C from the epistemic state and test whether effect E becomes less expected (probabilistic criterion: in the contracted state, C's occurrence raises P(E)); connects this to the project's Persons+Causes research, proposing KnowledgeOS distinguish observed sequence/correlation/causal belief/causal evidence/causal hypothesis/causal explanation; explicitly warns P(E|C)>P(E) does not automatically establish C causes E (spurious/direct/indirect causes need additional treatment), requiring causal_hypothesis be preserved separately from statistical_association.

b_rows_sample.anchor: # 7. This connects directly to our "Persons and Causes" work
b_rows_sample.statement: Connects Searle's institutional layer to the earlier O'Connor Persons and Causes work by distinguishing natural/physical capacity from institutional power, and introduces 'deontic power' (rights, obligations, duties, privileges, permissions, requirements, authorizations, entitlements) as the content that institutional status can generate.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance does not treat a later-arriving text as automatically governing... a later act is not automatically a supersession.
a_rows_sample.statement: A later-arriving instruction/act is not automatically treated as superseding a prior, already-executed one; which text governs is a disposition the PO/ARB must make explicitly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What a self-review CAN establish...What it CANNOT establish...that the migration design is sound...that its findings are right...that nothing was omitted that the author did not think of
a_rows_sample.statement: A self-review (same producer as the artifact under review) explicitly states it can establish mechanical completeness and provenance (re-runnable by anyone) but cannot establish design soundness, correctness of findings, or omissions the author itself did not think of; states it must never be cited as independent verification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: INFO-1 — a defect this pass found in its own artifact... The plan should scope the claim as 'exactly one writer OF GOVERNANCE EVIDENCE' and cite the discriminating test.
a_rows_sample.statement: The plan's claim of 'exactly one writer' is correct but not reproducible from the obvious grep, which returns three files; the discriminating test (references runtime/workflow AND writes) is what makes the claim survive, and the plan should scope its own claim accordingly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the S4b lane's registered executionContext names the producer as claude-code-session:5e1dd9ee. The plan 3817eb2b was produced by claude-code-session:1c8b041b.
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-2: a provenance discrepancy exists in the governance record itself (not the plan) — the plan discloses its own producer correctly, but the lane's registered executionContext names a different process as producer; reconciling this is left as a Governance act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the §1 inventory is a point-in-time measurement of a LIVE corpus... §1's numbers are a dated observation, not the migration's inventory, and must not be substituted for the Phase-1 run.
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-4: the plan's own current-state inventory numbers are only a dated snapshot of a corpus that continues to accept writes, and must never be substituted for the migration's own required Phase-1 inventory run.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Verified: the CONDITION was recorded two days earlier, in 2026-08-17-KOS-ATTR-ARCH-001-stage2-bounded-context-confirmation.md as coupling problem C-2
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the premise that a migration-plan finding is 'new evidence': the underlying condition (interpretation authority is environment-swappable via KOS_MECHANISM_PATH) was already recorded two days earlier as coupling problem C-2 with its own remedy route (R-37/ADR-C6); what the migration plan added was precision (a two-axis formulation and line-addressed evidence), not discovery.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Single Authority Resolver invariant is explicitly extended from governance-evidence record location to also govern the mechanism that interprets those records...an EXPLICIT SCOPE EXTENSION, not as an application of the existing invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision: Option A (bring the interpreter-selection axis under the same resolver boundary as the record-location axis) is adopted, but recorded explicitly as a deliberate scope extension of the existing invariant rather than a silent application of it, so that the estate's rule against silent scope expansion is honoured.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the delivered plan already presumes A... The two delivered artifacts are not aligned: the plan implements an answer the review says is not yet given.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observes that the migration plan's Phase 5 already operationally assumes Option A (bringing the interpreter mechanism under the resolver) while the governance review states the question is not yet determined and that governance must not determine it — an internal misalignment between two delivered artifacts that the pending decision must resolve.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This review establishes: completeness · provenance · conformity to decided governance constraints. It CANNOT and does NOT establish: technical soundness · implementation correctness · migration safety · production readiness.
a_rows_sample.statement: An independent (different producer) governance review explicitly separates what it establishes (completeness, provenance, conformity to decided constraints, all re-executed rather than re-read) from what only a separate technical Architecture review may establish (soundness, correctness, safety, readiness).

a_rows_sample.anchor: INFO-1 — the inventory figures have drifted by one, and the drift is fully accounted for.
a_rows_sample.statement: Re-measures the corpus independently and finds a one-grant drift from the plan's cited figures, traces it exactly to a governance act registered after the plan's commit, and confirms the plan was accurate at its own commit — demonstrating the corpus's live-growth property with concrete numbers.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 23 / 30 ... trials that lost a transition ... exit status of the losing process 0 — accepted, reported {"ok":true,"seq":2} ... sequence set of every survivor DENSE and MONOTONIC
a_rows_sample.statement: A concurrency experiment run in a temp directory (never against the real corpus) launched two concurrent `append` calls against the workflow-state.php writer 30 times; 23 of 30 trials silently lost a transition, the losing process reported success (exit 0), and the surviving sequence remained dense and monotonic every time — the same loss reproduced on the `grant` write path.

a_rows_sample.anchor: session-resolve.php EXECUTES an arbitrary program named by the environment and HANDS IT the authority record directory as an argument. ⇒ This is not only an interpretation path. It is a WRITE path
a_rows_sample.statement: session-resolve.php is found to be stronger a hazard than the plan states: it executes a subprocess named by the KOS_MECHANISM_PATH environment variable and passes it the authority record directory as an argument, making it a write path through a component whose own bytes contain no write call — a hazard whose value rises once relocation makes the target the durable authoritative store.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the durable artifact is a git blob, and git — not the copy — decides the committed bytes... a clone on a CRLF platform materialises different bytes and the Phase-4 hashes no longer verify
a_rows_sample.statement: Byte-preservation of the migration copy is undermined by an unpinned .gitattributes (`* text=auto`, eol unspecified): checkout normalisation is a no-op today (no CR bytes exist), but a future clone on a CRLF platform would materialise different bytes and invalidate the Phase-4 hashes, and the plan's own scope fence names .gitignore but is silent about .gitattributes, the file that actually governs committed bytes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PASS WITH DESIGN CLARIFICATIONS ... CL-1–CL-3 are GATES ON PHASE 3 — the migration must not begin until they are closed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Verdict: PASS WITH DESIGN CLARIFICATIONS, twelve items (CL-1..CL-12) ranked, of which CL-1 (concurrency/completeness claim must be bounded, not absolute), CL-2 (Phase 1 inventory must be re-executed and frozen at migration time, not pinned to a stale literal), and CL-3 (the plan names no act that produces the resolver it later switches to) are gate-class and block Phase 3 from beginning; none requires reopening B', R-CONFLICT, OPEN-M3, or placement governance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the withdrawal is real ... NO SILENT REINTRODUCTION FOUND. The stronger claim does not survive anywhere in the artifact.
a_rows_sample.statement: CL-1 (concurrency/completeness) is verified CLOSED: AMD3's bounded restatement ('no record lost RELATIVE TO the frozen manifest and both inputs') is checked at every site in the artifact and the withdrawn absolute claim is not silently reintroduced anywhere.

a_rows_sample.anchor: RC-4 — NEW GAP the remedy does not cover ... A write landing after the Phase-5 re-hash but before the writer is switched goes to the RUNTIME copy ... and is destroyed by Phase 7.
a_rows_sample.statement: RC-4: the freeze/manifest/re-hash design verifies the runtime copy at exactly one instant (the Phase-5 re-hash), three phases before the destructive Phase-7 removal; a write landing in that gap is in neither the frozen manifest nor either reconciliation input and would be silently destroyed by Phase 7's removal, which relies on a byte-verification performed earlier and never rechecked.

a_rows_sample.anchor: RC-1 ... Phase 2b as written is CIRCULAR with Phase 3, and Phase 3's precondition is therefore unsatisfiable.
a_rows_sample.statement: RC-1: as amended, a phase that pins .gitattributes AND commits the Phase-1 manifest in the same commit as the Phase-3 copy cannot complete before Phase 3 (its commit must contain Phase 3's output), while Phase 3 cannot begin before that phase completes — the same defect class as CL-3 (a phase consuming an artifact its own predecessor has not produced) reappearing inside a remedy meant to close a different clarification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: RC-2 — but the OTHER half of INV-R1's row-1 cell was not split, and it collides with both contract suites... an implementer who applies the boundary check literally makes the entire pinned contract suite exit 65 with no report.
a_rows_sample.statement: RC-2: every test in both pinned contract suites drives the components through a --dir temp path outside the governed evidence boundary, so a literal reading of the resolver's boundary-validation rule would make the entire pinned suite refuse with no report; the fix requires stating that a governed override selects a non-authoritative output location rather than violating the boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: RC-10 — a mis-resolved path MATERIALIZES rather than failing ... The writer creates its parent directory.
a_rows_sample.statement: RC-10: saveRecord() calls mkdir on its target's parent directory, meaning a resolver that returns a wrong-but-well-formed path does not fail loudly but silently manufactures a new evidence location — recreating the exact misfiling defect B' exists to close, inside the component built to close it; the refusal must therefore be enforced before saveRecord is reached.

a_rows_sample.anchor: RC-9 — 'canonical re-encode' is not defined ... a false CASE B (escalation) rather than a false CASE A (silent merge) — the safe direction
a_rows_sample.statement: RC-9: the plan's 'common prefix byte-identical' comparison rule for CASE A does not define its canonicalization method (e.g. key-order sorting), and since JSON decode/encode preserves insertion order, two semantically equal but differently-ordered records would compare unequal, producing a false escalation to CASE B rather than a false silent merge (CASE A) — the safe failure direction, but ambiguous as written.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-CONFLICT (PROPOSED): a conflict in the authority record is never resolved by choosing a side. seq density (O-6) makes loss detectable; a resolution that leaves a seq gap is invalid by construction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes R-CONFLICT: any resolution of a governance-evidence conflict is invalid by construction if it leaves a sequence gap, chooses one side silently, or is otherwise not seq-density-preserving.

b_rows_sample.anchor: History ≠ Reconstruction Guess
b_rows_sample.statement: A candidate governance principle proposed alongside R-CONFLICT and other estate principles (Recording ≠ Asserting; Reference ≠ Ownership): History ≠ Reconstruction Guess — recorded as a recommendation, not yet adopted at this point in the file.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D2 constrains how D1 is implemented — this is the load-bearing consequence.
b_rows_sample.statement: The R-CONFLICT decision (D2) binds how the relocation (D1) may be implemented: the migration must preserve sequence integrity and provenance, must not delete or re-create history, and if a relocated record and a runtime record ever diverge, R-CONFLICT governs — neither side may be silently chosen.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STRICT EXTENSION ... append the runtime tail M+1…N ... PREFIX DISAGREEMENT ... MUST NOT be resolved mechanically.
b_rows_sample.statement: R-CONFLICT is operationalized into exactly two mechanically-distinguishable divergence shapes: STRICT EXTENSION (the common prefix is byte-identical and one side merely extends further — resolved automatically as a union, not a choice) and PREFIX DISAGREEMENT (the common prefix itself differs — a genuine authority conflict that must be recorded, preserved on both sides, and escalated to a PO/ARB act, never resolved mechanically).

b_rows_sample.anchor: RC-9 — 'canonical re-encode' is not defined ... a false CASE B (escalation) rather than a false CASE A (silent merge) — the safe direction
b_rows_sample.statement: RC-9: the plan's 'common prefix byte-identical' comparison rule for CASE A does not define its canonicalization method (e.g. key-order sorting), and since JSON decode/encode preserves insertion order, two semantically equal but differently-ordered records would compare unequal, producing a false escalation to CASE B rather than a false silent merge (CASE A) — the safe failure direction, but ambiguous as written.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RD-3 — Phase-7 mismatch disposition routes post-demotion writes into §6 CASE A, which would import non-authoritative bytes that §8 says require a governance act
b_rows_sample.statement: RD-3: AMD4 routes every Phase-7 mismatch to the same reconciliation logic (CASE A/B), but CASE A appends the runtime tail as a legitimate extension, meaning a post-writer-switch write to the demoted store would be silently imported into the authoritative store — contradicting the plan's own rule that re-promoting a demoted source is a governance act, not a merge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CASE α — pre-writer-switch ... RECONCILE under §6 ... CASE β — post-writer-switch ... not authoritative — written against a demoted store ... QUARANTINE · record the conflict · ESCALATE. Never imported.
b_rows_sample.statement: AMD5 splits the Phase-7 mismatch disposition into two named cases with opposite treatment: CASE α (pre-writer-switch, authoritatively-produced bytes) reconciles under the existing R-CONFLICT logic, while CASE β (post-writer-switch, written against an already-demoted store) is quarantined, recorded as a conflict, and escalated — never imported — with a conservative tie-break (unresolvable ordering defaults to CASE β).

b_rows_sample.anchor: RD-3·a — CASE β has no terminating condition, and criteria 12 and 15 are jointly unsatisfiable in it ... after a β event the runtime source therefore never equals manifest + reconciled delta, so §4.4's own gate can never be satisfied
b_rows_sample.statement: Two of AMD5's own acceptance criteria are jointly unsatisfiable after a CASE β event: criterion 12 requires the runtime source to equal 'manifest + reconciled delta' before removal, but criterion 15 defines CASE β bytes as deliberately never reconciled, so the removal gate could never be satisfied, be permanently blocked, or be satisfied only by destroying the quarantined bytes — none of which the plan states.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The conflict history becomes a domain event stream rather than simply an overwritten database row. That gives KnowledgeOS much stronger reconstruction capability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the R-CONFLICT concept as an event stream (EvidenceQualified events from two sources triggering EvidenceConflictDetected, then Conflict Resolution, then ConflictResolved), arguing this gives much stronger reconstruction capability than treating the conflict as an overwritten database row.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EvidenceConflict ... - ConflictId - ConflictingEvidence[] - DetectedAt - ConflictType - ResolutionStatus - ResolutionAuthority - ResolutionDecision ... A conflict resolution must preserve: provenance; history; reconstruction capability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Models the R-CONFLICT idea as a first-class EvidenceConflict domain aggregate (with ConflictId, ConflictingEvidence[], DetectedAt, ConflictType, ResolutionStatus, ResolutionAuthority, ResolutionDecision fields), owned by the Knowledge Evidence Context, whose invariant requires any resolution to preserve provenance, history, and reconstruction capability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RECORD EXISTENCE != AUTHORITY ESTABLISHMENT; PHYSICAL STORAGE ORDER != DOMAIN EVENT ORDER
b_rows_sample.statement: Two DDD non-confusions asserted as load-bearing for the migration's DV-3 correction: the durable store may already contain copied governance records before authority transfers, and those copied records do not themselves establish authority; the authority-boundary discriminator must be the domain event (the transfer), never physical file position.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A self-check that can assert its own success is EVIDENCE, never assurance.
b_rows_sample.statement: The assurance-tooling boundary discipline: an author's own trace/test suite is required delivered evidence but never discharges the independent-review gate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: QUARANTINE LAUNDERING: moving a post-demotion record out of the demoted store would hide the quarantined evidence, making the source spuriously satisfy the final-rehash comparison and incorrectly opening the removal branch.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names and corrects an inverted rationale (the original plan said a move would 'break the enumeration'; the corrected reasoning is the opposite -- a move makes a comparison PASS when it should FAIL) -- a general anti-pattern for any evidence-quarantine mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PREMISE 2: a migration mechanical write on a store confers no authority, and is evidenced by a governance append that describes it -- which is what makes the placement-decision recursion terminate.
b_rows_sample.statement: The load-bearing premise of the C-4 termination argument, moved inside the argument by this correction; without it the argument for where evidence lands would appear to terminate after one iteration when it does not.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 23 of 30 concurrent-append trials silently lost a transition; every survivor was dense and monotonic -- density is NOT a completeness proof.
b_rows_sample.statement: A reproduced concurrency experiment (mktemp dirs via --dir, never against the live corpus) showing the read-modify-write append path has no lock/lease/CAS, so a losing writer's transaction vanishes while the surviving sequence remains perfectly dense -- refuting an earlier absolute 'no record silently dropped' claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: quarantine is a domain state with a business consequence, not a directory condition: an undisposed conflict means the migration aggregate cannot legitimately transition to its completed state.
b_rows_sample.statement: A DDD reading of the quarantine mechanism: a single undisposed quarantine can block migration completion indefinitely, by design, because the aggregate refuses an invalid state transition rather than because of a tooling limitation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Removal (Phase 7) is not Deletion: evidence persists at the verified durable target, a byte-verified copy exists and is authoritative, history is relocated with provenance intact -- and removal occurs only after Phase 4 hash verification passed and Phase 5 switched.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes the migration's terminal cleanup act from the R-CONFLICT-forbidden act of destroying historical governance evidence.
