a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZOOM-OUT-03-CALIBRATED-CONTEXT-RETURN-2026-09 ... PRINCIPAL RESULT: O-F insufficient — class reachability ⇏ estimand variability.
a_rows_sample.statement: FROZEN, GATE MET, EXECUTED 2026-09-05: primary Delta_loss is NON-IDENTIFIABLE/DEGENERATE (A5=0 exactly, not merely negligible); the M1 artifact from KR-ZOOM-OUT-01 is eliminated by stratification (0.000); M0 (0.497/0.520) replicates only as a descriptive phenotype with no single winner; FR-004's prediction is not met; and the retrospectively-validated O-F* repair (O-F*) is shown to FAIL on this very experiment — it would not have been authorized had it been checked in advance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Hypothesis → Estimand → O-F* → Population → Calibration → Control → Freeze → Execution → Adjudication
a_rows_sample.statement: The experimental protocol frozen 2026-09-05, introducing O-F* (Estimand Non-Degeneracy Preflight): every declared-variable quantity must have a pre-execution variation witness under the frozen computation because 'class reachability does not imply estimand variability'; it runs before the freeze because its failure is grounds to rewrite the estimand while that is still legitimate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observed diagnostic ⇏ new primary estimand ... Observed convergence ⇏ theory promotion
a_rows_sample.statement: Two research-governance safeguards (explicitly not theory claims) stated because KR-ZOOM-03's directed diagnostic and KR-ZOOM-OUT-01's conditional-population result both appeared only after the pre-registered primary estimand had already returned a weaker verdict and could not be adopted; calibration must be a separate pass with its own gate, inspected before analysis code runs, because in KR-ZOOM-OUT-01 the null stratum silently became the 'winning' M1 artifact and the calibration-gate failure was invisible until audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not immediately create another theory document. ... Lens Freeze → Pre-registration → O-F* → Synthetic Witness Generator → Controls → Execution → Adjudication
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01 as the next artifact — a pre-registration plus synthetic witness generator running the R1-R6 tests on controlled synthetic traces first, biological examples serving only as structural inspiration, explicitly citing the O-F* protocol as part of the required execution order.

b_rows_sample.anchor: At every observation you have infinite possible dimensions to be discovered. ... the projection to different observation field by zooming in can be the fact finding process about an event or process
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that at every observation there is a potentially unbounded discoverable dimension space, and that zooming into different observation fields to find causes/situations/sources of an event constitutes the fact-finding process about that event, using a Nexus egress=70GB/day example with potentially relevant dimensions {Network,Backup,Repository,CI/CD,GitLabRunner,Configuration,Users,Traffic,Logs,Storage,Time,Security,Deployment,...}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D_t subseteq D* and potentially D* -> open/unbounded discovery space. ... Don't claim literally that the dimensions are mathematically infinite unless the model establishes such a domain. Instead: the discoverable dimension space is open-ended relative to the current representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the informal 'infinite possible dimensions' claim to a precise formulation: the currently represented dimensions D_t are a subset of a potentially discoverable D*, and the discoverable dimension space is open-ended relative to the current representation (D_t -Inquiry-> D_{t+1}), without D_{t+1} necessarily being a superset of D_t since dimensions can also become irrelevant/superseded/out-of-contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn(K_t,O,Q) -> FocusedInquirySpace ... The dimensions explored by Zoom-in need not have been present in the original observation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates Zoom-in from the earlier K_t->Subgraph(K_t) (found inadequate) to ZoomIn(K_t,O,Q)->FocusedInquirySpace, where focus is not deletion of the rest of K_t and the explored dimensions need not have been present in the original observation -- a discovery operation rather than a within-representation detail operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Graph Traversal != Epistemic Investigation ... KnowledgeGraph = representational substrate ... ZoomIn = inquiry-directed exploration over that substrate and its discoverable extensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates Graph Traversal (a Knowledge Graph can represent an edge like GitLabRunner-causes->Egress) from Epistemic Investigation (KnowledgeOS asks why the edge should exist, requiring Evidence, Provenance, Time, AlternativeHypotheses, Assessment, Determination), giving KnowledgeGraph=representational substrate while ZoomIn=inquiry-directed exploration over that substrate and its discoverable extensions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t) = Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t) rather than simply FocusedState -> OriginalState. ... this is exactly why our previous Zoom-out experiments struggled: we were trying to classify Zoom-out before clearly separating restoration from integration.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zoom-out from mere restoration (FocusedState->OriginalState) to Integration: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t)=Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t), diagnosing that prior Zoom-out experiments struggled because they attempted to classify Zoom-out before separating restoration from integration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn = search for potentially relevant structure ... Zero = test eliminability of represented structure. ... ZoomIn discovers and Zero tests.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Zoom-in and Zero as complementary operations relative to the same (Q,C,Pi,S): Zoom-in searches for potentially relevant structure (discovers), Zero tests eliminability of represented structure (tests); a candidate pipeline ZoomIn->ExpandedRepresentation->ZeroLens->RelevantSubspace->FactFinding is proposed but explicitly not assumed to be a fixed order, tagged [PROP] not axiom.

b_rows_sample.anchor: projection to different observation field ... I would be careful. ... Unless we have pi^2=pi or an appropriate semantic projection definition, don't call every Zoom-in a projection. Use inquiry-relative view transformation ... or focus transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against calling every Zoom-in operation a mathematical 'projection' unless an established idempotent projection structure (pi^2=pi) or semantic-projection definition is demonstrated; recommends 'inquiry-relative view transformation' or 'focus transformation' as neutral terminology, consistent with the Zero Algebra lesson to discover the algebra rather than impose it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn: Where should I investigate? EpistemicAgency: What should I do next? FactFinding: What does the evidence establish? ZoomOut: How does the finding change the broader state?
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates four distinct research questions into a coherent architecture: ZoomIn (where should I investigate), Epistemic Agency (what should I do next), Fact Finding (what does the evidence establish), Zoom-out (how does the finding change the broader state), combined into Observation->Relevance->ZoomIn->DimensionDiscovery->FactFinding->Determination->ZoomOut->Integration->K_{t+1} with a feedback loop from DimensionDiscovery back to NewObservation->NewZoomIn.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 ... ZF1 -- Context preservation ... ZF2 -- Dimension expansion ... ZF3 -- Cross-boundary discovery ... ZF4 -- Determination dependence ... ZF5 -- Investigation != determination ... ZF6 -- Zoom-out integration ... ZF7 -- Resource/agency interaction
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 with seven candidate hypotheses: ZF1 ZoomIn(K_t,Q) does not imply Delete(K_t); ZF2 D_t subseteq D_{t+1} can occur through investigation; ZF3 a relevant dimension need not be contained in the initial observation's representation; ZF4 newly discovered dimensions can change Determine(Q); ZF5 ZoomIn != Determine; ZF6 a finding discovered during Zoom-in can modify the broader state; ZF7 the next investigated dimension depends on K,Q,Delta,Resources,Context,Contract,Risk.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Backup -> large transfer, GitLab Runner -> large transfer, Replication -> large transfer ... the system must not say I found GitLab Runner, therefore GitLab Runner is the cause. ... No Determination Without Alternative Space.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses a multi-cause Nexus-egress failure case (Backup, GitLab Runner, and Replication all plausibly producing large transfer) to argue against single-hypothesis-collapse ('I found X, therefore X is the cause'), requiring the full hypothesis set H_Q to undergo Evidence Assessment before Determination, stated as the principle 'No Determination Without Alternative Space.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_t -> ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q) -> D_t subseteq D_{t+1} -> Acquire -> Assess -> Determine -> ZoomOut(Finding,K_t) -> K_{t+1} ... Terminology Correction: View Transformation vs. Projection
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a four-level Decoupled Dimensional Expansion & Integration Pipeline (1. Observation Entry O_t={d_0}; 2. Dimensional Discovery ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q)->D_t subseteq D_{t+1}; 3. Fact-Finding Acquire->Assess->Determine; 4. Integration ZoomOut(Finding,K_t)->K_{t+1}), and replaces the term 'projection' with 'Inquiry-Directed View Transformation' to avoid assuming idempotence (pi^2=pi) prior to empirical discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t <=_O Focus(K_t,Q) where <=_O means that the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable. ... ZF1 -- Context Preservation: Zoom-In changes inquiry focus without itself removing or invalidating surrounding Knowledge State.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF1's undefined comparison ZoomIn(K_t,Q)!=Delete(K_t) to K_t<=_O Focus(K_t,Q), where <=_O means the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable, avoiding accidentally turning Zoom-In into an undefined representation-theoretic operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Discovery of a dimension != acceptance of that dimension into Knowledge State. ... exactly analogous to your existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge. ... ZF2 -- Dimensional Expansion: Inquiry-directed investigation can introduce candidate explanatory dimensions not represented in the initial active representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF2's D_t subset D_{t+1} (which conflates dimension discovery with state evolution) by introducing D_t^cand as candidate dimensional space distinct from D_t^rep (accepted into Knowledge State), giving D_t^rep subseteq D_{t+1}^cand and a later integration D_{t+1}^cand -> D_{t+1}^rep, analogous to the existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(I_t) ... ZF3 currently risks becoming tautological ... GitLab Runner may already exist somewhere in the Knowledge Graph but not be connected to the egress observation. That is not dimensional discovery.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF3's under-specified d* not-in Rep(O_t) (risking tautology) by distinguishing not-observable-in-O_t, not-represented-in-K_t, and genuinely-discovered-during-investigation, requiring d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(investigation trace I_t), noting a dimension already present elsewhere in the graph but unconnected to the observation does not count as dimensional discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) != Determine(K'_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) with K'_t = Expand(K_t,d*). ... Otherwise a change in determination could simply result from changing standards, evidence, inquiry, or reasoning regime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF4 (Determine(Q|D_t)!=Determine(Q|D')) to hold the full determination signature Q,C,EC,S,R fixed and intervene only on the discovered dimensional representation, giving Determine(K_t,...)!=Determine(K'_t,...) with K'_t=Expand(K_t,d*), so the change is attributable to dimensional expansion alone rather than confounded with standards/evidence/inquiry/reasoning-regime changes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Zoom-In that discovers ... has succeeded even if Fact-Finding concludes: Cause remains underdetermined. So: DiscoverySuccess not-implies Determination should probably become a candidate invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Retains and operationally sharpens ZF5 (ZoomIn:(K_t,O_t,Q)->D^cand versus FactFinding:(D^cand,E,H_Q,M,S)->Standing->Determination), proposing the candidate invariant DiscoverySuccess does not imply Determination: Zoom-In can succeed in surfacing candidates even when Fact-Finding concludes the cause remains underdetermined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomOut should not be defined as ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t. That would recreate the old restoration model. Instead: ZoomOut(F,K_t) = Integrate(K_t,F) -> K_{t+1} ... ZoomOut = integration of finding rather than: ZoomOut = inverse(ZoomIn).
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly forbids defining Zoom-Out as the inverse of Zoom-In (ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t would recreate the old restoration model); Zoom-Out is Integrate(K_t,F)->K_{t+1} where F may contain newly discovered dimensions, assessed evidence, determined relationships, rejected hypotheses, unresolved alternatives, provenance, and temporal information, so K_{t+1}!=K_t may occur even though Zoom-In itself deleted nothing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* in ArgMax_{d in D^cand} E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d) as a candidate agency policy, not a kernel law. ... ZoomIn != Agency. Agency selects the next investigation; Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF7's dimension-selection formula (which assumed Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions are comparably valued, costs are scalarizable, and an argmax exists) to an explicitly candidate agency policy d* in ArgMax_{d}E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d), not a kernel law, reaffirming ZoomIn != Agency (Agency selects the next investigation, Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZF8 -- Representation Boundary Non-Closure ... An initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions. ... ZF3 asks: Can the relevant dimension cross the initial boundary? ZF8 asks: Is the initial dimensional representation itself epistemically non-closed?
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds ZF8 (Representation Boundary Non-Closure): the initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions, distinguished from ZF3 (can a relevant dimension cross the boundary) by asking instead whether the initial representation is itself epistemically non-closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zoom-In != Zero != Fact-Finding ... Determination ... Zoom-Out ... Epistemic Agency ... This is much more promising than trying to make Zoom-In or Zoom-Out kernel primitives.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a six-way functional separation as the architectural conclusion: Zoom-In (expand/search the inquiry space) != Zero Lens (determine what can be eliminated while preserving contract) != Fact-Finding (establish what evidence supports) != Determination (establish what can be decided under the epistemic regime) != Zoom-Out (integrate finding into broader state) != Epistemic Agency (select what to investigate/do next); recommends testing ZF2+ZF3+ZF5 first as the foundational experiment before the rest of the architecture is tested.

b_aliases: Zoom-in as fact-finding discovery, not detail-inspection

A sentence delta is determinate if it uniquely determines an epistemic state ... for any determinate sentence delta, there is an objective sentence phi such that \models O\delta\equiv O\phi
a_rows_sample.statement: Full formal Only-Knowing O operator (e consists exactly of the alpha-worlds), its ASK/TELL characterizations via O, and the determinate-sentence theorem (every determinate sentence is O-equivalent to some objective sentence) -- the formal basis for the Representation Theorem and the strongest available candidate formalization of 'all that is known' for the Zero TODO.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Having a knowledge base means that these sentences are all that is known. ... having an incomplete knowledge base means knowing where that knowledge is incomplete. ... Armed with this meta-knowledge, an agent is in a position to do something better than giving up ... it can apply a default, perform sensing, ask a question ... enables the agent to know what it does not know.
a_rows_sample.statement: Four key quotes arguing Zero should mean KNOWING that nothing is missing (not merely having no known gaps), that incompleteness itself should be meta-known so the agent can act on it (apply a default, sense, ask), and that the main justification for an agent reasoning about its own knowledge is enabling it to know what it does not know -- directly relevant to, and possibly in tension with, this batch's other 'Zero cannot be known as Zero' argument (Fitch's-paradox translation in S2530) and the structural-unknowability classification (S2528).

The triangle operator -> Quantifying-in with explicit belief
a_rows_sample.statement: Final unhedged recommendation to integrate six findings directly into Theory v1.2 (TELL/ASK->core operations, Representation Theorem->Sat semantics, Only-knowing->Zero definition, Explicit belief B->tractable reasoning, successor-state axioms->delta semantics, triangle operator->quantifying-in), without the [PROP]/[OPEN] hedging used by the more disciplined reviews elsewhere in this batch (e.g. S2520-S2524, S2526-S2528).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Only-knowing can provide a formal model for one aspect of epistemic completeness, but Zero is broader. ... OnlyKnowing \rightarrow Zero\ candidate not OnlyKnowing=Zero. ... having an incomplete knowledge base means knowing where that knowledge is incomplete.
a_rows_sample.statement: Narrows S2532's Only-Knowing-as-Zero-basis claim to OnlyKnowing -> Zero-candidate (contributory, not defining), since Zero also depends on what the boundary inquiry itself can establish (KnownBoundary(K,pi) does not automatically establish Zero(K,pi)); restates the existing Zero invariants (Unknown!=Absent, Unresolved!=False, NoEvidence!=EvidenceOfAbsence, NoKnownGap!=Complete) as still standing.

b_rows_sample.statement: Instead of treating delta as an unspecified transformer, investigate K_{t+1}=Succ(K_t,e_t) where each state component carries conditions for becoming true, becoming false, and persistence — i.e. the frame problem, borrowed from situation-calculus successor-state axioms F(x,do(a,s)) ≡ gamma_F(x,a,s) v (F(x,s) & ¬delta_F(x,a,s)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Table: what I would actually add to KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3 (T1-T5) vs What I would NOT adopt
b_rows_sample.statement: Recorded editorial recommendation: five candidate theoretical commitments (T1 explicit/implicit knowledge, T2 reasoning is semantics-dependent Cn_S(K), T3 evaluation may consume implicit knowledge Eval_c(Cn_S(K),r,Gamma), T4 state transition needs persistence semantics Succ_S, T5 explanation is not determination) proposed for Theory v1.3 as strong candidates, none yet kernel-promoted; explicitly rejects Sat=FOL-entailment, Zero=CWA, Zero=Delta=empty universally, Boundary=frame axioms, delta=situation calculus, Identity=unique-names+domain-closure, DL=Boundary-taxonomy, mandatory default reasoning, FOL-as-representation-language, and YES/NO/UNKNOWN-sufficiency.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1}=Succ_{\mathcal S}(K_t,e_t) ... successor semantics must account for: newly introduced content; removed or invalidated content; persistent content; contextual applicability; provenance/history. This does not define δ as situation calculus.
b_rows_sample.statement: delta(K_t,e_t)->K_{t+1} remains an open transition problem; adopts K_{t+1}=Succ_S(K_t,e_t) as a research framework requiring successor semantics to account for five things: newly introduced content, removed/invalidated content, persistent content, contextual applicability, and provenance/history. Explicitly: this defines situation-calculus successor-state reasoning as a formal candidate to investigate delta against, not a definition of delta itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: pickingUp(x,do(c,s))\equiv startPickup(x)\in c\lor(pickingUp(x,s)\land endPickup(x)\notin c) ... Poss(startMoveLeft,s)\equiv\neg movingLeft(s) ... Poss(\{startMoveLeft,startMoveRight\},s) should be false. The converse of the foundational axiom need not hold.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends successor-state semantics to concurrent action sets (successor-state axiom for a concurrent-action fluent), and identifies the 'precondition interaction problem': individually-possible concurrent actions (startMoveLeft, startMoveRight) can be jointly impossible even though each satisfies its own precondition axiom, requiring additional interaction constraints beyond the individual precondition axioms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [EXT] throughout. Extracted, not endorsed. ... The induction axiom is second-order. The extraction states the consequence plainly: the system is not fully first-order decidable. Any transfer inherits this. ... It rests on the causal completeness assumption ... This is an assumption about the axiomatiser's knowledge, not a theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Reiter's formal ontology and axioms (already captured in S2536) under an explicit [EXT]/'extracted not endorsed' framing, emphasizing two carried-forward limitations for any KnowledgeOS transfer: the induction axiom is second-order (not fully first-order decidable), and the successor-state axiom rests on an unproven causal-completeness ASSUMPTION about the axiomatiser's own knowledge, not a theorem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "conflicting_effects_from_F_false": ["F"], "conflicting_effects_from_F_true": ["F"], "conflict_resolved_silently_in_favour_of_gamma_plus": true, "finding": "when gamma+ and gamma- both name F, the SSA yields F TRUE with no signal that the effect axioms were inconsistent. The frame solution PRESUPPOSES consistent effect axioms; it does not detect their inconsistency."
b_rows_sample.statement: Executed result: a deliberately conflicting action (gamma+ and gamma- both naming fluent F) is silently resolved to F=TRUE from both prior states, with the successor-state axiom giving no signal that its own effect axioms were inconsistent -- confirming determinism and persistence-of-unmentioned-fluents work correctly, but exposing that inconsistency detection is entirely outside the mechanism's scope.

a_rows_sample.statement: The proposed chain is validated edge by edge: 'KnowledgeOS creates PKS' is a hypothesis (n=0, every PKS is authored by a person); 'PKS contains Engineering Knowledge' is WRONG, violating I-7 (a PKS contains product knowledge and bindings; reusable method must not live in it — the current breach is the exception that proves the rule); 'knowledge organized by Ontology' holds with the precision that L-A organizes artifacts/carriers, not knowledge itself (I-1); 'used by Capabilities' holds (capabilities may read across space boundaries, never own — H-1); 'Capabilities executed through Runtime' is imprecise (capabilities are advisory scripts invoked on demand; the runtime executes Execution Assets/ASTs; 41 enforced controls live runtime-side while every capability is advisory — the drawn edge hides this finding); 'Runtime produces Evidence' should attribute production to WORK (P-7/P-8), the runtime only hosts the work; 'Evidence improves KnowledgeOS' is only partly true (n≈3 informal, B-1's fact).

a_rows_sample.anchor: W-3 · "PKS is a projection" — FALSIFIED for every existing PKS artifact
a_rows_sample.statement: The claim 'PKS is a projection' is falsified for every existing PKS artifact: examined fields (Authority: Generated, human-asserted; Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS; a Disposition History with ARB reviewer endorsement 9.9/10; a Commission) are incompatible with a projection, which would carry authority:derived (machine-checkable), no acceptance (regenerated, not accepted), a source and regeneration command, and no Commission. A mechanical grep for authority:derived|generated across docs/pks, docs/knowledgeos, docs/implementation returns 10 files, every one a prose mention of the vocabulary, not an application of it — those paths sit outside knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include. This sharpens a prior Ontology Classification finding ('blocked in practice') to stronger: existing PKS artifacts are positively authoritative — authored, commissioned, reviewed, disposed, and accepted — incompatible with 'derived'.

b_rows_sample.statement: Twelve concepts projected into PublicDigit, a hypothetical Hospital Information System, and a hypothetical ERP System: MISSION, STRATEGY, DESIGN POLICY, CAPABILITY, KNOWLEDGE, ARTIFACT, KNOWLEDGE SPACE, PRODUCT are invariant across all three; PRINCIPLE specializes (partly external in Hospital and ERP, owned by a regulator/accounting standard); PKS fails (one per product, or per deployment?); RUNTIME ADAPTER disappears in both new domains; PROJECTION (I-4) fails, since a discharge summary and a financial statement are both generated and legally/formally authoritative.

b_rows_sample.statement: Eleven responsibilities scored across five dimensions (Product Discovery, Strategic Discovery, Tactical Discovery, PKS Generation, Engineering Governance, Capability Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Verification, Evidence Collection, Operational Learning, Capability Evolution). Dimension totals: METHOD 8/11 complete (strongest dimension); BINDING 4/11 carry a coupling (SD-1 fatal, ES-005.1 leak, config paths, 2 product-specific by nature); EVIDENCE 4/11 at n=0, only 3 have more than a single instance; IMPLEMENTATION 6/11 fully manual, 0 generative; ENFORCEMENT 0/11 (before correction below).

b_rows_sample.anchor: CORRECTED 2026-08-02 — "0 OF 11 ENFORCING" IS TOO STRONG ... .claude/settings.json holds deny ×19 and ask ×22 — 41 controls the runtime genuinely ENFORCES. What I actually established is that no CAPABILITY enforces, not that nothing does
b_rows_sample.statement: A prior claim that 0 of 11 responsibilities are enforcing is corrected: applying the Boundaries!=Triggers vocabulary immediately falsifies it, since .claude/settings.json holds permissions.deny x19 (BOUNDARY, enforced) and permissions.ask x22 (TRIGGER, enforced) — 41 controls the runtime genuinely enforces; 10 hooks + 6 scripts are ADVISORY (16, not enforced). The sharper finding: enforcement lives in the RUNTIME ADAPTER, capabilities live in the PLATFORM — enforcement exists exactly where governance does not, and is absent exactly where it does.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Product Definition ... The generative relation is creates, not contains. KnowledgeOS → creates → PKS → guides → Product
b_rows_sample.statement: Product definitions: KnowledgeOS (the reusable engineering platform, output is rules and methods, never product knowledge; canon status: potential product, Supporting Subdomain, gate unopened); PKS (one product's knowledge, one per product, never reusable, generated is n=0, every PKS hand-built to date); Business Product (the software delivering business value); Running Software (deployed system + evidence); AI Runtime (an adapter, not a product, replaceable); Product Binding (the product-specific input contract a reusable method requires, SD-1 the archetype — 'the concept this baseline contributes'). The generative relation is 'creates', not 'contains': KnowledgeOS creates PKS, which guides Product — a compiler is not the program it produces.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ALREADY FULLY MODELLED — four layers, not two ... GOVERNANCE POLICY → CAPABILITY MAPPING → RUNTIME ADAPTER → CONCRETE CONFIGURATION
b_rows_sample.statement: The AI Runtime architecture is already fully modeled in PKS_Phase_III_Governance_Runtime_Adapter_Record.md as four layers: Governance Policy -> Capability Mapping (tool-neutral) -> Runtime Adapter -> Concrete Configuration (.claude/settings.json). .claude/settings.json is an adapter, not the governance model; another runtime could replace Claude Code and only the adapter would be rewritten. Capability Mapping exists so Claude-specific vocabulary (ask, deny, permissions) cannot leak upward into the governance model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PD-6 · Runtime — 2 criteria. BELOW the bar ... NOT A DOMAIN at the commissioned bar. A supporting subsystem with an adapter boundary
b_rows_sample.statement: PD-6, Runtime, scores only 2 of 9 criteria (integration characteristics observed; deployment autonomy only claimed at n=1) since UL divergence is falsified (no Capability Mapping artifact; deny/ask/allow approximate the abstract verbs) and semantic ownership is absent (no declared owner for .claude/) — below the commissioned bar, demoted from an earlier D-3 classification, and classified as a supporting subsystem with an adapter boundary, not a domain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SP-3 · AI Runtime — reclassified as an ADAPTER BOUNDARY, not a product ... already 4 layers
b_rows_sample.statement: The AI Runtime, proposed by the commission as a strategic product, is reclassified as an adapter boundary, not a product: ES-005.1 states the mount 'never moves and is never the architecture', the Runtime Adapter Record calls .claude/settings.json 'an ADAPTER'; it owns how one runtime implements each abstract capability but never owns governance vocabulary ('ask, deny, permissions cannot leak upward'); it is replaceable, not reusable, a different property. It is already modeled in four layers: Governance Policy -> Capability Mapping -> Runtime Adapter -> Concrete Configuration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASK[alpha,e] = YES if e|=Kalpha; NO otherwise ... TELL[alpha,e]=e \cap \{w\mid e,w\models\alpha\} ... e,w\models K\alpha \iff for every w'\in e, e,w'\models\alpha
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal semantics for ASK[alpha,e] (YES iff e|=K-alpha, else NO) and TELL[alpha,e] (intersect e with the worlds satisfying alpha), and the K operator (K-alpha true at w iff alpha holds in every world w' in the epistemic state e) -- the precise formal machinery underlying the TELL/ASK candidate used loosely elsewhere in this batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (\alpha\supset K\alpha) FALSE ... (K\alpha\supset\alpha) FALSE ... If \models\alpha then \models K\alpha TRUE ... For any subjective sentence sigma: \models(\sigma\supset K\sigma) [positive introspection] ... logical omniscience
b_rows_sample.statement: Catalogues formal properties of K: truth does not imply knownness and knowledge need not be accurate (K models belief, not factive knowledge, in this framework) while valid sentences are always known; complete positive introspection holds for subjective sentences; and the K operator suffers logical omniscience (knows all logical consequences of what it knows) -- a limitation later addressed by the B operator.

$$... **Given this particular required-distinction set and this adequacy criterion, at least three distinguishable flat classes are required.**
b_rows_sample.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.

States a methodological principle from the chromatic-number finding: colourability only proves pairwise coding capacity under the chosen abstraction, it does not establish that resulting values carry the required semantic or operational meaning -- cardinality sufficiency is not semantic adequacy.

a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a 3-way taxonomy of history dependence: Type I intrinsic-state dependence (part of what the knowledge state means, e.g. epistemic standing, belongs inside K); Type II transformation-context dependence (affects transformation evaluation without being knowledge content, e.g. Policy, supplied as an external T parameter); Type III audit/history dependence (needed for reconstruction/explanation/accountability without necessarily altering knowledge identity, e.g. Provenance) -- pinpointing Provenance's placement as exactly the Type-III unresolved case.

a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the ideal minimal sufficient Knowledge State via a biconditional: F(H1)=F(H2) if and only if H1 and H2 are indistinguishable by every mandatory future operation -- a mathematically precise target (coarsest operationally valid equivalence) replacing the vaguer question of how many fields K should contain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Aggregate boundary must retain every piece of information required to enforce its invariants and execute its domain behaviors correctly. a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the counterexample-class methodology (from S1621) to 4 specific classes -- provenance, revision history, identity-vs-content, identity-vs-status -- each showing content-only or identity-only state abstractions fail whenever some mandatory operation actually observes the discarded distinction, with each case's status remaining conditional on which operations are mandatory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K* = minimum information sufficient to preserve all mandatory behavioral distinctions. Not: K*=everything ever observed. And not: K*=smallest tuple someone can invent. This is the mathematically meaningful notion of minimality.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the minimal-state principle in its final form: K* is the minimum information sufficient to preserve all mandatory behavioral distinctions -- explicitly neither an unbounded record of everything ever observed nor an arbitrarily small invented tuple.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We must not force every operation into T:K->K because Step 255 already demonstrated that some operations may depend on external policy, authority, time, evidence or other typed context.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies Step 255's finding directly: no operation should be forced into the shape T:K->K, since operations may legitimately depend on external typed context (policy, authority, time, evidence) rather than K alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add requires a definition of identity/equality. This directly links Step 256 back to the unresolved Equality_K. ... set-like semantics Add(K,x)=K union {x} [versus] identity-aware semantics [which] may reject an object whose identity already exists.
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows Add cannot be formally defined until equality/identity is resolved, since two radically different semantics remain open: plain set-union (duplicates silently absorbed) versus identity-aware rejection of objects whose identity already exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Does removal mean x not-in K' or x in K' with status Withdrawn? These are radically different semantics. ... Remove != Withdraw unless the vocabulary explicitly decides otherwise. ... Reject(x) != Remove(x). This is an important Ubiquitous Language distinction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes true deletion from lifecycle-status change as radically different operation semantics, concluding Remove != Withdraw and Reject != Remove unless the theory explicitly decides to identify them -- since a status-changed object remains represented in K while a deleted one does not.

b_rows_sample.anchor: revision requires identity preservation: id(x')=id(x)? If yes, Revision(x,x') is a state transition on one entity. If no, Revision is actually Remove(x)+Add(x'). ... What makes two knowledge objects 'the same object' across revision? ... This is another reason why equality and identity cannot be pos
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows Revise cannot be formally defined until cross-time object identity is resolved: if id(x')=id(x), Revise is a genuine state transition on one entity; if not, Revise reduces to Remove+Add of two different entities -- the same identity/equality dependency recurring across multiple operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance(x3) = {Provenance(x1), Provenance(x2)}. If so, Merge is inherently provenance-preserving. This means that the operation registry itself can reveal whether provenance is operationally essential. ... Split requires a preservation invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows Merge is diagnostically important for the provenance question: if the merged object's provenance is the union of its sources' provenances, Merge is inherently provenance-preserving, meaning the operation registry itself (not abstract argument) can reveal whether provenance is operationally essential; separately notes Split requires an explicit semantic-preservation invariant across its decomposition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Every semantically relevant external variable must be explicit. ... T: K x Policy x Time -> K'. This is preferable to hiding Policy or Time inside an implicit global context. ... Deterministic Transformation != Immutable Knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a determinism-discipline principle: any externally-varying quantity a transformation depends on (e.g. current time, applicable policy) must be an explicit function argument, never an implicit global, or the transformation appears nondeterministic to the mathematical model; separately clarifies determinism (same inputs, same result) is orthogonal to immutability of the overall knowledge base.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R(T_i) = (Name, Domain, Codomain, Preconditions, Postconditions, Invariants, Parameters, Dependencies, Determinism, ProvenanceDependency, HistoryDependency, PolicyDependency, IdentityDependency) becomes the working registry schema.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the working operation-registry schema R(T_i) with 13 fields, extending the mandate's original 9-field proposal with explicit PolicyDependency and IdentityDependency flags.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we should not assume closure: T_i,T_j in T => T_j o T_i in T. The earlier audit already found that the governed transformation subset is not demonstrated closed under composition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms the corpus's established finding that the governed transformation subset is not closed under composition, applying it to the operation-registry construction: composition T_j o T_i is only meaningful when Codomain(T_i) intersects Domain(T_j), and closure must never be assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T_Add: K x X -> K, T_Merge: K x X x X -> K, Validate: K x E -> Result, Approve: Candidate x Authority -> ApprovedCandidate. Therefore KnowledgeOS may be better modeled as a typed transition system than as a single algebra.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms operations need not share one homogeneous signature shape by giving 4 explicitly differently-typed example operations, reaffirming the typed-transition-system (not single algebra) conclusion already reached in Steps 249-250.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Validate not-equiv Transform. This prevents a common category error in the kernel. ... Command is not Transformation ... Command -> Decision -> Transformation -> NewState ... Event != T. The corpus already distinguishes Command -> Transformation -> Event.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms three category-error-preventing non-collapses for the operation vocabulary: Validate != Transform (validation may determine valid/invalid without changing K); Command != Transformation (command is intent/request, not the state change itself); Event != Transformation (an event records an occurrence, distinct from the state-evolution-defining function).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ProvDep(T_i) in {0,1,?} ... This gives us a way to empirically determine where history must survive. ... transforms the vague question 'Does provenance belong in K?' into the operational question: exists T in T: ProvDep(T)=1? If yes, then provenance-sensitive information must be available to that op
b_rows_sample.statement: Converts the recurring vague 'does provenance belong in K' question into a precise operational test using explicit per-operation dependency flags (ProvDep, HistDep, PolicyDep in {0,1,?}): if any operation has ProvDep=1, provenance-sensitive information must be accessible to it, and only then does the placement question (K-resident, T-parameter, or external context) arise -- directly implementing S1621's Type-I/II/III taxonomy as a concrete research tool.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Required(T) = StateReq(T) union ContextReq(T). Only StateReq(T) constrains K. ... K* = argmin_K Complexity(K) subject to semantic sufficiency.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the kernel-minimization target by splitting an operation's total required information into StateReq(T) (must be resident in K) and ContextReq(T) (may be supplied externally, does not constrain K), restating the optimization target K*=argmin Complexity(K) subject to semantic sufficiency with this refined split.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T must be typed before K can be minimized. Operations may be partial. Operations need not share one homogeneous signature. Validation, Command, Event and Transformation must not be conflated. Provenance/History/Policy dependence must be explicitly tested per operation. Not established: the nine cand
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the step's established-versus-not-established results: established that T must be typed before K can be minimized, operations may be partial, need not share one signature, and 4 key terms must not be conflated, with dependency-testing mandatory per operation; explicitly not established that the 9 candidate operations or any particular signature is final.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The most important unresolved signatures are: Supersede, Merge, Revise, Transform. These operations have the highest potential to distinguish competing state/history models. ... Step 257 -- Formalize the Four Discriminating Operations ... Then we can run the first real congruence experiment ... That
b_rows_sample.statement: Names Supersede, Merge, Revise and Transform as the 4 highest-value operations for distinguishing competing state/history models, and sets Step 257 as their complete formalization (across domain/codomain/preconditions/postconditions/identity/provenance/history/policy/determinism/composability) in order to run the first real congruence experiment -- explicitly judged stronger evidence than proposing yet another candidate kernel tuple.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 12 operations fully specified [create, assert, retract, relate, merge, supersede, refine, resolve, remove, replay, validate, assess] each with Input/Preconditions/Output/Postconditions/Det/Auth/Gov/Hist/Computable/Failure modes. All 12 rated Computable=YES.
b_rows_sample.statement: Fully specifies concrete 11-field signatures for 12 named operations (create, assert, retract, relate, merge, supersede, refine, resolve, remove, replay, validate, assess), each rated computable=YES, directly executing the operation-registry schema Step 256 (S1623) had proposed abstractly -- e.g. retract has failure mode LOSSY-NO-INVERSE (executed), relate can fail via a cycle, merge may introduce contradiction (executed), replay is order-dependent (executed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: T: K x Q x C -> K' [not necessarily unary]. It simply means that transformation is a typed state transition, not necessarily a closed unary function. ... hidden inputs are forbidden ... Every semantically relevant external dependency must be explicit. ... Prov(k') = Prov(k) union Prov(q) union Prov(
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Transform need not be unary (T:KxQxC->K', a typed state transition rather than a closed K->K function), reaffirms that every semantically relevant external dependency (policy, time, authority, evidence) must be an explicit argument to preserve determinism, and proposes an unestablished provenance-propagation model Prov(k')=Prov(k) union Prov(q) union Prov(c) for Transform specifically.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic Normal Form (SNF): different surface expressions normalize to one stored semantic structure; expressions become views
a_rows_sample.statement: The first formal naming of SNF in the admitted corpus, illustrated by two paraphrase sentences both normalizing to one EVENT/ACTOR/OBJECT/JUSTIFICATION/CONDITION structure; explicitly classified 'New Candidate Mechanism (Not Kernel)'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic Invariance Layer: Expression Layer -> Semantic Parser -> Meaning Graph -> Knowledge Identity
a_rows_sample.statement: A proposed mechanism pipeline realizing SNF, cited as feeding Logical Architecture, never the kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expression Order != Meaning Structure
a_rows_sample.statement: The order-invariance facet of the Vani (Expression != Meaning) principle: meaning must be reconstructed from invariant relationships, not from the accidental arrangement of expressions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: two different sentences can become the same knowledge object; two similar sentences can become different knowledge objects
a_rows_sample.statement: States the semantic-identity discrimination rule contrasting KnowledgeOS's target behavior with an LLM's similar-expression-implies-similar-meaning risk.

a_rows_sample.anchor: rigorous SNF metric definitions: a semantic metric-space distance d (non-negativity, identity, symmetry, triangle inequality), a Bayesian posterior P(theta_i|E,C) over semantic interpretations, normalized semantic entropy H_sem, convergence C_snf, non-collapse NC_snf, transformation stability T_snf,
a_rows_sample.statement: A senior-mathematician-style formalization of an originally underspecified SNF measurement proposal (undefined D, undefined p_i, undefined C_snf/NC_snf/T_snf), giving each metric explicit mathematical properties and a proposed experimental protocol (1,000 controlled cases) with target thresholds.

a_rows_sample.anchor: structural similarity != semantic equivalence: a Jaccard-style graph-edit distance over SNF graphs measures 'SNF Structural Distance', not yet 'Semantic Distance' -- APPROVE(Architect,Design) vs AUTHORIZE(Architect,Design) may be semantically equivalent but structurally different, while adding one C
a_rows_sample.statement: A critical mathematical correction rejecting the premature identification of a graph-edit metric with 'semantic distance', renaming the former precisely.

a_rows_sample.anchor: three distinct uncertainties must not be conflated: model/interpretation uncertainty ('which interpretation should I choose'), representational uncertainty ('does my representation capture the meaning'), and epistemic uncertainty ('is this justified') -- the semantic compiler should expose the first
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines the Bayesian semantic-entropy proposal by noting that low entropy over a compiler's own candidate-interpretation space does not mean the expression is objectively unambiguous -- it only means the model's own candidate set has low uncertainty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: false convergence (semantic collision) is more dangerous than false divergence: if two equivalent sentences produce different SNFs, that is inefficiency; if two different propositions produce the same SNF, that is knowledge corruption.
a_rows_sample.statement: A stated safety asymmetry motivating the introduction of a hard non-collapse safety gate (rather than a weighted composite score that could average away a catastrophic collapse) and a proposed 'Semantic Collision Rate' metric.

a_rows_sample.anchor: do NOT use a weighted harmonic-mean composite SNF score; instead impose a hard safety constraint (non-collapse below threshold => FAIL, independent of the other metrics) plus descriptive metrics for the surviving system.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the mathematically-elegant but architecturally-dangerous idea of averaging convergence/non-collapse/transformation/entropy into one quality score, on the grounds that a catastrophic non-collapse failure must never be diluted by good scores elsewhere.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100-case synthetic pilot result: semantic collision rate 25% (5 of 20 deliberately distinct-meaning pairs collapsed to the same synthetic SNF); 0/20 distinct-meaning pairs passed the non-collapse threshold.
a_rows_sample.statement: A deliberately-seeded synthetic pilot demonstrating that the measurement framework mechanically detects injected semantic collisions; explicitly caveated as testing the measurement mathematics only, not whether SNF actually preserves semantics (which requires a real semantic distance, not a synthetic structural one).

a_rows_sample.anchor: gold-relation / confusion-matrix design (v0.3): compare SNF's EQUIVALENT/DISTINCT/UNKNOWN judgment against an independently-labelled gold relation, producing three failure classes -- false divergence, semantic collision, and false certainty (UNKNOWN converted into confident interpretation).
a_rows_sample.statement: A proposed next experiment testing whether SNF agrees with independently-established ground truth about semantic relations, rather than only self-consistency of the SNF metric.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the execution did not expose the generated numeric tables, so I won't invent numerical results from the run.
a_rows_sample.statement: An explicit, self-imposed experimental-integrity discipline: when a simulation's actual output is unavailable, the author refuses to fabricate plausible-looking numbers and reports only the (sound) design of what was attempted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SNF(E,C) = normalization-function_S(semantic-candidate(E,C)) -- SNF defined at a higher functional-abstraction level rather than as one prescriptive pipeline (EDC(URDNA2015(Graph(Normalize(KG-NF(Logical(K))))))), so the representation stays replaceable while the measurement vector stays stable.
a_rows_sample.statement: The key architectural correction of the batch's external-research SNF-formula proposal: rejects over-prescriptive implementation-coupled formulas in favor of an encoding-agnostic functional definition consistent with the Semantic-Compiler port contract.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Fingerprint(SNF) = Hash(CanonicalEncoding(SNF)) is a representation-equality check, not a semantic-equality claim: 'SNF equality -> Knowledge identity' is forbidden.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demotes the originally-proposed 'Goedel(KIR) = product of primes' / hash-plus-Goedel-verification fingerprint from a claimed semantic-proof mechanism to a fast identity/lookup fingerprint only.

a_rows_sample.anchor: False Collapse Rate (FCR) = P(SNF(Ei)=SNF(Ej) | Ei not-equiv Ej) and False Divergence Rate (FDR) = P(SNF(Ei)!=SNF(Ej) | Ei equiv Ej), as the two first-class complementary safety metrics, with FCR the more critical (a constitutional-violation-class failure).
a_rows_sample.statement: Names and formalizes the pair of binary error rates directly answering the 'false convergence is more dangerous than false divergence' asymmetry raised in the sibling document (S0317), with explicit probabilistic definitions and acceptance thresholds (target FCR<0.01, FDR<0.05).

a_rows_sample.anchor: defer KG normal forms (1NF-KG/2NF-KG/3NF-KG) and SAIT/STMS (Semantic Algorithmic Information Theory / Semantic Turing Machine System) as research candidates, not core SNF definition, because database/knowledge-graph normalization solves a different problem than semantic invariance (a KG can be perfe
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects folding external-research components with insufficient evidence strength into the core SNF specification, keeping them as a labelled research-candidate track instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: reject a composite SNF score entirely: report a measurement vector (Convergence, Distinct-separation, Transformation-preservation, False-collapse, False-divergence, Abstention-precision/recall, Interpretation-entropy) rather than a single 'SNF=87%' number.
a_rows_sample.statement: The senior-mathematician turn's final full acceptance of the 7-metric measurement vector as the correct experimental specification, explicitly naming the rejected single-score approach as 'the exact problem we fixed'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel should not become a hidden semantic interpreter simply because the candidate DTO happens to contain semantic fields. ... semantic mechanisms remain replaceable providers, not identity authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Representation-independence lens critique: proposes a clean pipeline (external representation -> interpretation/normalization -> meaning candidate -> Expression<->Meaning boundary -> knowledge admission -> KnowledgeAggregate) and warns the Kernel must not become a hidden semantic interpreter merely because candidate DTOs contain semantic fields; connects this to the SNF finding that semantic mechanisms remain replaceable providers, never identity authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: agreement is not truth. ... The Kernel must never infer: mechanism confidence -> domain confidence; nor: mechanism identity -> Knowledge identity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Semantic lens (SNF-derived) reiterates 'agreement is not truth' and constrains the Kernel to never infer domain confidence from mechanism confidence, nor Knowledge identity from mechanism identity; states SNF itself is not part of the Kernel, but its lessons constrain the Kernel boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Is the Kernel a 'boundary' or a 'core'? ... What is the relationship between the Kernel and the Expression<->Meaning Port? ... What is the relationship between the Kernel and SNF mechanisms?
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten unresolved architectural questions close the brainstorming, including the Kernel's relationship to the Expression<->Meaning Port and to SNF mechanisms, whether epistemic state/evidence/justification/history are Kernel-owned or mechanism-owned concepts, and how to prevent the Kernel becoming a God Aggregate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The architectural insight: Expression != Meaning ... The question: Does KnowledgeOS preserve meaning when expression changes?
b_rows_sample.statement: Vani (speech/voice/expression/transmission/literary creation) lens: expression is not meaning. A single meaning may have many expressions (human speech -> written text -> digital representation -> AI generated summary).

b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Sanskrit-compiler 'Expression != Meaning' lens to 'Candidate interpretation != Knowledge', concluding the Kernel should not care how a candidate was produced and its input should be a structured CandidateKnowledge+EvidenceReferences+Justification+Context bundle, never raw expression -- preserving the existing Expression<->Meaning boundary and P5's finding that semantic mechanisms remain replaceable providers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: How does the Kernel preserve meaning distinctions without interpreting meaning? The Vani lens requires preserving artha while discarding sabda, but the Kernel has no access to meaning. This is the boundary paradox.

a_rows_sample.statement: The regenerated transcript confirms exec/sigma.py's A1-A6 results were actually executed and produced the claimed output, serving as the evidentiary record for the whole Sigma-status package.

a_rows_sample.anchor: NOTE: this is TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION once you posit exactly two independent predicates. The mathematical content is the CHOICE OF TWO, not the 4.
a_rows_sample.statement: A1: the bijection Sigma0=P({Support,Refute}) ~= {0,1}^2 is confirmed (|P(S)|=4, states Unknown/Supported/Refuted/Conflict) but flagged as true by construction once exactly two independent predicates are posited -- the real mathematical content is the choice of Support/Refute as the two predicates, not the resulting count of four.

a_rows_sample.anchor: collapse Unknown ~Refuted -> BREAKS: UNKNOWN != FALSE (42x) / Unknown != Absent (19x) ... => all 4 required. MINIMALITY CONFIRMED relative to these laws.
a_rows_sample.statement: A2: each of the six pairwise collapses of the four Sigma0 states breaks a corpus-stated non-collapse law (e.g. UNKNOWN != FALSE 42x, empty != ContradictoryEvidence per S271.21, UNRESOLVED != INVALID 9x, insufficiency is not refutation), so minimality is confirmed relative to those specific laws -- a genuine deletion argument.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sigma0(c1)=Supported Sigma0(c2)=Supported <- both Supported, while (c1,c2,contradicts) holds. Sigma0 is BLIND to it, as (dir,str) was. *** THE REDUCTION DID NOT FIX THE Sigma-blind-to-R DEFECT. ***
a_rows_sample.statement: A3: contradiction within a single assertion's evidence (Conflict={Support,Refute}) is derivable, but contradiction BETWEEN two assertions is a relation Sigma0 cannot express because Sigma0 is unary -- executed test constructs two assertions in an explicit contradicts-relation that both independently evaluate to Sigma0=Supported, proving the reduction to Sigma0 reproduces rather than fixes the earlier '(dir,str) blind to R' defect; a new finding not yet on any register.

a_rows_sample.anchor: union is a JOIN-semilattice op (monotone); retract is NON-monotone. They are compatible ONLY IF Sigma is DERIVED from the evidence set each time. ... OR-merge + retract TOGETHER FORCE Sigma to be DERIVED, not stored.
a_rows_sample.statement: A4: OR-merge(Supported,Refuted)=Conflict is a monotone join-semilattice operation, but Retract (withdrawing the refuting item to recover Supported) requires subtraction and is non-monotone; the two are jointly satisfiable only if Sigma is recomputed (derived) from the evidence set on each query rather than stored as a lattice element -- a proof, not a normative choice, that Sigma must be DERIVED. This corrects the file author's own prior classification of decision D-4 as normative and closes D-4 by derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sigma0 has 4 states; a lossless single vocabulary needs >= 4*|Gamma|. => Gamma OUTSIDE Sigma. CONFIRMED, and 272B's Sigma _|_ Lambda _|_ Gamma agrees.
a_rows_sample.statement: A5: ten constructed (Sigma,Gamma) cells are all independently meaningful, and the decisive corpus case S271.20 ('epistemically well-supported but administratively rejected') requires Gamma (governance) to sit outside Sigma (epistemic) since a lossless single vocabulary would need >= 4*|Gamma| values -- confirming Gamma's separation from Sigma, independently agreeing with 272B's Sigma-perp-Lambda-perp-Gamma orthogonality claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MISSINGNESS IS NOT REPRESENTABLE BY Sigma0. It needs D_t + a sufficiency predicate. 272B does not claim otherwise -- but nor does it close it.
a_rows_sample.statement: A6: Sigma0 maps three distinct epistemic situations ('never asked' has no Sigma value at all since no assertion exists; 'asked, no evidence' maps to Unknown; 'insufficient evidence' maps to Supported) onto only {undefined, Unknown, Supported} because Sigma0 has no sufficiency axis (Q was dropped from the ratified 6-tuple) -- missingness is not representable by Sigma0 and requires D_t plus a sufficiency predicate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Σ has a minimal four-valued semantic space" ≠ "the state representation is determined." The first is proven. The second is false: Σ was one of six blockers, and closing it leaves five — plus the one A3 just added.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharp distinction: proving Sigma has a minimal four-valued semantic space is NOT the same as the full state representation being determined -- Sigma was only one of six blockers, closing it leaves five plus a newly discovered sixth (Sigma0-perp-R).

a_rows_sample.anchor: P's type | §262.15 "remains an open sub-test" | admissibility law | 42.9 vs 42.41, neither matches the ratified 6-tuple | authority boundary | D-2 | missingness carrier | §276.15, live | 𝒪_core ratification | 01 — not ratified | Σ₀ ⊥ ℛ | A3 — new
a_rows_sample.statement: Six items remain open even after closing Sigma: the type of P (an open sub-test at §262.15), the admissibility law (two candidate laws at 42.9/42.41 neither matching the ratified 6-tuple), the authority boundary (decision D-2), the missingness carrier (live at §276.15), O_core's ratification status (not ratified), and the newly found Sigma0-perp-relation defect (A3).

a_rows_sample.anchor: M4–M6 are exactly Σ₀ = P({Support, Refute}) minus (0,0). M1–M3 are the three ways (0,0) arises. So the seven states are not a new Σ — they are Σ₀ with its zero element resolved into three, plus a structural condition. ... the repair belongs at (0,0), not across Σ.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mathematician's lens: Step 281's seven mandatory states are not a genuinely new Sigma space but Sigma0=P({Support,Refute}) with its zero element (0,0) resolved into three refinements (M1-M3) plus a structural condition (M7) sitting outside Sigma entirely (M4-M6 = the three non-zero elements) -- the repair belongs specifically at the (0,0) collapse point, not spread across all of Sigma; candidate A is judged the minimal repair, B the more expressive one, pending which the corpus's own minimality criterion should decide.

a_rows_sample.anchor: > **My written `Σ` said `dir ∈ {Refuting, Neutral, Supporting}` — three — and treated `Conflicted` as a\n> separate derived predicate. My implementation already returned four. 272B is right:** direction is the\n> **powerset of `{Support, Refute}`**, not a trichotomy. **`Conflict` is `D=(1,1)`, not a side channel.**
a_rows_sample.statement: The author corrects their own prior documentation of Sigma's direction component: written documentation stated dir is a trichotomy {Refuting, Neutral, Supporting} with Conflicted treated as a separate derived predicate, but an executed comparison shows the author's own Sigma() code already returns four distinct direction values (Neutral/Supporting/Refuting/Contested, mapping to 272B's Unknown/Supported/Refuted/Conflict); the reconciled canonical form adopts 272B's account that direction D is the powerset of {Support,Refute} (isomorphic to {0,1}^2), with Conflict being the state D=(1,1) rather than a separate side-channel axis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: - **DERIVED, never stored — proven, not chosen** (`consolidation/03` §A4): OR-merge + Retract are\n  jointly satisfiable only if Σ is derived (retract needs subtraction; a stored join cannot undo).\n  "D-4 is hereby closed by derivation." Caveat: "DERIVED **relative to 272B's own commitments**."
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and reconciles D-4's closure: Sigma is proven to be derived (not stored) rather than this being a free normative choice, because OR-merge and Retract are only jointly satisfiable if Sigma is computed from the evidence set each time (a stored join-semilattice element cannot be 'undone' by retract, which requires subtraction); the closure is explicitly caveated as being derived relative to 272B's own prior commitments, not an absolute proof independent of all other framing choices.

a_rows_sample.statement: A same-date (2026-08-30) source explicitly refutes its own earlier four-state Sigma claim ('That is one too many... Sigma = {Unknown, Supported, Refuted} — three states, minimal') against a different same-date source's 'MINIMALITY CONFIRMED, |Sigma_0|>=4'; the reconciliation document asserting 'no contradictions' does not include the refuting document in its table, leaving the Sigma_min>=4 result with an unreconciled same-date refutation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 277 -- Canonical Transformation Inventory and O_core Closure ... we cannot responsibly declare K minimal until we know what operations the state must support.
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 redirects the next step away from Part 1's recommendation (Policy/Authority interface formalization) to 'Step 277 -- Canonical Transformation Inventory and O_core Closure', on the ground that K-minimality cannot responsibly be declared before the complete transformation family T is established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: State Transformation != Query != Governance Predicate != Representation Operation. This distinction is fundamental. ... Assert can change knowledge state. Whereas Query observes knowledge state. And Authorize determines whether an action is permitted.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the fundamental distinction driving Step 277's whole reduction: state transformation, query/observation, governance predicate and representation operation are four different mathematical roles that cannot be forced into one homogeneous operation algebra.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O = O_T ∪ O_E ∪ O_Q ∪ O_G ∪ O_R ... O_semantic != O_operational ... O_semantic != O_implementation
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the corrected layered operation universe O = O_T (state transformations) ∪ O_E (evidence) ∪ O_Q (query/observation) ∪ O_G (governance) ∪ O_R (representation), replacing the previous flat O_core=O_S∪O_E∪O_H∪O_G∪O_Q∪O_X union, and states O_semantic != O_operational != O_implementation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T_K = {t | t: K x I -> K'} ... A transformation may be partial: t: K x I ⇀ K ... Pre_t -> t -> K' -> Post_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the canonical partial state-transition schema t:K x I_t ⇀ K with explicit Pre_t/Post_t, arguing partiality is necessary because operations like Retract(K,p) with p not-in K or Supersede requiring evidence/temporal/authorization conditions cannot be pretended total.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assert, Retract, Supersede, Merge, Split ... We now test whether all five are genuinely primitive. ... Model A -- destructive removal ... Model B -- epistemic transition ... Because KnowledgeOS explicitly values history, provenance and replay, Model B is generally more compatible
b_rows_sample.statement: Tests each of the five historically-supported state operations for primitivity: Assert is REQUIRED; Retract's semantics remain an open choice between destructive removal (Model A) and a history-preserving epistemic-status transition (Model B), with Model B favoured as more compatible with KnowledgeOS's stated values; Supersede is REQUIRED and history-preserving by construction; Merge and Split are both flagged as only CANDIDATE primitives (possibly decomposable into Assert + conflict-resolution + linking, or into assertion-partitioning + relation-removal + lineage-preservation respectively), minimality unresolved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Replay(K0,H) = fold(T,K0,H) ... If demonstrated, Replay need not be included in the primitive operation kernel. ... Trace, Query, Explain ... do not necessarily alter K. Therefore ... not in T_K.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues Replay is potentially a derived fold over the transformation sequence (Replay(K0,H)=fold(T,K0,H)) rather than a primitive operation, and that Trace/Query/Explain are observational (do not alter K) and so belong to the query layer O_Q, not the state-transition kernel T_K -- significantly shrinking the candidate primitive set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T_candidate = {Assert, Retract, Supersede, Merge, Split, LinkEvidence} ... smaller != proven minimal. ... o is primitive iff exists r in R_mandatory : r not-in Closure(T_{-o})
b_rows_sample.statement: States the resulting candidate primitive kernel T_candidate={Assert,Retract,Supersede,Merge,Split,LinkEvidence} (reduced from ~20 heterogeneous operations), formalizes the operation-minimality criterion (o is primitive iff some mandatory distinction is lost by T minus {o}), and explicitly labels T_candidate as NOT YET PROVEN minimal -- the deletion/composability experiments remain future work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy does NOT disappear. ... we have separated semantic transition from authorization of transition. ... Policy gates transformations without necessarily becoming part of the knowledge-state representation itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies that removing Authorize/Approve/Reject/ChangePolicy from the state-transition kernel does not solve Policy; it separates semantic transition from authorization-of-transition, with Policy acting as an external gate (Authorize(...) -> Decision -> transformation) rather than a stored component of K -- explicitly said to resolve part of the earlier circularity concern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Test T1 -- Assert elimination ... Test T4 -- Merge elimination ... Test T7 -- Replay derivation ... Test T8 -- Policy independence ... Test T9 -- Representation independence
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies nine mandatory falsification tests (T1-T9) for the next step: elimination tests for Assert/Retract/Supersede/Merge/Split/LinkEvidence (can each be expressed without the named primitive?), a derivation test for Replay-as-fold, a Policy-independence test (can t(K,i) be defined independently of Authorize?), and a representation-independence test (can two different serializations of the same semantic K be observationally equivalent?).

b_rows_sample.statement: Completes the mandate's required gap-status table across seven candidate gaps (O_core, Authority, Determination, K, Sigma, Transformation, K-sufficiency), finding six retired/derived/substantially-derived and only K-sufficiency left 'unresolved with no owner' — declared OPEN by Step 277 which explicitly commissioned a next step to test it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### PA-1 (`EXECUTED`, CRITICAL) — the commissioned K-sufficiency step was silently replaced ... Step 277 ends: "Next: STEP 278 — K-SUFFICIENCY AND TRANSFORMATION MINIMALITY TEST" The actual Step 278 is "POLICY–AUTHORITY INTEGRATION..." and it mentions K-sufficiency zero times.
b_rows_sample.statement: PA-1 (EXECUTED, CRITICAL): Step 277 explicitly commissions 'STEP 278 — K-SUFFICIENCY AND TRANSFORMATION MINIMALITY TEST' as its next step, but the actual Step 278 that was written is 'POLICY-AUTHORITY INTEGRATION, TEMPORAL SEMANTICS, AND GOVERNANCE CLOSURE', mentioning K-sufficiency zero times; its header claims to supersede an earlier draft of itself, not the commissioned step, and no artifact records the substitution. Identified as the fourth instance of the same corpus-wide 'commissioned-but-not-performed' failure mode (alongside the repaired measure-theory model, Regime, and Determination).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### PA-2 (`EXECUTED`, HIGH) — the estate adopted this session's numbers and dropped its method ... | congruence-vacuity (SO-2) | **0** | **NOT ADOPTED** |
b_rows_sample.statement: PA-2 (EXECUTED, HIGH): canonical-construction's BLOCKED-MANIFEST cites second-order's so_exp06_closure.py and reproduces its five closure percentages verbatim (so the package was read), yet a grep of Steps 272-278 shows the underlying methodological findings were NOT adopted: congruence-vacuity (0 occurrences), AuthorityAct typing (0), Context typing (0), R restored to 8 fields (0); invariant-expressibility mentioned only once. Step 277 declares K-sufficiency OPEN while its defining criterion (congruence plus invariant-expressibility) sits unadopted nearby — 'the estate took the measurements and left the instrument.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: 14-element lower bound forced by the corpus's own non-collapse laws; upper bound 18. Open only: are `Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce` mandatory? ... note independently: Qualify, Determine and Derive are forced by laws the corpus repeats 20, 19 and 18 times, yet appear in neither §256.2 nor §259.7.
b_rows_sample.statement: D-1 narrowed to whether four operations (Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce) are mandatory; K's ontology is invariant across all 16 possible resolutions, but the congruence proof and Minimality(K|T) are not (Step 277: 'Minimality: OPEN'). Independently notes that Qualify, Determine, and Derive are forced by corpus laws repeated 20/19/18 times respectively yet are absent from the two canonical operation-registry sections (§256.2, §259.7) — a gap regardless of which D-1 option is chosen.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ## The one thing no decision covers ... K-sufficiency. Step 277 declares it OPEN and commissioned Step 278 to test it; Step 278 did Policy–Authority instead and mentions it zero times (PA-1). ... This needs no decision. It needs the commissioned step to actually be performed, with the criterion `Sufficient(K, 𝒪, ℐ)` rather than congruence alone.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes K-sufficiency from the six named decisions: unlike D-0 through D-5, K-sufficiency is not blocked by a normative choice but by a commissioned step (Step 278's original mandate) never having been performed. Recommends actually performing the K-sufficiency test using the Sufficient(K,O,I) criterion (congruence plus invariant-expressibility) rather than congruence alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ⚠️ **G-16 moved to NARROWED — see [`05-ADDENDUM-STEP-272A.md`](./05-ADDENDUM-STEP-272A.md) §3.** Step 272A retracts Step 277's closure claim. **FULFILLED 9 → 8 · NARROWED 8 → 9.** Theoretical holes remain **11**.
b_rows_sample.statement: A retroactive correction note records that Step 272A (landing after this document's initial version) retracts Step 277's prior 'Classification: CLOSED' claim for O_core's transition-signature question (G-16), moving it from FULFILLED to NARROWED and revising the overall counts (FULFILLED 9->8, NARROWED 8->9, theoretical holes remaining at 11).

b_rows_sample.anchor: > ## **AUTHORITATIVE STATUS: `𝒪_core` is CLOSED as a TAXONOMY and OPEN as a KERNEL.**\n> **Freezing it now would freeze an explicitly unproven minimality claim.** Step 277 says so in its own\n> boxed conclusions. **P0 "freeze canonical `𝒪_core`" must become "verify then freeze."**
b_rows_sample.statement: O_core (the operation universe) is closed as a taxonomic decomposition (Step 272A's 19-operation, 5-family O_sem) but open as a kernel/minimal primitive set, because Step 277's own conclusion explicitly states its candidate primitive transformation set T_candidate={Assert,Retract,Supersede,Merge,Split,LinkEvidence} is 'not yet proven minimal'; therefore a planned action item to freeze the canonical O_core must instead become 'verify then freeze.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **`Split`** | in `𝒯_candidate`, "minimality unresolved" | **executed: LOSSY on `ℛ`** — `Split;Merge` does not recover relations | **`Split` cannot be a state primitive without a declared `ℛ` policy.** Unreconciled. |\n| **`LinkEvidence`** | in `𝒯_candidate` | **absent** — `e` is a field of the assertion, fixed at creation | **`LinkEvidence` would MUTATE an assertion**, contradicting `ReplayAssertion`'s immutability invariant. Unreconciled. |
b_rows_sample.statement: Two unreconciled conflicts are found between Step 277's T_candidate operation set and this stream's own executed algebra: (1) executing Split followed by Merge does not recover the original relation set R (Split is lossy on R), so Split cannot be a state primitive without an explicitly declared R-handling policy; (2) LinkEvidence, if implemented as described, would mutate an existing assertion's evidence field, but in this stream's model evidence e is a field of the assertion fixed at creation time (immutable), contradicting the ReplayAssertion immutability invariant; also notes 'relate' (adding an R edge of any type) exists in this stream's algebra but is not listed separately in T_candidate, which only covers Supersede for one relation type.

group_evidence.why_grouped: an UNKNOWN-OBJECT-CANDIDATE row (batch B0047, source S1953) named these as alternative candidates for one piece of evidence. why_uncertain: This entry restates, for book-writing-control purposes, the same O_core-not-frozen and Sigma-not-yet-canonical findings already registered under the two candidate labels; flagged rather than merged into either single label because it applies the finding jointly to four different constructs (O_core, Sigma, Q_t, Authority) as one governance-control table.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Shipments above 50,000 require managerial approval even when all release conditions are satisfied. ... Determination ⇏ Authorization. ... Release(S) only if ReleasePermitted(S) and ManagerApproval(S). ... Determination != Decision != Authorization.
a_rows_sample.statement: 21A.18-21A.19: introduces an additional organizational policy (shipments over EUR50,000 require managerial approval regardless of release-condition satisfaction) -- with ShipmentValue(S)=EUR75,000, the release determination stands but ManagerApprovalRequired(S) also holds, so Determination⇏Authorization; the decision layer has alternatives {Release,Hold} with decision rule Release(S) only if ReleasePermitted(S)∧ManagerApproval(S); since ManagerApproval(S) is currently absent, Delta_Decision={ManagerApproval(S)}, so the correct system answer is 'the shipment satisfies the operational release criteria, but the decision contract still requires managerial authorization' rather than a bare 'release it' -- exemplifying Determination≠Decision≠Authorization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: It is tempting to conclude immediately: 'All four records exist, therefore release is permitted.' That is premature. ... Evidence ⇏ Determination.
b_rows_sample.statement: 21A.9: warns against the premature conclusion that four existing records alone permit release -- KnowledgeOS must still verify source authority, applicability to S, temporal validity, current rule version, absence of exceptions, and contract satisfaction, giving Evidence⇏Determination even once all four evidence objects exist.
